0.content:
Aberrant Chimeric Monster (also: Aberrant Chimeric Monsters, Aberrant Chimeras, chimeric beasts, man-made monsters of Snezhnaya, Koshchei's chimeras): Aberrant Chimeric Monsters are the hybrid beasts of Snezhnaya, products of the bio-alchemy that flourished before it was forbidden. In the reign of the Belyi Tsar alchemists, above all Koshchei, freely combined living things into new animals. Most were consumed in the war against the Onslaught of Dark Beasts, and the handful that survive are rare, dangerous exceptions. They include armoured beasts, burrowing predators, winged elephants, horned bears, the two-headed Chimeric Winged Lion and the Immortal Construct.

They are not fae and not natural wildlife: each was designed, or assembled, for a purpose, and many have lost the purpose they were built for. Most have little awareness and follow a leader or simply hunt. A few are tied to named figures: Zver, the intelligent chimera who served the Belyi Tsar, and Zhara, an Immortal Construct.

Nature: Man-made monsters from Snezhnayan bio-alchemy, combining the traits of different animals. In-game text describes them as pieces of life, scattered like puzzle parts, put together as the researchers pleased.

Archive and Loading Screen text say alchemy was practised freely across Snezhnaya during the Belyi Tsar's reign, before it was forbidden. Koshchei is named as the creator of the group. The wiki says he first combined animals, was praised for it, and later experimented on fae. Monsters built around one function rarely survive in the wild once their place or purpose is gone, and the Armored Beast is noted as an exception. Most of the creations broke the laws of the world and died; the Horned Bear is a stranger case, assembled spontaneously from life segments rather than to a design, and able to wield elemental power.

Society: They have no society. Most possess little real awareness and simply obey a leader or follow instinct. Before the Cataclysm the chimeras fought the Abyss under Zver's command and the Tsar's banner, according to the Eye of Graeae; Chimeric Winged Elephants also worked with the Vila on intelligence and communications, carrying the Tsar's orders as his army advanced.

Abilities and limits: Chimeric Armored Beast: a four-legged beast with a carapace and a charging horn, built as a shock force; it fires crystals of Geo energy. Chimeric Burrowbeast: tunnels through earth, rock, ice and snow and sees in the dark, ambushing prey at night (Electro). Chimeric Winged Elephant: a short-legged flying elephant made to cross terrain freely and reach high fruit. Chimeric Horned Bear: a Pyro bear of spontaneous construction. Chimeric Winged Lion: a two-headed, winged boss with Anemo and Electro power, said to be unmatched among chimeras. Immortal Construct: a mindless, winged, red-leafed boss with Pyro power.

Individuals: Zver: a two-headed chimera that gained intelligence. It was a loyal servant of the Belyi Tsar, dragged his body back from the battlefield at Khaenri'ah, and guards his resting place at the Pale Crown Palace; it died in 7.0 after the Traveler defeated it. Zhara: an Immortal Construct with a humanoid upper body and long fair hair, animated by Koshchei's fragment of the Eye of Graeae, who protected Okurov in Flamefeather Valley for centuries.

Relations: Koshchei created them and treated life as a puzzle to be reassembled; he abandoned results he judged failures. The Belyi Tsar took Zver in and named it. Aksinya, who once worked with Koshchei at Hvergelmir, is spoken of with contempt by Zver. The Vila are the closest fae ally in the war record.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 only scattered survivors remain across Snezhnaya, wild and hostile. Zver is dead.

Zhara was unable to revive after Aksinya adjusted her inert body, per the wiki's summary of Chorus of Solace. The Immortal Constructs that remain in Flamefeather Valley are the mindless leftovers of Koshchei's experiments. No new chimeras are shown being made.

1.comment: Aberrant Chimeric Monster: Koshchei and the origin of the chimeras
1.content: Koshchei was a Snezhnayan bio-alchemist who saw life as a puzzle to be taken apart and reassembled. He built the first Aberrant Chimeras by combining animals and was praised; wanting more, he began experimenting on fae. Rather than executing him the Belyi Tsar recruited him to Hvergelmir. Later the Eye of Graeae persuaded him, Pavlina and Alvis to betray Aksinya; he took a third of the Graeae's power to Flamefeather Valley and lived in Okurov as "Doctor Moreau", pursuing eternal life through the Perfect Tree. The wiki's Koshchei page is the main source for this life and is of medium confidence.

2.content: Zver ("the Beast" in Russian) is the two-headed chimera that stood guard over the Belyi Tsar's body in the Pale Crown Palace. According to the Eye of Graeae it was one of Koshchei's prototypes, abandoned as half-formed, then named and valued by the Tsar. It followed the Tsar to every battlefield and brought back his body from Khaenri'ah. Fighting the Traveler it taunted the Eye of Graeae about its lost memory, its body split in three and Aksinya's banishment to the Shadow Realm, then died, saying it had watched over the body for five centuries and kept its vow. A flashback has the Tsar forgiving Zver for not following its creator's orders, after Zver complains of its maker's contempt; Zver says its loyalty is its own choice.

3.comment: Aberrant Chimeric Monster: Chimeric Winged Lion
3.content: A winged, two-headed beast fought as a boss in the Volkodlak Tundra. Its Archive entry calls it a byproduct of a grand ambition, one of the Prototypes that failed to become the intended perfect creation and was remade as a two-headed monster. It commands Anemo and Electro power, and the text suggests anomalous materials fused into its shell lend it unusual strength. The Adventurer Handbook says the entity is a byproduct engineered on the way to a certain great wish.

key: Remnant Body of the Eternal Flamefeather
4.content: A winged, crimson-leaved construct that roams Flamefeather Valley and the Everfrozen Earth, now a mindless, soulless remnant. The Archive says it was abandoned before the grand ritual could be completed; its purpose as a biological vessel is lost. Zhara belongs to the same kind, animated by the Eye of Graeae's fragment.

5.comment: Aberrant Chimeric Monster: Chimeric beasts of the frozen lands
5.content: Four common chimeras survive in Snezhnaya. The Armored Beast hunts in packs and fires crystalline energy. The Burrowbeast ambushes from shadow and, by one Vestnik report, may grow very large. The Winged Elephant once relayed orders for the Belyi Tsar's army with the Vila. The Horned Bear is the odd one out, formed from life segments without a plan and able to use elemental power freely.

6.content:
Abyss Herald (also: Abyss Heralds, Wicked Torrents, Frost Fall, Presager of the Abyss, Fortune Lector): Abyss Heralds are elite melee fighters of the Abyss Order who command intense Abyssal power through blades. They come in two kinds: Wicked Torrents (Hydro) and Frost Fall (Cryo). The Archive calls them silent vanguards and envoys of the Abyss, counterparts to the singing, ranged Abyss Lectors. Most are anonymous. Klingsor, a one-time Sumeru Skeptic who embraced the Abyss, is the best-known named Herald.

Wicked Torrents debuted in 1.4, with the Presager of the Abyss in Archon Quest Chapter I Act IV; Frost Fall followed in 3.5. Unlike mages, Heralds are individual threats and several have personal roles in the story.

Nature: A Herald is a person-sized, humanoid creature of the Abyss, armed with a sword of water or ice. Archive text for Wicked Torrents calls the type silent figures at the Abyss's vanguard whose tidal blades "engulf everything in an instant"; the Frost Fall entry says that just as saints spread the gospel, there are envoys to correct twisted strains and remove dissonance, and that their dark frost is said to freeze even the soul.

Klingsor shows how a Herald can come to be: a human Skeptic who found a Khaenri'ahn ruin and its gospel, "embraced the defilement's blessings" and was transformed. His current form is a Hydro Wicked Torrents Herald. Whether every Herald was once a person is not stated.

Abilities and limits: Fast, aggressive melee attackers, with some ranged attacks. In the Hydro form the blades throw torrents of water; in the Cryo form, bursts of ice. At low health a Herald raises a tough elemental shield and falls the moment that shield breaks.

Tutorial text: Wicked Torrents commands "warped torrents", and some attacks lengthen the cooldowns of skills already on cooldown. Frost Fall commands ice and frost, and some attacks drain stamina. Fans note that some Wicked Torrents attack names (Surging Tide, The Wicked Torrents) share wording with Tartaglia's talents; this is wiki trivia, not an in-world link.

Society: Heralds are listed among the Abyss Order's sentient Abyss creatures, alongside Lectors, Iniquitous Baptists and mages. The Order's hierarchy is officially unknown: the Traveler's Sibling leads, an "inner circle" exists, and Haden, an Iniquitous Baptist, led its force in Natlan, but how Heralds rank is not stated.

Relations: Heralds serve the Abyss Order, and so, indirectly, its leader, the Traveler's Sibling. Their natural enemies are the Traveler, Dainsleif, and the guardians of the lands they attack.

A Frost Fall Herald stands with the sibling in the ambush where the sibling tampers with the Ley Lines and wounds Dainsleif (the Bedtime Story era, 4.7). Klingsor works with Nasejuna, then head of the Order of Skeptics, in Khvarena of Good and Evil.

Individuals: The Presager of the Abyss is an unnamed Hydro Herald who works directly under the Traveler's Sibling and clashes with the Traveler four times in Archon Quests: first in the Call of the Abyss domain, then at Wolvendom (assisted by Hilichurl Shooters), again in the Call of the Abyss domain (assisted by Abyss Mages), and finally in the Chasm's underground mines, where he is killed. He flees after the first three fights. Klingsor is described in his own entry. The Fortune Lector, a Cryo Herald, guards the last chamber of the Caribert quest, where it tests the Traveler before the Sinner's crystal.

Scene use: This project's suggestion (not canon): treat a Herald as a silent, disciplined opponent who does not parley, in contrast to a Lector or a mage. Heralds do bark short battle cries (Frost Fall: "Foolish mortals!"), but full conversation is not shown. If a scene needs a Herald who talks, remember that Klingsor is a Herald with a human history and a mission, not a typical one.

7.content: Klingsor was once a ranger of the Order of Skeptics in the Girdle of the Sands, a descendant of the Khaenri'ahn Hadura. Resenting the shame attached to Khaenri'ahns, he came to suspect the Skeptics hid the truth. Sent to supervise visiting Akademiya scholars in the ruins, he found material that confirmed his doubts and embraced the Abyss, becoming a Herald. His first attack on the Vourukasha Oasis was repelled by the Pari and the Skeptics. In the present he persuades Nasejuna to help seize the Great Songs of Khvarena in order to break the seal at Tunigi Hollow; the Traveler stops them. He is covered further in his own entry.

8.comment: Abyss Herald: Presager of the Abyss
8.content: An unnamed Hydro Wicked Torrents Herald who works directly under the Traveler's Sibling. The wiki counts four encounters across Archon Quests: the Call of the Abyss domain, Wolvendom (with Hilichurl Shooters), the Call of the Abyss domain again (with Abyss Mages) and finally the Chasm's underground mines during Memories of Inteyvat, where the Traveler and Dainsleif defeat him. He appears again in Silent Seeker of Knowledge only as a dream.

9.content:
Abyss Lector (also: Abyss Lectors, Fathomless Flames, Violet Lightning, Abyss Chanter): Abyss Lectors are the ranged elites of the Abyss Order, spellcasters who chant over books and verses and fight with catalysts. They are the counterpart of the melee Abyss Heralds. There are two kinds: Violet Lightning (Electro, debuted 1.5) and Fathomless Flames (Pyro, added 2.4). The best-known individual is Enjou, a Pyro Lector who posed as a human clerk in Enkanomiya and kept turning up afterwards, as Sanka and under other names, in Natlan.

Their Archive entries say that the surface people slightly misread their name: "Lector" can also mean an exegete, someone who interprets scripture. Several Lectors are written as scholars of the Abyss rather than as soldiers.

Nature: Archive text calls the Fathomless Flames Lector a wielder of abyssal fire who pursues the meaning behind texts and scriptures, and says that reading "the word of grace" grants them great power. Violet Lightning Lectors are called the evangelists and scholars of the Abyss, who sing the praises of darkness and strike the hearts of unbelievers with violent violet lightning.

A Lector is a sentient Abyss creature, not a beast. Some are capable of subtle behaviour. Enjou disguised himself as a human clerk for the entirety of a long trial and was friendly to the Traveler. Comonqui, a Lector in Natlan, was a "spectator" who came to watch the destructive power of the Abyss.

Abilities and limits: Ranged elemental attacks with a catalyst, shielding themselves when wounded.

Tutorial text: the Fathomless Flames Lector sings of the warmth of the dark flame, and some attacks leave a brand of abyssal flame on a character that explodes after a short time and hurts the whole party. It defends itself with a shield of abyssal fire, which becomes easier to wear down if its Darkfire Furnace is destroyed. The Violet Lightning Lector calls thunder in praise of the darkness and can disrupt elemental power: some attacks drain Elemental Energy from characters they hit.

Society: Lectors work in the Abyss Order's service, usually at a distance from the front line. Enjou is, in his words, a "lowly clerk" who studies ancient lore; he is aware of the Order's plans but not part of the inner circle, and he avoids fights when he can.

Relations: Lectors serve the Abyss Order and its leader, the Traveler's Sibling. They are opposed by the Traveler, Dainsleif, and the people whose lands they invade.

Enjou has the most personal relationships: he is amicable toward the Traveler despite trying to kill them once to check whether they hold Before Sun and Moon, he negotiates with the vishaps, and in Natlan makes a deal with Kinich and Ajaw. Before leaving the Traveler, he remarks that Paimon could betray them.

Individuals: Enjou (Fathomless Flames) is the principal named Lector; see his entry. Egill ("One Who Calls The Living", Pyro) and Agnarr ("One Who Mourns the Dead", Electro) are twin bosses in the Perils in the Dark quest, after the dark fog is dispersed. Comonqui ("a burning flame" in Nahuatl, Pyro) is a boss in the Echoes of Life Archon Quest, defeated by Kachina and Mualani. The unnamed "Baptist of the Ruined Kingdom" (Electro) manages the failed purge ritual and is defeated by Halfdan, Dainsleif and the Traveler.

Scene use: This project's suggestion (not canon): a Lector suits a scene about forbidden texts, ritual and temptation. Enjou is the exception that shows the range: soft-spoken, evasive and curious rather than cruel.

10.content: Enjou is the Pyro Abyss Lector the Traveler meets in Enkanomiya as a helpful human translator and clerk. After the Traveler wins the trial, he reveals himself, fights them, and explains that he sought Before Sun and Moon to prove that gods and Celestia came from beyond Teyvat. He then spares them, having grown fond of them. In Three Realms Gateway Offering (2.5, limited-time event) he restores the Towers of the Void and strikes a deal with vishaps. In Natlan he appears as Sanka, Kokuchuu and Hayne, bargaining with Kinich and Ajaw for time to do "historical research" and finally setting out deeper toward the burning Mare Jivari in search of his homeland; the wiki ties the Lavawalker title to him. He is described more fully in his own entry.

11.content:
Abyss Mage (also: Abyss Mages, Pyro Abyss Mage, Hydro Abyss Mage, Cryo Abyss Mage, Electro Abyss Mage, Pyrochanter, Hydrochanter, Cryochanter): Abyss Mages are the Abyss Order's everyday spellcasters: hooded, masked creatures who command one of four elements (Pyro, Hydro, Cryo, Electro) and shield themselves behind a barrier of that element. Adventurers say they sit at the lowest rung of the Order's ranks. They are usually found near hilichurls, whom they can talk to and manipulate, or with other mages. They are far weaker than Abyss Heralds and Lectors, but still dangerous.

They first appear in 1.0 and are among the first agents of the Abyss the Traveler meets, in Mondstadt, where a Cryo Abyss Mage ambushes the Traveler and a Hydro Abyss Mage is later tracked to the winery.

Nature: Archive text calls them "Abyss creatures" that can command the elements to a limited extent. The Adventurer Handbook says that, for unknown reasons, they can speak with hilichurls and so bend their minds easily, and that the language they chant is long forgotten and the source of their magic.

Each mage is bound to one element. Pyro, Cryo and Hydro mages date from 1.0; the Electro mage was added in 2.0. In appearance the four are alike (robed, masked, floating casters), except that the Hydro mage wears a white mask and has no element emblem on its clothing, while the others wear a black mask and their emblem.

Abilities and limits: Mages fire elemental bolts and cast area spells from range. Their key defence is an elemental shield, and breaking it leaves the mage stunned and exposed.

Mages are often seen performing a ritual or patrolling a set area. A mage in the middle of a ritual has no shield but raises one quickly if it survives the first blow; patrolling mages always have theirs up. When the shield is destroyed the mage is stunned for a long time and takes full damage; if it is not finished off, it tries to regenerate the shield.

Society: Mages are said to be the lowest-ranking Abyss creatures, wandering the lands to scheme small acts of destruction, a rumour reported by adventurers in the Hydro mage's entry. Many are seen in the open, unlike the more elusive Heralds and Lectors.

Relations: Mages serve the Abyss Order and, through it, the Order's leader, the Traveler's Sibling. They command hilichurls; Dainsleif says many hilichurls are cursed Khaenri'ahns whom the Abyss Order conscripts.

The Order's more dangerous sentient creatures include Abyss Heralds and Lectors. Diluc and Jean treat Abyss Mages as a lead to the Order in the Prologue (Abyss Mage quest): Diluc, with his sources, traces one to the Dawn Winery, and Venti notes that a certain energy dispersed from the fallen mage's body, which he reads as having been used to cut his connection to Dvalin.

Individuals: Named mages are minor. Cryochanter Abyss Mage Emery is the main antagonist of the Troublesome Work world quest and refuses to return a book before Lisa electrocutes him. Hydrochanter Abyss Mage Landrich is lit on fire by Diluc when interrogated about a threatening note to the Knights (Darknight Hero's Alibi). "Mr. Fluffball", a Pyro mage nicknamed by Klee, takes one of her bombs in True Treasure and accidentally kills itself with it.

Scene use: This project's suggestion for scenes (not canon): use a mage as an early or low-stakes Abyss threat near a hilichurl camp, or as a ritual interrupter. Keep them small and bound to one element; for real menace, use Heralds and Lectors.

12.comment: Abyss Mage: Abyss Mages in the Prologue
12.content: At the story's opening, an unnamed Cryo Abyss Mage was behind an ambush in The Outlander Who Caught the Wind, a Hydro mage behind the ambush was defeated by Diluc, and the Cryo mage controlling Dvalin reported to the Traveler's Sibling. A Hydro Abyss Mage was tracked to the Dawn Winery in the quest "Abyss Mage" by Diluc and Jean; Venti noted that a certain energy dispersed from its body after defeat, which seemed to have been cutting off his connection to Dvalin.

13.comment: Abyss Mage: Emery, Landrich and Mr. Fluffball
13.content: Three named Abyss Mages from side quests: Emery (Cryo, Troublesome Work; refused to return a book and was electrocuted by Lisa), Landrich (Hydro, Darknight Hero's Alibi; interrogated and set on fire by Diluc) and "Mr. Fluffball" (Pyro, True Treasure; Klee's nickname, killed itself with a stolen bomb). All are played largely for humour.

14.content:
Adeptus (also: Adepti, Mighty and Illuminated Adepti, Mighty and Illuminated Adeptus, adeptal beings): The adepti (singular adeptus) are Liyue's immortal guardians. Most are illuminated beasts: ancient cranes, deer, qilin and similar creatures that speak, live for millennia and wield elemental power. A few gods are also counted among them. Most signed a contract with Rex Lapis (Morax), the "Prime of Adepti", to protect Liyue from demons and evil gods, and they fought beside him in the Archon War. Afterwards most withdrew to the mountains of Jueyun Karst. Well-known adepti include Cloud Retainer, Moon Carver, Mountain Shaper, Madame Ping, Xiao and the half-qilin Ganyu.

Their full title is "the Mighty and Illuminated Adepti." Mortals revere them almost as gods and leave offerings at the edge of Jueyun Karst, but rarely go further. Now that Liyue is under human rule, several adepti live quietly among humans in Liyue Harbor.

Nature: Most adepti show mortals their true beast forms. Full-blooded adepti can also take human form, and some prefer it, like Madame Ping and Xiao. They are long-lived but can die. Children of an adeptus and a human, such as Ganyu and Yanfei, can be called adepti. Humans are not adepti, even when they master adeptal arts, as Shenhe has.

Society: The adepti are a loose fellowship under Rex Lapis, not a government. Most live apart in mountain abodes and meet only in a crisis. Many go by sacred names such as Cloud Retainer, Moon Carver, Mountain Shaper and Streetward Rambler.

Abilities and limits: Adepti command elemental energy without needing a Vision. Each carries a personal "adeptal energy" that is dangerous to humans over long exposure. They create private pocket realms called abodes and practise adeptal arts. They are formidable fighters, and the yakshas were their elite demon-slayers.

Relations: Adepti are bound to Rex Lapis by contract, and mortals worship them from a distance. Their relationship with the Liyue Qixing is guarded. When Rex Lapis appeared to die in Chapter I (1.0), they suspected the Qixing, until the threat of Osial forced the two sides into an alliance.

History: The adepti fought for Morax and Guizhong in the Archon War. After the Guili Assembly fell, Morax led his people south of Mt. Tianheng to found Liyue Harbor, and the adepti contracted with him to protect it. When the war ended about two thousand years ago, most withdrew to Jueyun Karst.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the adepti still guard Liyue, mostly from seclusion. Rex Lapis lives on as Zhongli. Cloud Retainer (as Xianyun) and Madame Ping live in Liyue Harbor, and Xiao keeps watch from Wangshu Inn.

15.comment: Adeptus: Sacred Names of the Adepti
15.content: Adepti go by sacred names. In Chinese they are usually four characters plus the honorific "Perfected Lord" (zhenjun). English keeps a short form: Cloud Retainer, Moon Carver, Mountain Shaper, Streetward Rambler (Madame Ping), and the dead Sea Gazer and Skybracer. Rex Lapis ("Sovereign Lord Rock King") and Xiao ("Conqueror of Demons", literally "Great Sage who Subdues Demons") use higher or different forms. The names do not prove adeptus status. Teapot spirits like Tubby (Rain Calmer) have them, and humans have adopted grand fake ones to pose as adepti. Shenhe has none because she is human.

16.comment: Adeptus: Jueyun Karst and the Seclusion of the Adepti
16.content: After the Archon War most adepti withdrew to Jueyun Karst, the misty peaks west of Liyue Harbor, including Mt. Aocang, Mt. Hulao and Qingyun Peak. Locals hold their rituals at its edges and do not go further. A Sigil of Permission, a Rex Lapis-made talisman, lets its holder enter the adepti's lands without offence. In Chapter I the Traveler carried a Fatui copy from Childe there to seek the adepti's help.

17.content: Adeptal energy is the distinct power each adeptus carries. Lent briefly, it can empower a mortal: three adepti infused the Traveler during the battle against Osial. Over longer periods it overwhelms human souls. Madame Ping warns that prolonged contact with adeptal treasures harms humans. Qiqi is the cautionary case: so much adeptal energy was poured into her to save her life that she could not bear it, and she had to be sealed in amber.

18.comment: Adeptus: The Adepti and the Osial Crisis
18.content: After Rex Lapis's apparent death at the Rite of Descension, the adepti blamed the Qixing and the two sides faced off outside the city. When the Fatui freed the sealed god Osial, the adepti joined the Qixing and Millelith on the Jade Chamber. Cloud Retainer, Moon Carver and Mountain Shaper channelled their power into upgraded Guizhong Ballistae. Madame Ping, Ganyu and Xiao lent the Traveler adeptal energy. Ningguang finally brought the Jade Chamber down on Osial. Cloud Retainer remarked that the adepti had not fought a god in several millennia.

19.content:
Aeonblight Drake (also: Perpetual Motion GL-Faf, Perpetual Motion Dragon, Aeonblight Drake (Heavy Assault Pack)): The Aeonblight Drake is a huge dragon-shaped combat machine, one of the Ruin Machines, found in Sumeru in the Ardravi Valley area of Devantaka Mountain. Its boss title is Perpetual Motion GL-Faf. It is a normal boss that fights on the ground and in the air, and it can take on and use the element that has harmed it most.

Its Adventurer Handbook entry calls it a being that inspires fear, as the lord who once ruled these lands did, and proof that a now-destroyed realm reached heights mortals should never have reached.

Nature: A tireless machine built in the shape of a dragon, with thrusters, a tail, a head it can strike with, and an element-storing core in its neck.

It is an automaton of the Ruin Drake group. The group is described as modelled on vishaps, the ancient creatures able to absorb or counteract elemental power, with structural changes and an unusual energy system that strengthen that ability. The group page says the colour of the Chaos Storage in the neck reflects the element currently absorbed.

Lore: The Handbook for the Ruin Drake group calls the machines war machines said to have been left by a now-destroyed nation, Khaenri'ah, that imitate the vishaps' ability to counteract elements. The Aeonblight Drake's own Archive entry speaks of that realm's attempts at perpetual motion.

Abilities and limits: Game mechanics (labelled as such): it deals Physical damage and has high Physical resistance. Grounded it uses tail sweeps, thruster smashes, nose strikes and a charge; airborne it uses a machine gun volley, a missile barrage and a charge. Its Energy Surge scatters bombs that land as Physical or as the absorbed element.

Individuals: The Aeonblight Drake of Ardravi Valley is the open-world boss. Its event form, Aeonblight Drake (Heavy Assault Pack), appeared in the limited-time event Feast of the Departed Warriors.

Relations: It is a Ruin Machine boss alongside the Ruin Serpent and the Perpetual Mechanical Array. It is not part of King Deshret's machinery: the Primal Constructs of the desert are a separate line of automata.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1, the Aeonblight Drake remains a boss in Sumeru. Its builders' purpose and the identity of the lord the Handbook mentions are not explained.

20.content: Ruin Drakes are Ruin Machines modelled on vishaps, found in Sumeru and Fontaine. They use Physical attacks, have high Physical resistance and adapt to elements through their Energy Surge attack. The Aeonblight Drake is the boss of the group.

21.content: Perpetual Caliber is the exclusive drop of the Aeonblight Drake.

key: Algorithm of Semi-Intransient Matrix of Overseer Network
Tomb Guard of the Desert King
22.comment: Algorithm of Semi-Intransient Matrix of Overseer Network
22.content:
Algorithm of Semi-Intransient Matrix of Overseer Network (also: Tomb Guard of the Desert King, Matrix of Overseer Network, ASIMON, Field Annihilation Array, Anoushbord): The Algorithm of Semi-Intransient Matrix of Overseer Network is a large Primal Construct, an automaton left by the ancient civilisation of King Deshret. It is a normal boss found at the Dune of Elusion in the Hypostyle Desert of Sumeru, with the boss title Tomb Guard of the Desert King. It fights with lasers and by turning invisible behind deployed parts.

The Adventurer Handbook calls it a perpetual-motion device that governs the many ruin machines scattered through the desert and still seems to carry the will of its lonely ruler, King Deshret. Players often shorten its name to ASIMON; the abbreviation appears in official media only once, in a Spanish achievement name added in 4.0.

Nature: A perpetual-motion machine from an ancient desert civilisation, working as a governing node over lesser constructs.

It belongs to the Primal Constructs, the elite leftover technology of King Deshret's civilisation found across the Great Red Sand. The Primal Construct Handbook text calls such machines guardians of the ruins who punish those who disturb the pure dreams of their lord; their dreams and oaths survive now only as mantras inscribed upon them.

Lore: The boss's description card, titled Matrix of Overseer Network, speaks of an ancient capital buried beneath the sands, where an autonomous machine was developed and built, and which still remembers the dreams of the fallen King Deshret.

Abilities and limits: Game mechanics (labelled as such): it deals Physical damage. It opens every fight with a Laser Zone, then follows with Repulse, Reshape and Prospect attacks, each matching one of its part types, and with tracking lasers and a missile. Its signature behaviour is an invisible state: it leaves Repulsor, Reshaper and Prospector parts on the field and gains very high resistance while they attack the player.

Individuals: The open-world boss is at the Dune of Elusion. The same model is used as a stage boss in some quests, under other names: Field Annihilation Array (The Evincing Shadow) in the world quest Dual Evidence, and Anoushbord (Forgotten Mechanical Guardian) in The Temple Where Sand Flows Like Tears.

Relations: The Handbook says it governs the many ruin machines scattered through the desert. It belongs to King Deshret's technology, a separate line from the Khaenri'ahn Ruin Machines.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1, the Algorithm remains in the Hypostyle Desert. Whether it truly preserves the king's will is not established.

23.comment: Algorithm of Semi-Intransient Matrix of Overseer Network: Primal Construct
23.content: Primal Constructs are elite automata left by King Deshret's civilisation, found mostly across the Great Red Sand. They deploy parts and may become invisible; Electro on a part being repaired, or Quicken, Frozen or Petrification on the construct itself, ends the state. The Algorithm is their boss form.

24.comment: Algorithm of Semi-Intransient Matrix of Overseer Network: Light Guiding Tetrahedron
24.content: The Light Guiding Tetrahedron is the exclusive drop of the Algorithm of Semi-Intransient Matrix of Overseer Network.

key: Visitor from the Far Side of the Sea of Stars
25.content:
All-Devouring Narwhal (also: Visitor from the Far Side of the Sea of Stars, the All-Devouring Narwhal): The All-Devouring Narwhal is a colossal whale-like creature from the sea of stars, outside Teyvat's sky. It is the pet of Surtalogi the Foul, Skirk's master. It fed on the Primordial Sea beneath Fontaine, which made the sea level rise, and its rampage set off the flood the Prophecy of Fontaine foretold. Neuvillette and the Traveler defeated it in the Primordial Sea, and Skirk shrank it to an orb and took it away.

Poets liken the night sky to an ocean; this beast is the nightmare version of that image, a leviathan that swims between worlds. It is drawn to the "blood" of Fontainians and cannot resist its instinct to devour. After the story, the battle can be relived as the weekly boss fight in the Shadow of Another World domain.

Nature: A vast, mysterious creature "from another world". Neuvillette describes it as a monster that crossed the stars weeping. It is not a native of Teyvat and belongs to no known species. It devours, and it craves energy and living things.

Its in-game Archive entry reads, before the finale, simply as a mysterious, gargantuan creature from another world. After the finale the entry adds a reflection: poets compare the starry sky to the sea, and the universe may be constantly trying to infiltrate Teyvat, or a higher power may have raised borders (the false sky) to protect it. The Archive does not say which.

The creature is a pet only in Surtalogi's eyes. Skirk calls it uncooperative, a glutton and a failure as a pet. Neuvillette names its instincts as the fight's key: it "cannot resist its instinct to devour", and so it can be provoked into swallowing someone.

Origins: Its origin world is unknown. Surtalogi, one of the Five Sinners of Khaenri'ah, left Teyvat after the Cataclysm to seek stronger opponents among the stars, and the Narwhal became his pet. According to the quests it:
- entered Teyvat at some point and began drinking energy from the Primordial Sea, which raised sea levels around Fontaine;
- was, in the account Neuvillette investigated, awakened by chance by the young Tartaglia (then Ajax, who says he was fourteen) when he fell into an unknown chasm or abyss; and
- turned up in Fontaine's Primordial Sea, where it had been fighting Tartaglia since he escaped the Fortress of Meropide.

Events: During the Fontaine Archon Quest (4.2), the Narwhal appears first in the Traveler's dream and then in person. It bursts out of a rift in space into the Opera Epiclese during Furina's trial, and the crowd flees. Neuvillette's first attempts to stop it fail, and the creature turns toward the escapees. Tartaglia, in his Foul Legacy form, appears out of the rift and attacks it, which gives Neuvillette time to join him. Tartaglia then falls unconscious into the hole.

Abilities and limits: It swims through solid ground as if it were water, rising to leap or dive at its target. It conjures falling crystals and beams of light, and it can swallow a fighter whole.

Game mechanics (labelled as such): it is a weekly boss. Most attacks are Hydro: leaps and dives that crack the ground and burst into splashes, a rain of crystals, beams of light, and an Eye of Maelstrom that pulls players inward and then explodes. The domain's text says Pneuma or Ousia (Arkhe) attacks can quickly destroy the whirlpool.

The signature mechanic is hostility. Damage dealt, and the Eye's destruction, fill a Fury meter that also rises with time. When it is full, the beast devours a character and sends them into its belly to fight the Dark Shadow. Beating the Shadow takes a large share of the Narwhal's HP, paralyses it and fills the party's Energy. Below 20% HP it stops devouring.

Relations: Surtalogi owns it. Skirk, his disciple, defeated and shrank it when it threatened her student. Tartaglia has an old tie with it, and he built the whale shape into his own fighting style after meeting it.

Neuvillette and the Traveler are the ones who finish it in the story. Skofnungr carries a graft of its flesh, and the Dark Shadow in the Narwhal also wears Surtalogi's form, suggesting its power is bound up with imitations of him.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it is shrunk to an orb that Skirk threw through a rift after the 4.2 battle, and it has not been shown since. The weekly domain Shadow of Another World (a Trounce Domain in Salacia Plain, Court of Fontaine region) lets the player relive the fight as a memory, and is unlocked after finishing the Fontaine Archon Quest. It is a replay, not a new appearance.

26.comment: All-Devouring Narwhal: Dark Shadow of the Narwhal
26.content: The Dark Shadow is the armoured, claymore-wielding figure inside the All-Devouring Narwhal's belly. A hostile entity in Skirk's story quest (Whispers Betwixt Stars and Night, 5.7) wears the same form; Skirk explains that those longing for Surtalogi's strength imitate him on a subconscious level. When its armour breaks, the wearer is Skofnungr, a Khaenri'ahn friend and follower of Surtalogi who fused some Narwhal flesh into his heart.

key: Memories: The Titan Amidst the Stars
27.comment: All-Devouring Narwhal: Shadow of Another World
27.content: A Trounce Domain in the Court of Fontaine region that unlocks after the Fontaine Archon Quest's Finale. The player can relive the battle against the Narwhal there. Its description calls that battle the intersection point of this world's fate and says Fontaine now treads a brighter path. Rewards are weekly-boss materials: Lightless Silk String, Lightless Eye of the Maelstrom and Lightless Mass.

28.comment: All-Devouring Narwhal: The whale and the Prophecy of Fontaine
28.content: In "Apocalypse", Paimon concludes that the whale is the real cause of the disaster in the prophecy. Neuvillette later calls it the root of Fontaine's calamities and the beast that enacts the prophecy. Its drinking from the Primordial Sea raised the water and its defeat caused the final upheaval.

29.comment: All-Devouring Narwhal: Tartaglia and the whale
29.content: In The City of Rains and Remembrance (4.0) Tartaglia says that at fourteen he fell into an unknown abyss, dreamed of a vast whale and had awakened "it"; Neuvillette's investigation in Finale says he by chance awakened the All-Devouring Narwhal after falling into an unknown chasm. He later fought it in the Primordial Sea after escaping the Fortress of Meropide, which delayed its landing. His Foul Legacy transformation uses a whale motif.

30.content:
Aranara (also: Aranaras, forest spirits of Sumeru): The Aranara are small, plantlike forest spirits of Sumeru, living mainly in Vanarana, a village hidden inside a dream in Dharma Forest. The Dendro Archon Greater Lord Rukkhadevata, whom they called Queen Aranyani, made them to guard the forest and its creatures. They are friendly, curious and easily frightened, shy of adults, close to children, and they treasure memories and songs.

Most adults think them a myth or a child's imaginary friend. The Akademiya's Amurta darshan looked into them and, since its sensors cannot detect them as children can, filed them as "unidentified lifeforms". Their central story is the Aranyaka World Quest series (3.0), in which the Traveler helps them make a Bija fruit to save a Forest Watcher named Rana.

Nature: Aranara come in many shapes, colours and hats (a mushroom cap, a pair of leaves) and always seem to smile. Many have a leaf on top of the head that works as a small propeller and lets them fly. They do not need to sleep or eat, are very afraid of fire and salt, and can be revitalised with Dendro energy.

Like plants, an Aranara in great danger can turn into a seed and hibernate; once the crisis passes the seed sprouts back into an Aranara, which takes a lot of energy. The last stage of an Aranara's life is growing into a Vasara Tree, whose size and growth speed depend on the memories it holds. They can hide from human eyes, talk to plants and mushrooms, and befriend wild animals such as Rishboland Tigers. They are long-lived and sentimental.

Abilities and limits: Each Aranara has its own Ararakalari, powers drawn from its memories and channelled through the plants of the forest. They can fight, restrain or weaken enemies, shield against the Withering, teleport over great distances in an instant and seal off areas.

Ararakalari burn memories as fuel, so using one costs the Aranara something of itself. Aranara can also selectively create and remove dreams and memories. An Aranara's Ararakalari can grow when it gains new memories, its own or someone else's: Aramuhukunda gained the ability to counter the Withering after seeing Queen Aranyani do so, and Arama received his teleportation by inheriting his memories. Channelling the power through a Kusava seed strengthens it and can let a human use Ararakalari briefly.

Society: The Aranara live in Vanarana, a hidden village. Their elder Araja and the lively Arana are two of the main figures; most Aranara have names beginning "Ara-".

Aranara love festivals. In the Aranyaka story the village holds a Festival Utsava, where a Bija can be formed, and Aramuhukunda recalls an earlier Festival Utsava shared with Nara Varuna. Many practise crafts learned from humans: cooking, shopkeeping, song gathering, mending the Varuna Contraption, and tending the Vanarana nursery. Named Aranara across Sumeru also offer small tasks and games.

Origin: Rukkhadevata created the Aranara shortly after she left the desert to make Dharma Forest. She sang a song that made the Ashvattha Tree grow "from Sarva"; it bore a pomegranate, and each seed became an Aranara, Aramuhukunda being the first. The Aranara guarded the forest, befriended its creatures and for a time lived alongside humans.

History: The Aranara first lived in Old Vanarana and were friendly with Sumeru's humans, many of whom visited them in Vanarana and the Ashvattha's Concourses. When the Cataclysm struck, many Aranara fought the invaders from the Abyss before leaving Old Vanarana, and built a new Vanarana to the north. The true Vanarana was hidden in a dream, anchored to the real world by the Tree of Dreams. When Sumeru's people stopped dreaming, the Aranara grew wary of grown humans.

Relations: Aranara trust children and few adults. The golden-haired Traveler is accepted as kin of Nara Varuna, and the Forest Watcher Rana is trusted as an exception. After Rana is saved, Arana leaves Vanarana to travel with her. The Aranara also gave the Tighnarians the name Valuka Shuna when they came to the rainforest.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Aranara still live in Vanarana and its dream, Mahavanaranapna. Arama stands as the new Ashvattha Tree in Old Vanarana, Marana's Avatar is destroyed and Old Vanarana is recovering, though the Withering is still present elsewhere in Sumeru.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay guidance (project recommendation): write Aranara as gentle, shy and curious, speaking simply and warmly and using words such as "Nara"; they hide or freeze when frightened.

31.content: Ararakalari are the memory-fed powers of the Aranara. Each Aranara has a unique one, which may attack, restrain, teleport, seal an area or guard against the Withering. Using it consumes memories, but new memories can add new abilities. Arama says they originate in the "Mahamaitri Kusa Stotra", a song praising Queen Aranyani, humans and the Aranara. A Kusava seed makes them stronger.

32.content: A Vasara Tree is what an Aranara can choose to become at the end of its life; it keeps dreams and memories, and even some awareness, and other Aranara still treat it as the Aranara it was. The first Vasara Tree is the Ashvattha Tree that Rukkhadevata made. In Aranyaka the Traveler cleanses three Vasara Trees (Araji, Aramaha, Arayama), each of which bears a Vasoma Fruit to feed the corroded Ashvattha Tree. It can no longer bear a Bija, so Arama becomes the new Ashvattha Tree in Old Vanarana. Arana, though ancient, refuses to become a Vasara Tree while she still wants to play with humans.

33.content: Marana is the Aranara name for the Withering. In Araja's telling it began after Rukkhadevata returned to Sarva, and urges everything toward death. The Aranara say it can turn Vana (forest) into Valuka (desert). Its avatars take many forms. In the Aranyaka story the Traveler and Arama destroy Marana's Avatar in the Land of Grounded Dreams beneath Old Vanarana, after which Old Vanarana begins to rejuvenate.

34.content: Vanarana is the Aranara's village in Dharma Forest. Old Vanarana, the original home, was abandoned in the Cataclysm and became the heart of the Withering. The Aranara built a new Vanarana to the north and hid the true one in a dream, Mahavanaranapna, held to the real world by the Tree of Dreams (Araja). It is entered by playing the "Rhythm of the Great Dream" on a Vintage Lyre at the Phantasmal Gate or a Silapna.

35.content: Nara Varuna was the Aranara's name for the Traveler's Sibling, a golden-haired human who helped repair the Varuna Contraption and shared the last Festival Utsava with Aramuhukunda and his friends. Before leaving, they told the Aranara to expect another golden-haired human who would bring even better memories. The Aranara therefore welcome the Traveler as kin of Nara Varuna.

36.content: Arana is an Aranara of Vimara Village, with a pale mint body, floppy ear-like structures, a dark green conical hat decorated with a blue butterfly, and two orange leaves that act as a propeller. She was Rana's childhood friend but forgot her. In the Aranyaka quests she shielded Iotham and then Rana from the Withering, and she gave up her memories to the new Ashvattha Tree to produce the Bija. She then befriended Rana again and left to travel with her.

37.content: Arama is a pale green Aranara with a yellow flower on its head and a red scarf, and the protagonist of the Aranyaka story. It wins the Traveler's trust, helps destroy Marana's Avatar and then grows into the new Ashvattha Tree. Aramuhukunda is the oldest Aranara, first to sprout from the Ashvattha Tree; he became a Vasara Tree to hold back Marana's Avatar and, at the end of the story, happily returned to Sarva. Araja is the village elder, who became the Tree of Dreams and created Mahavanaranapna.

38.content: Queen Aranyani is what the Aranara called Greater Lord Rukkhadevata, the Dendro Archon who made them and led them until she disappeared. Her song was closest to the Sourcesong. After her memory was removed from the Irminsul in the 3.2 Archon Quest, the Aranara are said no longer to remember her under that name and instead speak of the Lord of Verdure.

39.content: Aranara songs are tied to power and identity. Playing the right song on a Vintage Lyre can open a Silapna or a Gloomy Path, or call a Dendrograna. Song gatherers collect other Aranara's songs and look for the Sourcesong; the closer a song is to it, the stronger the Ararakalari.

40.content:
Augury Bird (also: Augury Birds, Augury Bird fae): Augury Birds are one of the less common kinds of Snowland Fae, set apart from the six common kinds (Vila, Domovoy, Leshy, Volkodlak, Snegovik and Jack Frost). They grow head-wings as they mature, shimmer faintly with a dusting of small crystals, and live only a little longer than humans. Their defining gift is a sight of their own fate, which they regard as a burden rather than a blessing. Celaeno says the living ones can be counted on one hand.

Nature: Like other Snowland Fae, Augury Birds were part of the creation of the fae in Hyperborea and are native to Snezhnaya, though the two known individuals now spend time in Nod-Krai. Unlike many fae they are not long-lived. Celaeno says they do not live much longer than humans and treats death as part of the natural cycle.

Physically they look nearly human. As they grow up they develop a pair of working wings on the head. Linnea's profile describes this as two stubborn tufts of hair that eventually unfurl into tiny wings, accompanied by a shimmering dusting of small crystals on her skin. Hidden under a hat or headwear, an Augury Bird can pass as a human, which is exactly what Linnea did for years.

Abilities and limits: Augury Birds are born with a prophetic sense. Celaeno describes it as seeing "crossroads in the flow of fate", meaning immutable future events that every path leads to. Two limits matter.
- It shows only the Augury Bird's own fate. They cannot foretell the future of a friend or of the world.
- What is seen cannot be changed, according to Celaeno. She says that trying to defy it only makes the suffering worse.

Linnea's first vision came after she touched Celaeno's hand during the Spirit Envoy Championship in Nod-Krai: she collapsed and saw her own future, including the end of her life, which left her numb and in tears. How the sight is triggered is not explained in the sources read.

Like other fae, Augury Birds use elemental power without a Vision. Linnea carries a Moon Wheel that her Jack Frost companion once swallowed, and her power is Geo.

Society: There is no recorded Augury Bird community in canon. The known family is a single household in the tundra of inland Snezhnaya: Celaeno, her parents, and Linnea, who is Celaeno's younger sister. Celaeno also helped raise the human girl her parents swapped Linnea with.

Relations: Linnea and Celaeno are sisters by birth. Lumi, a Geo Jack Frost, travels with Linnea. In Nod-Krai, the Adventurers' Guild and the children of Speranza know Linnea as an advisor, naturalist and teacher. Lumi's size-changing outburst, the Traveler and Paimon, and Aguara (the Traveler's Tepetlisaur Whelp, who found Celaeno by scent) all feature in the story that reveals the kind.

Individuals: - Celaeno: the elder sister. A tall young woman with long, straight dark blue hair and lavender eyes. Blunt, prickly and protective of the human girl her family adopted; she fought in the Spirit Envoy Championship with Haemus, lost in the final to the Traveler, and afterwards returned to Snezhnaya. After the quest she can be found in Snezhnograd, where she says she is running errands and escorting the human girl, and where she finds the capital too loud.
- Linnea: the younger sister, raised by humans in Nod-Krai, now an Adventurers' Guild advisor and naturalist. Playable (Geo, Moon Wheel).
- Their parents: unnamed Augury Birds in the tundra of inland Snezhnaya.

How {{char}} behaves: A recommended way to portray an Augury Bird, as this project's interpretation and not canon: treat the sight as private, unwelcome and personal, never as a fortune-telling service. A character may say that they know their own fate but cannot reveal anyone else's. Keep the wings hidden under a hat in public. Do not give the kind a catalogue of prophecies or let them predict world events.

41.comment: Augury Bird: Celaeno and the changeling swap
41.content: Celaeno is the elder Augury Bird sister, from the tundra of inland Snezhnaya. Her parents, wanting to spare their next child the burden of foresight, had Linnea raised by humans and brought up a human girl with a rare disease in her place. Celaeno came to Nod-Krai intending to hurt Linnea with the truth, found she could not, and became a wary relation. She tamed the Radiant Bladehorn Haemus and fought in the Spirit Envoy Championship before releasing him.

42.content:
Automatons (also: Automaton, Automatons family, Mechanical enemies, Primal Constructs, Secret Source Automatons, Domain Keepers): "Automatons" is the game's name for mechanical enemies. They are not one race or one invention: the family groups machines built by different, often long-dead makers. The biggest group is the Ruin Machines of Khaenri'ah (which have their own entry). The rest are Primal Constructs from King Deshret's desert, Clockwork Meka built in Fontaine, Secret Source Automatons found in Natlan and on the Frost Moon, and the Domain Keepers of the Temple of Space. Most fight with physical force and have no will of their own.

Two odd cases sit beside the groups: the Maguu Kenki, a masterless mechanical swordsman, and Knuckle Duckle, a duck-shaped home robot built by Aino. Nothing new was added in 7.0 or 7.1.

Nature: Machines, not living creatures. Most still active are leftovers of lost civilisations with no master left; dormant ones wake when someone comes near.

The groups differ in how they work: Ruin Machines are mostly Physical fighters; Primal Constructs also use Physical attacks but can turn invisible; Clockwork Meka are imbued with Arkhe energy; Secret Source Automatons respond to Nightsoul; Domain Keepers watch the elements. The Adventurer Handbook says Clockwork Meka were also "an excellent assistant to thieves and brigands".

Groups: - Ruin Machines (1.0): Khaenri'ah's, own entry.
- Primal Constructs (3.1): Deshret's desert guardians.
- Clockwork Meka (4.0): Fontaine's, charged with Arkhe.
- Secret Source Automatons (5.0): Natlan's ancient machines, plus a Frost Moon variant (6.7).
- Domain Keepers (6.5): Temple of Space guardians.

Two named machines have their own place: the Maguu Kenki (1.6, Golden Apple Archipelago and Inazuma) and Knuckle Duckle (6.0, Nod-Krai). Both are covered in sub-entries.

Abilities and limits: Mostly Physical damage and a weak point that stuns them when hit; several groups have a trick such as invisibility or retaliation.

Gameplay (not literal lore): Primal Constructs fire parts and turn invisible, which can be broken with Electro attacks or by triggering Quicken, Frozen or Petrification. Clockwork Meka are charged with Pneuma (bright white clockwork) or Ousia (dark blue); striking them with the opposite Arkhe overloads them. Secret Source Automatons prepare a stronger counter when a character uses Nightsoul's Blessing against them. A Domain Keeper switches into an elemental form after enough hits of one element.

Society: Automatons have no society: they have routes, instructions and defence duties. The Overseer Device and the Matrix of Overseer Network were built to command or oversee other machines, not to rule people. The Algorithm of Semi-Intransient Matrix of Overseer Network governs the many constructs of the desert, and its Archive text says the lonely ruler's will still seems to dwell in it.

Relations: Automatons relate to people through whoever built or now uses them. Fontaine's Maison Gardiennage uses humanoid meka for municipal security, and the Fontaine Research Institute of Kinetic Energy Engineering is the main body behind meka research. The Ruin Machines are tied to the Abyss Order and the Fatui by their own entry.

Individuals: Named machines: the Algorithm of Semi-Intransient Matrix of Overseer Network (Primal Constructs, 3.1), Icewind Suite (Coppelia and Coppelius, 4.0), Prototype Cal. Breguet (4.1), the Secret Source Automaton Hunter-Seeker (5.0), Configuration Device (5.1) and Overseer Device (5.6), the Precursor's Secret Source Matrix of Overseer Network and its Local Legend Mushteshir (6.7), the Maguu Kenki and Knuckle Duckle.

Scene use: This project's suggestion (not canon): present Automatons as relics that obey old instructions rather than monsters with motives. Pick the group by setting: the desert for dream-haunted guardians, Fontaine for tools turned to security, Natlan for forgotten work machines.

43.content: Primal Constructs are elite automatons found mainly across the Great Red Sand, leftover technology of King Deshret's civilisation. Their three Archive entries (Repulsor, Reshaper, Prospector) all open with the same line: the guardians of the lost desert ruins have power enough to punish any who disturb the pure dreams of their lord. They add that the machines were not first built as guards but to rebirth the paradise that the "foolish desert ruler" dreamed of, that the lord of the blazing sun promised his people a utopia on the other side of existence that turned out to be a mirage, and that the master of the sands studied taboo knowledge to create a dream paradise, with these machines possibly being the fruits of it. Today only mantras inscribed on the machines preserve the dreams and oaths.

44.content: Clockwork Meka are enemy machines made by Fontaine to serve as laborers and later modified for combat. They are charged with Arkhe, either Pneuma (bright white clockwork) or Ousia (dark blue clockwork), which lets them deal elemental damage. Hitting a meka with the opposite energy overloads it, so that it temporarily loses its Arkhe and can only attack physically or not at all. Common Meka (Normal and Specialist Meks) and bosses form the group; a Normal Mek takes one opposite-Arkhe hit to weaken, a Specialist Mek two, a boss three.

45.content: Secret Source Automatons are mainly found in Natlan and appear idle until disturbed. Archive text says they were created by a long-lost civilisation to carry out work: the Hunter-Seeker collected samples and had only basic combat functions; the Configuration Device was a manufacturing machine, shaped like a giant claw, that could transform to build colossal cities even inside a volcano; the Overseer Device was a domination mechanism by which a mighty ancient race oversaw the running of its cities through "phlogiston-engineered intelligence", and it keeps only basic commands since that civilisation fell in wars with an emerging race. Rumour says they were not built by humans.

46.comment: Automatons: Precursor's Secret Source Matrix of Overseer Network
46.content: A variant of the Secret Source machines found on the Frost Moon, which uses the moon's Archaeolune Energy to gather Hydro. Its Archive text calls it an ancient machine trapped in lunar ruins that has lost the purpose its makers gave it; it now attacks anything entering its ground. Records of a lost civilisation call these machines "Ur-Namrasit-Tilimtu-Babbar", "the one who brings light to the darkness"; the "pioneers" engraved their most earnest words in golden sigils, hoping their successors would keep the light of the universe shining, but the machine named "overseer" never found the one it should have served.

47.content: Domain Keepers are elite automatons that guard the Temple of Space (Segment-Domain Tau) in the sky above Windrest Peak. Their Archive text calls them shadow constructs born from the overflow of a mighty primordial being, guardians of the Pillar Hall of the heavens. Entrusted with "eyes" but able only to extol the "Ideal Forms" of the noumenal world, they cannot see the phenomenal world's complexity and so are not counted among the angels. The text wonders if this contradiction was a design of their creator or a failure of their master to grasp the primordial being's intent. The Adventurer Handbook says the guards' differing appearances suggest different roles. The wiki credits their making to Asmoday, the temple's former owner.

48.content: The Maguu Kenki is an autonomous humanoid swordsman of unknown make. Archive text says it was built from the memories of the first-generation master of a sword school (the Tengu Sweeper technique is mentioned), but malfunctioned, lost control and was discarded. It cannot or will not speak and seeks only to communicate with crossed swords; its vicious mask is said to be inspired by a famous oni. In Inazuma it stands at Serpent's Head on Yashiori Island. It first appeared in the limited-time Golden Apple Archipelago event (1.6) on Twinning Isle, where wiki trivia says Ako Domeki's crew had taken it and were shipwrecked 500 years ago; this trivia is not tied to a direct statement in the Archive.

49.content: A duck-shaped kuuvahki mechanism made of scrap metal and mechanical bearings, and a boss. Its Archive text says it is as strong and tough as the Fatui's newest weapons, yet is simply a toy duck that can punch very hard, shaped by its creator's tastes. In its own dialogue it calls itself a multipurpose armed robot for domestic use created by Master Aino under the code name "Knuckle Duckle", with security, surveillance, storage, dusting, cleaning and krumkake baking functions. It guards the Workshop's Trove used by Aino and Ineffa.

50.content:
Avatar of Lava (also: Avatars of Lava, Eroding Avatar of Lava, Fluid Avatar of Lava, Lava Dragon Statue, Seeing Eyes): Avatars of Lava are elite creatures of Natlan with a core of lava. They must keep absorbing heat to stay active, and are often found dormant until the Traveler uses Elemental Sight. Archive text treats them as hollow leftovers of very old attempts to make life from fire and phlogiston, with no more will than a stone. Two ordinary types exist (Eroding and Fluid) and one boss form, the Lava Dragon Statue.

The Adventurer Handbook says their traits depend on the circumstances of their formation: the heat of the core, which it calls the "Seeing Eye", and the rock around it.

Nature: A strange monster that needs to absorb thermal energy continually or it goes inert. Its heart is a core of molten rock and the body is built from stone around it.

The Eroding type's Archive entry says the ancient civilisation drove huge constructs and cities with golden patterns that guided the flow of phlogiston. Besides machines with fixed structures, it says, Avatars of Lava are badly damaged lifeforms once made the same way, and after the flames of the sacred mountain went out most of them lost purpose and direction.

Abilities and limits: They fight in melee and with eruptions of heat. Eroding types are of the Geo kind; Fluid types are Pyro.

Gameplay (not literal lore): the Eroding Avatar of Lava and the Lava Dragon Statue carry a "Fury" gauge that fills when they are hit with Pyro attacks. At set intervals they take damage equal to a share of their HP; filling the gauge outright defeats the Eroding type, while the boss shifts into a different state depending on its form. The Fluid type has no Fury gauge but resists Pyro strongly, as the boss does while it is not in a weakened state.

Relations: They are hostile to anyone who comes near. Archive text places them among the leftovers of Natlan's ancient fire-and-phlogiston age, alongside constructs such as the Primal Constructs, and not within any tribe or order. No tribe or faction is said to command them.

Individuals: The Lava Dragon Statue is the one distinctive individual form: a boss in the Atocpan area of Natlan, introduced in 5.5, called "Stone-Hearted Final Form of Flowing Flame". Its Archive entry calls it a creature raised in a geothermal fissure to restore an ancient race, now only a senseless beast that punishes anyone who comes near.

Scene use: This project's suggestion (not canon): use an Avatar of Lava as a mute, instinct-driven guardian of a hot cavern, or as a quiet reminder of the ancient age that burned out. Do not give it speech, goals or a master.

key: Stone-Hearted Final Form of Flowing Flame
51.comment: Avatar of Lava: Lava Dragon Statue
51.content: A boss form of the Avatar of Lava found in Atocpan, first seen in 5.5. Archive text says it was created in the depths of a geothermal fissure in an attempt to restore an ancient race but became a senseless beast acting only on primal instinct. It carries a Fury gauge that fills under Pyro attacks and is in a weakened state when its lava body is exposed.

52.content:
Bake-Danuki (also: tanuki, tanuki youkai, raccoon dog youkai): Bake-danuki, also just called tanuki, are youkai of Inazuma that look like small plump raccoon dogs, often with a leaf on the head and a bag around the neck. They can transform into objects and even people, and love pranking humans. Their leader is Ioroi, the Hidden Protector of the Grove, sealed inside a large statue in Chinju Forest.

The in-game Archive calls them carefree, leaving no trace when they go, with mystical arts known only to their own kind. They are not wicked and tease humans for fun. The one recorded exception was a past battle in Chinju Forest, after which most bake-danuki were sealed in stone statues.

Nature: Youkai tricksters. They shapeshift into objects and people, and the Archive stresses they mean no harm.

In open-world play they disguise themselves as torches, vases, crates, rock piles, chests, explosive barrels and similar objects, or dance and teleport away to lead players on. When a prank ends they vanish in a puff of smoke. Kichiboushi is a rare brown-furred example. Ioroi's statue form shows a large, jolly bake-danuki in a conical straw hat holding a sake cup, surrounded by smaller statues.

Abilities and limits: Transformation into objects and humans, and illusions. They are not fighters.

Their magic is passed down only among their kind. A folk tale in Glimpses of Mysterious Inazuma has the samurai Takehiko learn bake-danuki magic to hide himself inside a stone; this is in-world folklore.

Society: Loose communities under one leader, Ioroi, who lives in Chinju Forest on Narukami Island.

Named bake-danuki include Ioroi, Kichiboushi, Shousei, Gyoubu Koban, Giichiro (a statue), Mamesuke, Shibasuke, Tsukumo, Tetsunosuke, Ginkaku and Kinkaku. Ioroi plans to make Kichiboushi his successor once the younger tanuki is grown.

Relations: Rivals and sometime friends of the kitsune. They tangle with the Shogunate's officers when pranks go too far.

Ioroi and the Kitsune Saiguu competed for years: she dared him to steal a Naku Weed from the imperial garden, Ei nearly cut him down, and the Saiguu begged for his life. He still owes her, and calls her "that sneaky kitsune".

Individuals: - Ioroi: leader, Hidden Protector of the Grove, sealed in Chinju Forest.
- Kichiboushi: a young, rare brown bake-danuki who guides the Traveler to Ioroi's comb and is Ioroi's intended successor.

History: Bake-danuki have long lived on Narukami's lands. About 500 years ago the Cataclysm and Ioroi's reaction to losing the Saiguu led to most of them being sealed in stone statues.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 bake-danuki appear only in Inazuma. Ioroi remains in statue form; no Nod-Krai (6.x) or Snezhnaya (7.0-7.1) content features tanuki.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon): playful and boastful, quick to claim credit, secretly kind. A tanuki prank should be harmless and end in a puff of smoke.

53.content: Ioroi is the leader of the bake-danuki, sealed in a statue in Chinju Forest. He was spared by the Raiden Shogun at the Saiguu's request and made Protector of the Grove. He misread her disappearance during the Cataclysm as hide-and-seek, caused trouble to draw her out, took the Sacred Sakura comb, and was sealed by Kamuna Harunosuke. He deflects whenever her fate is mentioned.

54.content: Kichiboushi is a rare brown-furred bake-danuki who helps the Traveler find Ioroi's comb and whom Ioroi intends as his successor.

55.content: Open-world tanuki lead players with dancing and teleporting or disguise themselves as nearby objects. Completing fifteen pranks earns an achievement; the spoils are ordinary goods such as produce.

56.content:
Bathysmal Vishap (also: Bathysmal Vishaps, Dragonheirs of the Depths, Dragonheir of the Depths, Hydro Vishaps, Coral Defenders, Bathysmal Vishap Herd, Rimebiter Bathysmal Vishap, Bolteater Bathysmal Vishap): Bathysmal Vishaps, called the Dragonheirs of the Depths by the people of Enkanomiya, are a race of vishaps that live in the deep sea. They are aggressive toward humans, refuse man-made light, and adapt so quickly that individuals can carry Hydro, Cryo or Electro. They terrorised Enkanomiya (Byakuyakoku) for thousands of years until the Watatsumi Omikami suppressed them under the sea with jade coral. In recent years a few have appeared in Fontaine.

Their best-known members are the Coral Defenders: a Cryo Rimebiter and an Electro Bolteater, bred and modified in Enkanomiya and grafted with fragments of Orobashi's coral.

Nature: Vishaps of the Light Realm, living in the deep sea and in the caverns of Enkanomiya. The Adventurer Handbook calls them a mighty race that hates light not from weak eyesight, but because the sunlight and the surface world were taken from them, so they refuse man-made light.

They are intelligent and unusually adaptable. They can choose which inherited traits to pass to their offspring and can even create new traits, including elemental affinities, so adaptation can happen within a single generation. The Byakuyakoku Collection gives an example: a heat-resistant vishap that matures in a cold place will have offspring with thick body fat, a tendency to sleep, and possibly a Cryo affinity. Before maturing, an individual can also choose which of its stored traits to activate, for instance heat resistance in a hot place or cold resistance in a cold one. One researcher remarked that they had already stored an armoury of abilities in their bodies before meeting the people of Enkanomiya.

Society: Little is known of their social life beyond what Enkanomiya's records say. The Handbook says the strongest members of the Coral Defenders herd use different elements as a show of their hatred, and that the herd was selected and bred by the people of Enkanomiya. The Bolteater Archive text says its Electro form arose from social adaptation (division of labour).

History: For thousands of years the Dragonheirs of the Depths preyed on the people of Enkanomiya, then called Byakuyakoku. Learning that the dragons loved the dark and feared light, the people hung thousands of lanterns, which was not enough. They prayed until Istaroth, one of the Four Shades of the Heavenly Principles, answered by giving Abrax the knowledge to build the Dainichi Mikoshi, the artificial sun on which Enkanomiya relied for an untold span of years.

Several thousand years ago the Watatsumi Omikami (Orobashi) defeated them and suppressed them beneath the sea with jade corals, then brought the people of Enkanomiya to the surface and made Watatsumi Island their home.

Legacy: The spirit of Watatsumi Island is said to feel the calls of Enkanomiya in the depths, and the island's soil is slowly bleaching into Holy Soil. By tradition, every few centuries the shrine maidens of Sangonomiya Shrine break the barrier when the spirit veins flow smoothly, retrieve a Jade Coral Branch left to suppress the Dragonheirs, and perform the Watatsumi Goryou Matsuri so the sunken spirit can return.

Abilities and limits: Individuals can carry Hydro, Cryo or Electro, and some wield more than one element. A signature attack, Cleansing Shower, drains Energy from its target, and a target without enough Energy loses HP instead.

Primordial Bathysmal Vishaps combine physical and Hydro attacks. The Rimebiter is Cryo, the Bolteater is Electro.

Variants: - Primordial Bathysmal Vishap: a Hydro form found in Enkanomiya; one Local Legend named Cineas lives in Machimos in the Sea of Bygone Eras. One also appears in Fontaine.
- Bathysmal Vishap Hatchlings: young vishaps, including Rimebiter and Bolteater hatchlings, which appear in Enkanomiya and Fontaine.
- Rimebiter Bathysmal Vishap (Cryo) and Bolteater Bathysmal Vishap (Electro): together the Coral Defenders, also known as the Bathysmal Vishap Herd. The Bolteater is met only in this fight.

Relations: Enemies of humans in Enkanomiya, with lanterns and the artificial sun as their historical deterrents. Watatsumi Island's Omikami subdued them. Neuvillette, the Hydro Dragon reborn as a human, is the Dragon of Water who would otherwise have been born from them.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 they remain hostile in Enkanomiya and are quietly appearing in Fontaine, where most people do not know of them.

Gameplay: Game mechanics, not lore: the Coral Defenders are a normal boss challenge that requires completing the related Archon and World Quests; Cleansing Shower drains Energy (or HP when Energy is short).

How {{char}} behaves: Treat them as proud wild creatures who distrust humans and light, not as mindless beasts: they are intelligent and can learn language. Fontaine's hatchlings are calm unless provoked. Canon does not show a Bathysmal Vishap speaking, so avoid inventing dialogue for one.

57.comment: Bathysmal Vishap: Dragonheirs of the Depths
57.content: Name the people of Byakuyakoku gave the race. Thousands of lanterns and later the Dainichi Mikoshi held them off, and the Watatsumi Omikami finally suppressed them under jade coral.

58.content: A pair of powerful vishaps, Cryo Rimebiter and Electro Bolteater, modified at the Vishap Research Lab to carry grafted fragments of Orobashi's coral. Their Handbook text says the herd was bred and selected by Enkanomiya's people, which no vishap would count as a debt.

59.comment: Bathysmal Vishap: Bathysmal Vishaps in Fontaine
59.content: Some Bathysmal Vishaps have recently surfaced in Fontaine at Loch Urania. Before the tree in Erinnyes Forest is restored a single Primordial Bathysmal Vishap lives there; afterwards hatchlings appear who are peaceful unless attacked. Most Fontainians do not know of them. Separately, a Primordial Bathysmal Vishap named Cineas lives in Machimos in Enkanomiya.

60.content:
Breacher Primus (also: Breacher Primuses, Overgrown Breacher Primus, Shatterstone Breacher Primus, Elynas' cells): Breacher Primuses are elite creatures of Fontaine, aligned with the Abyss and found mostly in and around the body of Elynas. The Archive calls them a strange life form with no known kin among Teyvat's creatures. According to Elynas himself they are his cells, made after his death, and they work like a body's defenders, driving harmful things away from him and his children.

They are not very intelligent. Elynas admits they sometimes attack the very people he would like them to spare, and Fontaine's earliest records after the Cataclysm show them both attacking and protecting humans. Known kinds include the Overgrown (Dendro) and Shatterstone (Geo) Breacher Primus, each in a small and a large form.

Nature: Alien, Abyss-aligned lifeforms that behave like the defensive cells of a giant body. They are tied to Elynas, the great beast whom the Melusines call "Father".

The wiki says they were created from Elynas' body shortly after the Cataclysm, around the same time as the Melusines, through the Abyss's power and his remains by methods canon does not explain. Elynas in the quest "Limner, Dreamer, and Robotic Dog" calls them his cells and says he retains some control over them when needed. They are described as an elite enemy group, outside the ordinary ecology of Teyvat.

Abilities and limits: In combat they use Physical attacks, a single projectile and melee strikes. Periodically a Primus enters a stressed state, gains a shield of its element and unleashes sustained elemental attacks. The Overgrown kind fires waves of Dendro missiles and the Shatterstone kind smashes the ground to cause Geo quakes. Breaking the shield, whether by elemental reactions or a single Arkhe attack, leaves it paralysed for a long time and exposes its core as a weak point (gameplay, labelled as such).

Society: They have no society. They act as Elynas' defenders, responding to threats near his body rather than to ordinary social cues, which is why they can strike friends and foes alike.

Relations: Elynas is their source and the only figure shown steering them. The Melusines are his other creation and the ones the Primuses are meant to shield. During the quest, Jakob's actions endanger Elynas and the Traveler is trapped by a spell, and Elynas sends a Shatterstone Breacher Primus to free them, after which it fights beside the Traveler for a time. Elynas apologises that his cells are not clever enough to avoid attacking friends too.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 they remain as hostile creatures in and around Elynas in Fontaine's depths. No later canon changes their nature.

Elynas' brief "time of life" ended after the Traveler stopped his revival, so the guiding voice behind them is again silent; the Primuses persist as instinctive guardians.

61.comment: Breacher Primus: Elynas and his cells
61.content: Elynas is the great beast the Melusines call "Father". He says he gave life to his children by accident, from the wounds of a battle in his body, and that the Breacher Primuses are his cells, able to push harmful things away but not wise enough to spare friends. He does not want to be revived, knowing his living body would crush the Melusines' homes.

62.comment: Breacher Primus: Overgrown and Shatterstone variants
62.content: The Overgrown Breacher Primus uses Dendro: in its stressed state it gains a Dendro shield and fires waves of Lushmissiles. The Shatterstone Breacher Primus uses Geo and brings down Stonefalls that cause quakes. A Shatterstone one is the kind that frees the Traveler in "Limner, Dreamer, and Robotic Dog".

63.content:
Cicin (also: Cicins, Electro Cicin, Hydro Cicin, Cryo Cicin, Fatui Cicin Mage, Fatui Cicin Mages, Cicin Mage): Cicins are common creatures found across Teyvat that look like small bats. The Archive describes them as little creatures able to manipulate an element only slightly, individually very weak, and shaped by that weakness into evasive fliers. In numbers they can still do real damage. They are best known as the minions of Fatui Cicin Mages.

Nature: The Archive entries for all three varieties open the same way: little creatures that can ever so slightly manipulate their element, known collectively as Cicins. The Cryo entry says they are individually very weak and that this weakness is exactly why they evolved unique ways of moving to avoid predators. The Electro entry says that, though weak alone, they can cause significant damage under the right circumstances. The Hydro entry says they adore the rare Mist Grass plant. Electro and Hydro Cicins are met in several places, with Guyun Stone Forest named as a location for both; Cryo Cicins are found on Dragonspine (introduced in version 1.2). The English name comes from Latin cicindela, firefly or glowworm.

Abilities and limits: Game mechanics, for reference: a Cicin has low HP, hovers out of reach and fires a single elemental bolt or icicle (Electro, Hydro or Cryo) at its target. When summoned by a Fatui Cicin Mage they gain special group attacks they cannot use alone, such as converging on a target to burst together. For narration, treat a Cicin as a darting, flickering nuisance: a few stinging bolts, not a siege.

Relations: Fatui Cicin Mages are an elite group within the Fatui who use Delusions to command elements. The Hydro Cicin Archive entry says it is by exploiting the Cicins' love of Mist Grass that Fatui Mages have sought to commandeer them in battle. The Adventurer Handbook adds that, as Cicins go crazy for Mist Grass, the mages take pleasure in toying with their prey, and that they seem to wander the land aimlessly as if compelled by some unknown duty. In the wild, mages are most often found alone, and an Electro or Cryo mage always summons three Cicins of her element.

Individuals: No individual Cicin is named in canon. Fatui Cicin Mages are likewise an unnamed enemy group.

64.content: Fatui Cicin Mages are an elite enemy group of the Fatui who use Delusions to command elements. They summon Cicins of their own element, and the Cicins fight beside them and help with defence and special attacks. The Adventurer Handbook describes them as taking pleasure in toying with prey, and as seeming to wander without purpose, as if compelled by some unknown duty. Cicins go crazy for Mist Grass, and the mages exploit that to command them. Electro and Cryo mages are documented; the Cryo mage was added in version 1.2.

65.content: Per the Hydro Cicin Archive entry, Cicins truly adore the rare and wonderful Mist Grass plant, and the Fatui have sought to exploit this to commandeer them. The Adventurer Handbook entry for the Fatui mages phrases it as Cicins going crazy for Mist Grass. Nothing further is said about how the plant is used.

66.content:
Clockwork Meka (also: Clockwork Mek, Mek, Meks, Meka, Fontaine meka, Fontainian automatons): Clockwork Meka (singular Mek) are Fontaine's machines: clockwork automatons that were built as laborers and surveyors and later modified for combat. They are powered by Arkhe, the Pneuma and Ousia energies native to Fontaine, which lets them deal elemental damage. Most are not truly intelligent.
