They are used by the Maison Gardiennage, sold to private citizens, and favored by thieves and brigands.

Each mek sits in one of two energy states, Pneuma-aligned or Ousia-aligned, and a hit from the opposite Arkhe throws it out of balance and cripples it for a time. The in-game Handbook calls them machines made possible by Fontaine's advanced engineering and its energy sources, and also excellent assistants to thieves and brigands. They first appeared as an enemy group in Version 4.0.

Nature: Meka are powered by Arkhe. A mek is either Pneuma-aligned (its clockwork glows bright white) or Ousia-aligned (dark blue) and uses different attacks depending on which. Hit it with the opposite Arkhe and it temporarily loses its energy: it is reduced to physical attacks, or cannot attack at all. Some models deal the same damage type whichever way they are aligned.

Weaker meka are thrown off by one opposing Arkhe attack, specialist models need two, and boss-class meka three. The alignment is unstable by nature, so a mek tends to settle in one state or the other. Combat-oriented meka keep a backup power system that supports low-level fighting, while utility meka lose combat ability entirely until they recover. The Arithmetic Enhancer Mek has a self-repair function that restores it after a while.

Origins: Clockwork machinery was established in Fontaine long before the present, but traditional meka ran on elastic potential energy and were regarded as novelties. About 400-500 years ago Alain Guillotin and his peers learned to produce controlled Pneuma-Ousia annihilation reactions, turning a latent environmental danger into a powerful if unstable energy source. He also invented artificial Pneumousia Blocks. His new-type meka ran on a kinetic core using this technology, and were far more efficient and structurally tougher than the older designs, which could not withstand the energy.

Models: Normal meks (low health): Area Alert, Arithmetic Enhancer, Geological Survey, Nimble Harvester, Recon Log, Underwater Patrol and Underwater Survey. Specialist meks (tougher): Annihilation Specialist, Assault Specialist, Deepwater Assault, Construction Specialist and Suppression Specialist. Boss-class machines include the Icewind Suite and the Prototype Cal. Breguet. Geological Survey Meks can be set to detect specific minerals, which makes them popular with Treasure Hoarders.

Society: Meka are used mainly by the Maison Gardiennage, but citizens may buy them for personal use. By law each purchase must be registered and recorded. People get around this, for example by filing off serial numbers, and there is a black market in which old military models fetch high prices. Parts and whole models have been smuggled out of Fontaine, though there are also legitimate sales abroad.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): ordinary meka are tools. They follow their programming and do not converse, with the rare exceptions above. In Fontaine a mek is a normal sight, a harvester in the field or a patrol unit on a quay, and not a menace. Hostile ones are typically owned or abused by thieves, or are military and security models.

67.comment: Clockwork Meka: Pneuma and Ousia alignment
67.content: Meka run on Arkhe energy: bright white clockwork marks Pneuma, dark blue marks Ousia. Opposite Arkhe overloads the balance and temporarily disables part or all of the mek. Pneumousia Blocks can power a mek briefly; its Repeaters normally refine ambient pneumousia.

68.content: A Recon Log Mek made by Alain Guillotin; the wiki says it was originally built to assist his sister Mary-Ann during her work with the Marechaussee Phantom. It was badly damaged in a fight with the Narzissenkreuz Ordo in Elynas. It is the standout example of a mek with real learning and autonomy.

69.comment: Clockwork Meka: Alain Guillotin and the first meka
69.content: The inventor behind modern meka, around 400-500 years ago. He created artificial Pneumousia Blocks and the kinetic core. See his own entry for his life.

70.content:
Consecrated Beast (also: Consecrated Beasts, Consecrated Fanged Beast, Consecrated Flying Serpent, Consecrated Horned Crocodile, Consecrated Red Vulture, Consecrated Scorpion, Phagocytic Form): Consecrated Beasts are wild animals that fed on the remains of gods or similarly powerful beings and were warped by them. They grew huge and strong, sprouted bone-like growths they cannot shed, and now fight with elemental attacks. They are elite enemies, found mostly in Sumeru and rarely in Inazuma and Fontaine. Five kinds are known: fanged beast (Dendro), flying serpent (Anemo), horned crocodile (Hydro), red vulture (Pyro) and scorpion (Electro).

The Adventurer Handbook calls them lifeforms twisted by eating some great being. Surviving the change is rare and painful. They first appeared in Version 3.4.

Nature: Ordinary animals, not a separate species: a predator, a reptile, a scavenger bird or an arthropod that ate the corpse of a far greater being and lived. They could not fully digest it, so the remains fused with their bodies into a bony shell.

Archive texts stress the cost. Most beasts that absorbed such power were killed by it; only a few evolved new forms. The devoured beings often have an almost immortal consciousness that cannot be silenced, and the power and will the beasts take in drives them toward more violence and carrion. The shell resembles a certain smelting material from Inazuma in composition.

Species: - Consecrated Fanged Beast (Dendro, 3.6): a predator with claws, a tail blade and vine attacks.
- Consecrated Flying Serpent (Anemo, 3.4): a flying reptile that fires projectiles and creates vacuum fields.
- Consecrated Horned Crocodile (Hydro, 3.6): a reptile that fires water blades and burrows to ambush.
- Consecrated Red Vulture (Pyro, 3.4): a scavenging bird that bombs from the air.
- Consecrated Scorpion (Electro, 3.4): a burrowing arthropod with claws, a stinger and tail spikes.

Abilities and limits: Aggressive, high-damage attacks of their own element. When they spot an intruder they enter a Phagocytic Form, a heavily armoured state that resists all elements, their own most of all. Periodically after a special attack they drop the form and release a Phagocytic Energy Block.

Distribution: Mostly Sumeru. Outside Sumeru, the wiki lists three: a Red Vulture and a Horned Crocodile on Elynas in Fontaine, and a Scorpion on Yashiori Island in Inazuma. The Fanged Beast has only one overworld spawn, at the mouth of Tunigi Hollow, and it appears only after the world quest The Hymn of Tir Yazad (Part 2).

Relations: They are wildlife, not Abyss creatures, though the wiki's Elynas page suggests the Fontaine ones may owe their mutation to abyssal power in his remains. They have no known leaders, society or ties to Ruin Machines, and are hostile to anyone who comes near.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): treat them as dangerous, animal-minded predators, not talking monsters. Do not give them speech, plans or loyalty. A scene near a god's remains or ruin can hint at one; the shell trophies are what adventurers take.

71.content: The state a Consecrated Beast enters as soon as it fights. The Archive tutorial says it is a powerful form, and that some attacks unleash Phagocytic Energy Blocks; destroying a block with the matching element absorbs its power, which can be released against the beast for heavy damage and a brief paralysis. In game terms it raises the beast's resistances; the lore meaning of the term is not explained beyond the devouring of a greater being.

72.content: The three enhancement materials dropped by the beasts, in rising quality. Their descriptions speak of a ruinous calamity, of beasts that gnaw at fallen gods only to share their end, and of ancient script on the pallid Marked Shell. A Marked Shell is crafted from three Sturdy Shells, and a Sturdy Shell from three Desiccated Shells.

73.content:
Domain Keeper (also: Domain Keepers, Segment-Domain Keeper, Segment-Domain Keepers, Pillar Hall guardian): Domain Keepers are elite enemies of the automaton family, shadow constructs that guard the Temple of Space, the Pillar Hall floating above Windrest Peak in Mondstadt. They arrived with the Temple of Space in Version 6.5 (Luna VI). They fight in Geo with materialised swords and can briefly take on the element they are struck with.

Their Archive text calls them guardians born from the overflow of a mighty primordial being, entrusted with "eyes" yet able only to extol the ideal forms of an unseen perfect world. Because they cannot grasp the complex phenomenal world they are not counted among the angels.

Nature: In the Archive they are shadow constructs "born of a flow" from the primordial being, the Heavenly Principles, and they stand guard over the Pillar Hall of the heavens. They are not living animals or angels.

The Archive observes a built-in contradiction: although given eyes as guardians, they can only praise the "Ideal Forms" of the noumenal world and cannot behold the phenomenal one. It leaves open whether this reflects their creator's rational design or her failure to grasp the intent of the being above her. A loading-screen tip notes the guards' differing appearances suggest differing roles.

Abilities and limits: Fights with Geo: hand and wing strikes, plus a sword that appears in its hand for spinning slashes, lunges and thrown blades. Its signature Deluded Eye state monitors Pyro, Hydro, Electro and Cryo hits; after enough hits of one element it transforms into that element with an immutable aura and strong resistance, then ends in a heavy ground slam.

Game mechanics (not narrative lore): it tracks all four elements at once, shows the leading one on a Fury bar, and transforms after three hits of the same element. If it does not transform it makes one slash and returns to normal. After four attacks in a transformed state it slams the ground in an area strike of that element and reverts.

Relations: Created by Asmoday and tied to the Watchers Nihilita and Melanta. Nihilita, called the Open-Eyed, opened his eye after Asmoday vanished and fell from the Temple to Windrest Peak, while Melanta stayed in the Cage of Suchness upholding the old rules. Which side individual Keepers favour is not stated; they behave as guardians of the status quo.

Scene use: Use Keepers as sentinel enemies in the still, windless halls of the Temple of Space. They do not speak. They respond to elemental provocation by briefly mirroring it. They should not be written as sapient, hostile to the Traveler by malice, or as the same being as the Open-Eyed.

Status as of 7.1: Introduced in Version 6.5 (Luna VI) together with the Temple of Space, which is entered after the world quest The Wind Has Ceased. It is a permanent enemy in that area. No Domain Keeper appears in the Nod-Krai or Snezhnaya content or in Versions 7.0-7.1 as far as research found.

74.content:
Domovoy (also: Domovoi, household fae, Grand Duke of the Domovoy): The Domovoy, "household fae", are one of the six common kinds of Snowland Fae. They are short, very long-lived people native to Snezhnaya. They were traditionally ruled by a Grand Duke of the Domovoy. The Fifth Harbinger Pulcinella (Mirko Radovidovich Veleshek) is a Domovoy, as were the late Grand Duke Alvis and Izmaylov, the president of the Royal Energy Commission.

Like all fae they were made by Hyperborean artisans and later joined the Belyi Tsar's realm; under the Tsaritsa many entered the human world as officials, craftsmen and politicians.

Nature: Domovoy are known for their small stature. They count among the six common kinds of Snowland Fae, alongside Vila, Leshy, Volkodlak, Snegovik and Jack Frost. Their name is the Russian word for a house spirit.

Artifact text says they can supposedly live indefinitely, but they still age and suffer for it: one lore piece shows an old Domovoy white-haired and frail after centuries. Pulcinella is considered tall for his people, roughly a head above other Domovoy. Like other fae they use elemental power without a Vision, and they share the cold-loving habits of their kin.

Society: The kind was traditionally led by a Grand Duke of the Domovoy. Alvis held that title from before the Belyi Tsar unified Snezhnaya. He ruled Kitezhgrad and its mining trade until the Cataclysm destroyed the city about 500 years ago, then founded Novokitezhgrad. The title has since lost its old power, since fae lost their monopoly on rank under the Tsaritsa, and Domovoy now work as officials, engineers and politicians.

Abilities and limits: Canon gives no kind-wide combat traits for the Domovoy. Individuals are known for craft and statecraft rather than martial display: Alvis monopolised mining, Izmaylov forged weapons and ran the Energy Commission, and Pulcinella is a career politician.

Relations: The Domovoy were among the fae who accepted the Belyi Tsar. Alvis was a staunch ally even before the unification and taught Aksinya, though he disliked her at first. After the Tsar's death the Domovoy adapted to the Tsaritsa's rule, and Pulcinella serves her directly. They sit beside the other fae kinds as part of the old fae aristocracy of the Pale Star Court.

Individuals: Known Domovoy include Pulcinella (Fifth Harbinger), the late Grand Duke Alvis, and Izmaylov (Energy Commission president). Their own entries carry the detail.

75.content: Alvis was Grand Duke of the Domovoy from before the Belyi Tsar unified Snezhnaya and Lord of Kitezhgrad until the Cataclysm, after which he founded Novokitezhgrad. He helped the Tsar defeat the Volkodlak king Miscislav's allies, mentored the human girl Aksinya, and later joined the betrayal that sent her into the Shadow Realm. He died in the 7.0 world quests (the wiki records Aksinya as his killer). See his own entry.

76.content: Pulcinella is a Domovoy about whom canon says he chose to enter the human world and never claimed to love humanity, only that it was a farsighted decision. He is Mayor of Snezhnograd and Fifth Harbinger. See his own entry.

77.content:
Dragon (also: Dragons, dragonkind, dragon race, dragons of Teyvat): Dragons are enormous elemental beings of the Light Realm and the original masters of Teyvat. The old world was ruled by the Dragon King Nibelung and the Seven Sovereigns, one elemental dragon per element, until the Heavenly Principles arrived, defeated them, took part of their Authorities and remade the world for humanity. Today most dragonkind survives as vishaps, Natlan's saurians and a few great individuals such as Dvalin (Anemo), Azhdaha (Geo), Apep (Dendro) and Neuvillette (Hydro).

Ancient gods and dragons have "never seen eye to eye", and many dragons long resented gods and humans as usurpers. The Archons' powers rest partly on Authority taken from the Sovereigns, so a living Sovereign cannot regain full power while the matching Archon's throne stands.

Nature: Dragons are born from the elements and live far longer than mortals or even gods. They usually grow stronger with age, and their size tracks their strength: Azhdaha at full power was as large as a mountain range. Their bodies reflect their element, like Azhdaha's stony hide or Dvalin's sleek wind-dragon shape.

Some are four-legged, some serpentine, some winged, some wingless. Dragons belong to the Light Realm, Teyvat's original form of energy, and thrive on "Holy Soil", land rich in primordial elemental power that is hostile to human farming. They are not immune to erosion and remain bound by many of the Heavenly Principles' rules, though canon says some fully fledged dragons (Neuvillette, Natlan's Thirteen Sovereign Lords) stand outside rules such as destiny. Vishaps and elemental dragons are especially vulnerable to the darkness of the Void Realm (the Abyss).

Society: In the old world dragons were the dominant race, led by Nibelung and the Seven Sovereigns, each of whom ruled a portion of the world attuned to their element. Vishaps follow and obey their Sovereign as the peak of their kind.

History: Long ago the Heavenly Principles came to Teyvat, defeated the Seven Sovereigns with the help of the Four Shades and remade the world for humanity. Dragons who refused to submit, such as the Bathysmal Vishaps, fled into the deep sea.

Later, Nibelung returned bearing the power of the Abyss. The surviving Sovereigns woke and joined him in a great war of vengeance (the war of funerary flame), which nearly destroyed the world. The dragons lost; the Heavenly Principles cast down Celestial Nails to mend and suppress the land, turning Apep's forests into desert. Weakened, the Heavenly Principles then used part of the Sovereigns' Authorities to make the Gnoses and the Archons' divine thrones, which began the Archon War.

Abilities and limits: A great dragon commands its element on a national scale and can rival an Archon: Azhdaha, Dvalin and Durin are all described in such terms. Lesser dragons can be killed by strong Vision or Delusion users.

A Sovereign's dragonhood is bound up with its Authority. Neuvillette only gained absolute control of Hydro, and the power to declare Fontaine's people truly human, after Focalors destroyed the Hydro Archon's throne in 4.2. Dragons draw on ley lines; Azhdaha planned to absorb the world's ley-line energy, and Dvalin's rampage threw Mondstadt's elemental flow into disorder.

Relations: Most dragons and the gods have been enemies since the Heavenly Principles' conquest, though exceptions exist: Dvalin is Mondstadt's protector, and Azhdaha was once Morax's friend.

Canon notes that most reborn dragons no longer carry the old hatred of gods and humans. Apep herself remains distrustful but chose to watch humanity rather than destroy it after Nahida and the Traveler saved her in 3.6. In Natlan, saurians live as equal companions of the human tribes.

Individuals: - Nibelung: the Dragon King, killed by the Heavenly Principles (own entry).
- Living Sovereigns: Dvalin (Anemo), Azhdaha (Geo, sealed), Apep (Dendro), Neuvillette (Hydro, in human form).

- Dead Sovereigns: the original Anemo and Hydro dragons, Xiuhcoatl (Pyro) and the Cryo Dragon. No Electro Sovereign has been named.
- Others: Durin, Rhinedottir's artificial abyssal dragon; Ajaw, a surviving Sovereign Lord of Natlan bound to Kinich; the Fell Dragon Prince Scylla of Fontaine; Kukulkan, Xiuhcoatl's brother.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1: Dvalin is Mondstadt's ally, Azhdaha is resealed, Apep watches over Sumeru's desert, Neuvillette holds the restored Hydro Authority as Iudex of Fontaine, and Natlan's dragons survive as saurians.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): great dragons are rare, ancient and politically significant; an ordinary Teyvat resident knows vishaps as dangerous beasts and the Sovereigns only as legends. Wild vishaps should be dangerous animals, not conversational characters. Saurians in Natlan are everyday companions.

78.comment: Dragon: Holy Soil and the dragons' fall
78.content: Holy Soil is land saturated with primordial elemental power. Dragons thrive on it; humans cannot farm it. Kukulkan says the Heavenly Principles treated Natlan's phlogiston-rich soil as Holy Soil and removed it, forcing the dragons there to devolve into saurians. Watatsumi Island's bleaching soil is another case, held back by the Watatsumi Goryou Matsuri. In Snezhnaya, the Cryo Dragon's corpse turned the land into Holy Soil of primordial ice.

79.content: "Elemental dragon" in canon refers to the Seven Sovereigns, the mightiest dragons, each holding one element's Authority. The Heavenly Principles stole part of these Authorities and later placed them in the Archons' divine thrones, so a living Sovereign stays incomplete until its Archon dies and the throne is destroyed. This happened for Hydro in Fontaine (4.2). A Sovereign can be reborn, normally from a pure vishap lineage; the impure Bathysmal Vishaps forced the Hydro Sovereign to be reborn in human form as Neuvillette.

80.content:
Elemental Lifeforms (also: Elemental Lifeform, elemental life form, elemental life forms, elemental lifeform): Elemental Lifeforms are creatures made of condensed elemental energy rather than flesh. Each is tied to a single element, carries that element as part of its body, and cannot be harmed by it. The family includes slimes (small, common and found everywhere), specters (floating sprites that can fly into a rage), hypostases (ultra-dense, cube-shelled constructs at the highest level of elemental purity), the Tainted Hydro Phantasms that took the place of the Oceanids in Fontaine's waters, and the Frostnight Scions, born of the Frost Moon's blessings in Nod-Krai.

Nature: Elemental Lifeforms are made purely of one element and are immune to it. Many keep that element applied to themselves at all times, so reactions with other elements still work on them. Their elemental energy is also their body: slimes are condensed elemental energy, with the type of energy fixing the element and the concentration fixing the size. An in-world book (Breeze Amidst the Forest, vol. I) observes that when life arises from the elements it either descends and becomes a slime or ascends and becomes a crystalfly. The loading-screen line calls slimes lowly life forms of minimal intelligence that become a bigger problem if ignored.

Higher forms are more structured: hypostases are said to have abandoned their former appearance and biological structure entirely, becoming compact, heavy structures with a shell of concentrated element around a reactive core.

Abilities and limits: Game mechanics, for reference (gameplay, not lore): specters have a Fury meter that fills from heavy hits and turns them enraged and larger, and they charge up and explode when defeated; hypostases are invulnerable while their cube shell surrounds them and can be hurt only when the diamond core is exposed, usually after an attack, and at low health they enter a revival phase in which they spawn elemental objects that must be dealt with in time; Tainted Hydro Phantasms periodically enrage, grow larger, and then ignore Frozen; Frostnight Scions periodically enter a Gloomveiled state in which they swap immunity for strong resistance and must be forced out of it with their own element or Lunar reaction damage.

Types: - Slimes: common enemies found all over Teyvat in Anemo, Cryo, Dendro, Electro, Geo, Hydro and Pyro forms, small and large. See their own entry.
- Specters: common enemies in Inazuma, Enkanomiya and Sumeru, first appearing in version 2.1. On Watatsumi Island they are considered pests; Kokomi has a Specter Eco-Management group (mentioned in a limited-time event quest).
- Hypostases: normal bosses at the highest elemental purity. All seven elements exist; the last, Dendro, arrived in version 3.2. They are found in Mondstadt, Liyue, Inazuma and Sumeru.
- Tainted Hydro Phantasms: elite enemies of Fontaine and Liyue, permanently Hydro, introduced in 4.0.
- Frostnight Scions: elite enemies of Nod-Krai in seven elemental forms, introduced in 6.0; the boss Frostnight Herra followed in 6.1.

Relations: Hilichurls exploit lifeforms: grenadiers dig up and throw slimes; some mitachurls infuse axes with Pyro or Electro slimes or build wooden shields from Dendro slimes; rogues ride Anemo slimes or fling Hydro ones; Large Anemo Slimes serve as cargo balloons. Slimes are drawn to strong elemental sources, and Mist Flower extract works as "Elemental Bait". The Sumeru Akademiya leads research on hypostases, but because of their danger little is known beyond scientific names and code names.

81.content: In the Adventurer Handbook each hypostasis carries a codename taken from a letter of the Hebrew alphabet: Electro is Aleph, Anemo is Beth, Geo is Gimel, Cryo is Daleth, Hydro is He, Dendro is Zayin and Pyro is Ayin. The sixth letter is skipped and Ayin used instead. Descriptions open with lines such as the Dendro Hypostasis's "Code Name: Zayin".

82.comment: Elemental Lifeforms: Mystical Beasts versus Elemental Lifeforms
82.content: Mystical beasts are creatures strongly shaped by an element and generally more resistant to the element they represent, but they are not made of pure elemental energy. Examples in this group include Vishaps, Fungi, Whopperflowers, Consecrated Beasts and Fontemer Aberrants. Elemental Lifeforms, by contrast, are pure elemental energy given form.

83.content: Frostnight Scions and the boss Frostnight Herra periodically withdraw into a Gloomveiled state in Nod-Krai. In it they use stronger attacks but trade elemental immunity for a high resistance, and they can be broken out of it by their corresponding element or by Lunar reaction damage. The Fury meter shown in this state is a gameplay readout, not a lore concept.

key: Searing Tide Pulsing Beneath the Mountains
Lone Suzerain of Land and Sea
84.content:
Emperor of Fire and Iron (also: Searing Tide Pulsing Beneath the Mountains, Lone Suzerain of Land and Sea, Armored Crablord, Tyrant of Fire and Iron): The Emperor of Fire and Iron is a colossal Armored Crab that lives in a cavern beneath a lake in Fontaine's Belleau Region. It is an ancient ruler of the Fontemer Aberrants, the strange sea creatures of Fontaine, and wears twin horns that burn with Pyro. It does not hunt travellers; it is an enormous, armoured creature that fights when disturbed. Sailors tell tales about it.

The in-game Archive calls it one of two sovereigns who once stood at the apex of the aberrant species, and its event panel titles it the "Lone Suzerain of Land and Sea". It is a repeatable world boss, and the crab's size, age and armour are the point of the entry: a creature that simply never stopped growing.

Nature: An Armored Crab (the small shell-borrowing crabs found across Fontaine) that grew far beyond its kin. The Adventurer Handbook calls it an ancient ruler of the Fontemer Aberrants, said to have witnessed Fontaine's seas before the first diluvian period. The tutorial calls it an Armored Crablord that has outlived and outgrown almost every other aberrant.

Ordinary Armored Crabs are gentle: they spend their lives looking for shells that fit as they grow, and the Archive says they show little of the aggression of wild animals because their territory is only the small home on their backs. The Archive explains the Emperor as the end of that story. A crab that avoids predation and keeps hunting and eating keeps growing and seeking new shells, until it became simply too gargantuan. Its armour is its nature rather than a borrowed shell.

Its title in the world is half-joking and half in awe. The Archive says that is how people speak of it, and imagines a Teyvat emptied of humanity in which no one would be left to call it "Emperor of Fire and Iron" at all.

Abilities and limits: Heavy claw strikes, charges and leaping slams (Physical), and Pyro attacks from the horns: volleys of fireballs that scorch the ground, trails of explosions and a large explosion at the arena centre. While its horns are intact it uses its strongest attacks.

Breaking the horns with elemental reactions paralyses it for a period. After they are destroyed it regenerates them by burrowing and resurfacing. The horns are low and exposed to melee during certain big attacks (for example the leaping slam and the central explosion).

Relations: Among the aberrants it belongs to the same group as the Armored Crab and the Sternshield Crab. The Archive records one human encounter: before the first diluvian period, a massive Armored Crab attacked a ship and was driven back into the depths by Basil Elton, who had not yet been reinstated as a naval commander. The text says "a massive Armored Crab", so whether that was this very creature is not stated.

Status as of 7.1: Alive and unchanged as of 7.1: it remains in its cavern as a repeatable boss. I found no mention of it in 6.x (Nod-Krai) or 7.0-7.1 (Snezhnaya) story content.

A different version, the Tyrant of Fire and Iron ("Indomitable Lord"), appeared only in the limited-time event On the Trail of Behemoths (5.3, January 2025). It is a variant for that event, not a separate canonical creature.

85.comment: Emperor of Fire and Iron: Tyrant of Fire and Iron
85.content: The Tyrant of Fire and Iron, titled "Indomitable Lord", is an event-exclusive variant of the Emperor of Fire and Iron met in the 5.3 limited-time challenge event On the Trail of Behemoths (14-27 January 2025). It reuses the Emperor's body and Pyro horns with event-specific mechanics, and the event's challenges were run through an NPC named Helka. Treat it as a gameplay variant, not as a second giant crab in the world.

86.comment: Emperor of Fire and Iron: Armored Crablord
86.content: Armored Crabs are shell-borrowing crabs found throughout Fontaine; the Archive notes a popular Fontaine storybook about one crab's search for a shell that fit, which touched adults deeply. Sternshield Crabs are the adult form that carry a Pyro aura on land. The Emperor is described as an Armored Crablord that has outlived and surpassed almost all other Fontemer Aberrants.

key: Fae with Crystals Growing on the Skin
87.content:
Fae of Crystalline Flesh (also: Fae with Crystals Growing on the Skin, hostile Snowland Fae, crystal-skinned fae): "Fae of Crystalline Flesh" is the game's label for the Snowland Fae that fight the Traveler in Snezhnaya. The group covers Snegovik (the ice-mage Glaciomancers, the ice-knight Glacial Wardens and the boss Guardian Blade of Drifting Snow), winged Vila (Halberd-Knight and Soarer Knight), the wolf-like Volkodlak brutes and the tree-like Wildwood Leshies. The Handbook says the crystals on their bodies formed from a surge of energy as they were being crafted into living beings.

The label is a game category, not a name the fae use for themselves. Most of these fae are curious rather than aggressive at first and leave travellers alone until provoked; Leshies are the exception. The people behind them, with their history, are covered under Snowland Fae.

Nature: Hostile members of the Snowland Fae, artificial peoples made long ago in Hyperborea and later gathered under the Belyi Tsar. Crystalline growths mark their bodies.

The group's Handbook text ties the crystals on these fae to volatile energy that surfaced as they were being made; Snegovik bear blue crystalline markings, Vila a green-tipped ear. The Snegovik appear as pale humanoids with ice-blue eyes; the male Snegovik are roughly twice human height. Vila have insect-like wings and pointed ears. Volkodlak, per the Handbook, are the most populous race of fae in Snezhnaya, a family of varied creatures. Leshies are tree-fae that may be the longest-lived of all.

Society: They are ordinary Snezhnayan fae who happen to be met as enemies, often as soldiers, guards or wilderness dwellers. Vila were among the clans that followed the Belyi Tsar from the start of his unification campaign; most of the Druzhna, his personal guard, were Vila. Snegovik are led by the Snegurochka princess, with the Great Snegurochka of the past, Yalyane Morevna, remembered as a figure of "crimson infamy". Leshies keep to forests and mountain wilds and are seldom seen near towns.

Abilities and limits: Snegovik use ice: Glaciomancers cast frost spikes and shelter in ice coffins; Glacial Wardens forge ice maces and shards. Winged Vila fight with Anemo-aligned halberds, swords and short flights. Volkodlak brutes fight with weapons and can imbue strikes with Dendro, Electro or Pyro (green, purple and red markings in the Raider's case); high-tier ones lean on elemental power, including the Voywolf Hunter and Fanged Zealot. Wildwood Leshies are Geo-aligned and root themselves to recover.

Individuals: Guardian Blade of Drifting Snow, boss title "Outcast Ice Shadow" (7.1): an ancient Snegovik held in high esteem who once served the Great Snegurochka and was charged with protecting the Snegovik clan for life; seven were given the duty, and only she remains. Every succession of the Snegovik sovereign must therefore happen under her watch. After the current Snegurochka princess took power she left the clan manor in the mountains, perhaps over differing ideals, and she is fought on Fellfrost Peak.

Relations: They are the hostile face of the Snowland Fae, met by the Traveler as enemies in the Snezhnayan wilds. The sources read give no shared cause behind their hostility; the Guardian Blade has left her clan's manor, perhaps over differing ideals. The Vila and Chimeric Winged Elephants cooperated in the Belyi Tsar's war. The Snegovik have a conflicted relationship with humans, as their Archive stories of love and tragedy suggest.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 these fae wander Snezhnaya, and the Guardian Blade (new in 7.1) has left her clan's manor.

The group first appeared in 7.0; only the Guardian Blade of Drifting Snow was added in 7.1. No canon event wipes them out or reunites them.

88.comment: Fae of Crystalline Flesh: Snegovik enemies
88.content: Female Snegovik, called Snegurochka, are born as ice mages: the Glaciomancers. Male Snegovik are born as ice knights who forge weapons from snow, like the Glacial Warden. Archive text says Snegovik souls were first made incomplete and become whole only through love of a human, which may be why so many love stories between Snegovik and humans end sadly; the Eye of Graeae treats that as a research perspective, not fact.

89.comment: Fae of Crystalline Flesh: Vila knights
89.content: Winged Vila warriors. The Soarer Knight's Archive entry says Vila followed the Belyi Tsar from the beginning of his unification campaign, scouted enemy formations by brief flight, and made up most of the Druzhna guard. The Halberd-Knight's entry recalls the unrest among the Vila during the Tsaritsa's first century.

90.comment: Fae of Crystalline Flesh: Volkodlak brutes
90.content: Brutes come in low and high tiers: Basher, Lobber, Raider and Sharpshooter are low-tier; Channel Contact, Fanged Zealot, Leomastiff Guard, Long-Eared Striker and Voywolf Hunter are high-tier. The Handbook says they may have been created to answer what makes a human human. The Raider's Archive entry describes small, agile Volkodlak with senses keener than a human's.

91.comment: Fae of Crystalline Flesh: Wildwood Leshies
91.content: Reclusive tree-fae that live deep in forests and mountains. Archive text says Leshies have only fragmentary sentience and cannot speak, yet records show they were made late, after Hyperborea's artisans had nearly mastered authority over life. They may be the longest-lived fae, and few outsiders have seen one live a full life.

92.comment: Fae of Crystalline Flesh: Guardian Blade of Drifting Snow
92.content: An ancient Snegovik swordswoman who left the House of Hesperides' manor after the current princess took power. She is the last of seven guardians sworn to protect the clan in the age of the Great Snegurochka, and every succession must occur under her eye.

93.content:
Fisher of Hidden Depths (also: Fishers of Hidden Depths, Hidden Depths Fisher, Deepdark Fisher): Fishers of Hidden Depths are Electro-aligned elite creatures of the Abyss family, first seen in Version 6.3 in the northern reaches of Nod-Krai. They are described as Abyssal creatures that slip through rifts from beyond this world. They come in groups, and their linked Deepdark Shields make a swarm hard to break unless the shield is shattered.

The in-game Archive describes them as deathless wanderers of the silent cosmic void, scaled rather than feathered, which use hooked beaks to draw biomass from world to world. The Adventure Handbook gives only the shorter line about slipping through rifts in the hidden depths.

Nature: The Archive text compares them to an old philosopher's definition of humans as "featherless bipeds": scaled instead of feathered, these outsiders collect biomass with hooked beaks and travel between worlds without dying. The text uses this to suggest, wryly, that they might fit the same simplistic definition of "human". It does not say they are people, nor where they come from. An item they leave behind, the Hooked Beak of the Deep Shadow, is described as a birdlike hooked beak used by predators from beyond this world to store seized biomass.

Society: Fishers are almost always met in groups. In the tutorial's words, their connections to one another form Deepdark Shields when several are present, and breaking one Fisher's shield shatters the whole swarm's shields at once and gathers the swarm around the Fisher whose shield broke. A lone survivor does not raise a shield.

Abilities and limits: Element: Electro. On entering a fight a Fisher roars and raises a Deepdark Shield that protects it and strengthens its attacks. Only elemental damage harms the shield, and Lunar reactions are especially effective against it. Kuuvahki currents, the pure non-polar kuuvahki waves released in northern Nod-Krai by plants and creatures such as Glimmerfruit, Mandragora, Spirebloom and Slothsheep, can also damage it; weak currents do little and strong ones damage it considerably.

Relations: The boss Lord of the Hidden Depths: Whisperer of Nightmares, who lurks at Ashveil Peak, summons four Fishers in its Deepdark Strike attack, and the Fishers are consumed by the boss's attack if left alive. Its Archive text uses similar wording about creatures that creep through rifts, but no text states a formal link beyond the shared name and mechanics.

Individuals: No individual Fisher is named in canon.

Status as of 7.1: As of Version 7.1 they remain regular elite enemies of northern Nod-Krai (Voidsea Outlook, Wavechaser Plain and Ashveil Peak are the northern areas where Abyssal contamination and kuuvahki currents are found), and no new information about them appeared in 6.x after their debut or in 7.0-7.1.

94.comment: Fisher of Hidden Depths: Fisher of Hidden Depths
94.content: Fishers of Hidden Depths are Electro Abyssal creatures from beyond the world that hunt in swarms in northern Nod-Krai. Their linked Deepdark Shields break together when one is broken, especially under Lunar reactions or strong kuuvahki currents.

95.content:
Fontemer Aberrant (also: Fontemer Aberrants, Fontemer Aberrant Material, Fontaine sea creatures): Fontemer Aberrants are Fontaine's native aquatic beasts: crabs, octopuses, jellyfish, seahorses, stingrays, sea hares and a whale-like mammal called the Blubberbeast. They live in the waters of Fontaine and along its shores, and they are not recorded anywhere else in Teyvat. Most fight by firing Hydro projectiles or pouncing. They are animals, not a kingdom: the Adventurer Handbook insists they have no courts, words or aristocracy.

The group name appears in the Adventurer Handbook as "Fontemer Aberrant". The Handbook says that, perhaps because of environmental requirements, the creatures can seemingly only be found in Fontaine, and it guesses that they developed from aquatic animals that once differed little from sea life elsewhere in Teyvat. Younger, smaller animals are usually tolerant of travelers; adults and the named "Local Legend" individuals are not.

Nature: Fontemer Aberrants are ordinary animals as canon describes them, not spirits or people. Most hunt for food and are unaggressive otherwise. Even the largest remain simple creatures that grew powerful by surviving.

Adventurer Handbook texts describe individual kinds this way. The Armored Crab lives in a borrowed shell and has no real territory beyond that shell on its back. Angelic Sea Hares, Hat Jellyfish, Bubbly Seahorses and similar small kinds hunt by firing watery projectiles. The Ball Octopus's water jets are strong enough to endanger careless tourist divers, which is one reason diving gear is thick. The Blubberbeast is a mammal that communicates with companions through melodious sounds; the Handbook notes that sound travels well in water and that a Research Institute scholar once took inspiration from this for an image-to-data transmission device that never spread beyond the Institute. The Hunter's Ray is a stingray that releases blades of water.

Abilities and limits: Hydro projectiles and jets are the common attack: bubbles, water guns, water blades. Crabs and some adults are tougher and hit harder. Giants carry an elemental ward that must be broken before they can be hurt properly.

Named abilities from the Archive sources: Bubble Shot (Angelic Sea Hare), Water Gun and Pounce (Ball Octopus), Bubble Spit (Bubbly Seahorse). Adults gain elemental flavors, such as Electro and Hydro for the Bubbler Seahorse, Cryo for the Cherubic Sea Hare and Pyro for the Sternshield Crab. These are gameplay data and should be used only as colour in a scene.

Society: There is no society. The Handbook calls Fontemer Aberrants simple aquatic animals with no courts, kingdoms or words, and says tales to the contrary are the romantic imagination of people unwilling to accept a bland world.

Fontainians still tell stories about them. A children's-style storybook about an Armored Crab seeking a fitting shell was, per the Handbook, very popular in Fontaine for a time and moved adults too. There is also a small, sparse fan community: Bubbly Seahorses are said to have many fans, and the text compares the more standoffish enthusiasts to some clockwork meka hobbyists.

Relations: People in Fontaine regard them as wildlife to avoid or admire. They are also associated with Fontaine's local waters and, in speculation only, with the Primordial Sea.

A Handbook text about the Emperor of Fire and Iron says it fought machines, other Aberrants and curious hunters alike, and that a giant Armored Crab once attacked a ship before being driven back into the depths by Basil Elton, then not yet reinstated as a naval commander. That attack is dated to before the first diluvian period. The same entry imagines a future empty of people in which the Emperor wears the Palais Mermonia like a coat of white stone, which is a thought experiment, not a prediction.

Individuals: The two famous individuals are the Emperor of Fire and Iron, a giant Armored Crab, and the Millennial Pearl Seahorse, a violet-lit ancient seahorse. Both live in caverns.

The Emperor of Fire and Iron (title "Searing Tide Pulsing Beneath the Mountains") is found in the Belleau Region and is said to have seen Fontaine's seas before the first diluvian period. Its drop, Emperor's Resolution, is its war-hammer claw. The Millennial Pearl Seahorse ("Nameless Lord of the Great Lake"), described as having a phantasmal beauty and a temper fiercer than a thunderstorm, lives in the Liffey Region; its drop is the Fontemer Unihorn. The Handbook describes the pair as the two sovereigns at the apex of the Aberrants and notes the "Pearl Seahorse" versus "Emperor" naming reflects the seahorse's slender elegance versus the crab's heavy bulk.

Status as of 7.1: As of Version 7.1 the species is unchanged. Nothing found shows a new Fontemer Aberrant in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 or any appearance outside Fontaine.

96.content: Xenochromatic Creatures are Fontemer Aberrants that the Traveler can borrow abilities from while diving in Fontaine to solve underwater puzzles. They do not attack and cannot be harmed. Five kinds are documented: Armored Crab, Hunter's Ray, Blubberbeast, Jellyfish and Ball Octopus. Borrowed powers last until the diver leaves the water entirely. The Hunter's Ray text notes a rumor that these are really ocean spirits that bless those accepted by, or able to control, the Fontemer, then dismisses it as groundless speculation from people without a grounding in natural philosophy.

97.content: Local Legends are named, unusually strong individual Fontemer Aberrants found in particular spots of Fontaine; unlike ordinary animals they attack on sight. The Archive notes these: the Blubberbeasts Fading Veteran (Elton Trench) and Dobharcu, Lord of the Hidden (Chemin de L'Espoir); the Hat Jellyfish Chassanion (under the Sealed Ruined Tower, later inside the Tower of Ipsissimus after the quest In the Wake of Narcissus) and Mageblade Corrouge (Roots of Erinnyes, fightable only after The Wild Fairy of Erinnyes); the Hunter's Rays Angelica and Medoro (the Fairy Knight Twins, Salacia Plain) and Cortana and Murgleis (Swords of the Gorge, Thalatta Submarine Canyon); the Cherubic Sea Hare Luachra the Brilliant (north-west Liffey Region); and the Sternshield Crabs Iron Viscount (Beryl Region) and Ocean Circuit Judge (Elynas).

98.comment: Fontemer Aberrant: Event variants of the sovereigns
98.content: Two boss variants appear only in limited-time events: the Tyrant of Fire and Iron, called "Indomitable Lord" in the On the Trail of Behemoths event, and the Enraged Millennial Pearl Seahorse, called "Best Ride" in the Specially-Shaped Saurian Search event. They are event enemies and are not standing wildlife.

99.content:
Frostnight Scion (also: Frostnight Scions, Icy Crystal Frostnight Scion, Blazing Brilliance Frostnight Scion, Surging Currents Frostnight Scion, Tangled Vines Frostnight Scion, Gleaming Charge Frostnight Scion, Gilded Sunshard Frostnight Scion, Veiled Cloudchaser Frostnight Scion): The Frostnight Scions are an elite enemy group of elemental lifeforms in Nod-Krai (Version 6.0, Luna I; the Hydro, Geo and Anemo kinds were added in 6.3, Luna IV). The Adventurer Handbook calls them elegant beings whose present form comes from long years of exposure to dense elemental energy. There are seven elemental kinds, one per element, plus a single boss, Frostnight Herra, who starts without a fixed element.

Far-northern prayers that still survive hold that they were born from the Frost Moon's blessings, a symbol of the pure source and the first radiance. Archive entries add that they cannot bear their pale purity being stained by the seven colours of heavenly light, so they reject any life that draws too near.

Nature: Canon describes them as elemental lifeforms, in the same family as slimes: like slimes, each kind is immune to its own element. The Archive stresses refinement more than savagery, though several kinds are called violent when provoked.

Two origin accounts sit side by side. One is elemental: the Handbook says long exposure to high concentrations of elemental energy produced their present forms. The other is devotional: the Handbook states flatly that they were born from the Frost Moon's blessings, as a symbol of the pure source and the first radiance, while the Archive entries attribute this to still-extant prayers of the far north. The Archive for the Icy Crystal kind adds that this kind is said to be closest to the original form of a Frostnight Scion.

Abilities and limits: Each kind keeps a lasting aura of its own element and is immune to it outside the Gloomveiled state. The seven kinds fight in distinct ways:
- Icy Crystal (Cryo): Cryo Aura, Swipe, Ice Ball, Stomp and a Frost Skirt attack.
- Blazing Brilliance (Pyro): Slash, Flying Slam, Stomp and a Fireball.
- Surging Currents (Hydro): Tail Swipe, Tail Slam, Stomp and a Bubble Shower.
- Tangled Vines (Dendro): Tail Swipe, Tail Strike, Stomp and a Bloomburst.
- Gleaming Charge (Electro): Tail Swipe, Tail Slam, Stomp and a Tri-Shot.
- Gilded Sunshard (Geo): Swipe, Crystal Ball, Stomp and a Crystal Hail.
- Veiled Cloudchaser (Anemo): Slash, Flying Slam, Stomp and a Dart Barrage.

(Attack names are the wiki's; the Archive text does not describe the moves.)

Gloomveiled state (game mechanic): they periodically enter it, gaining stronger attacks while losing their elemental immunity (replaced by a still-considerable resistance). A Scion is forced out of it by damage of its matching element or by Lunar reaction damage.

Relations: Their lore ties them to the Frost Moon and to Nod-Krai's old northern devotion rather than to any modern faction. The Herra's Archive text says the followers of the Frost Moon (see the Frostmoon Scions faction) regard these beasts as sacred. In play they are fought as ordinary hostile enemies.

Individuals: Frostnight Herra is the group's only named boss: a world boss on Hiisi Island, introduced in Version 6.1 (Luna II). Its in-game title is Guardian of the Holy Light. It starts without an element.

100.content: Frostnight Herra is the one boss among the Frostnight Scions, found on Hiisi Island in Nod-Krai (Version 6.1). Its name, per the wiki's etymology note, means "lord" in Finnish, Icelandic and Old Norse. Archive text calls it a proud being of the waning moonlight with iridescent wings, wielding ancient powers tamed by the Lord of the Sky, bound by an oath to the apostle of the golden city. Its attacks include sweeps, moon projectiles and a plunging strike, and in the Gloomveiled state it takes on the element that hurt it most.

101.content: Gloomveiled is the shrouded, empowered state Frostnight Scions enter periodically. In it a Scion hits harder and with extra moves, but loses its elemental immunity (keeping a high resistance). It can be forced out by its matching element or by Lunar reaction damage. The text read does not explain the shrouding in-world.

102.comment: Frostnight Scion: Frostnight Scion Origin Legends
102.content: Archive entries state that in far-northern prayers still spoken, the Scions were born from the Frost Moon's blessings and embody the pure source and the first radiance; this is why they find the taint of heavenly light's seven colours unbearable. This is presented as a prayer or legend, not as established history.

103.content:
Fungus (also: Fungi, Fungal beasts, Floating Anemo Fungus, Floating Dendro Fungus, Floating Hydro Fungus, Stretchy Anemo Fungus, Stretchy Electro Fungus, Stretchy Geo Fungus): Fungi are mushroom creatures found mainly in Sumeru and, in a few spots, in Liyue. The Adventurer Handbook calls a fungus "the congregation of overgrown and over-evolved spores." Most people treat them as monsters, though some are being tamed. They attack with every element, and Pyro or Electro changes how a fungus behaves.

Fungi count as Tri-Lakshana Creatures, so touching one with Pyro scorches it and touching it with Electro activates it. Their main boss is the Jadeplume Terrorshroom, the lord of the fungal beasts. Quests also show a gentler side: some fungi are the displaced survivors of the dragon Apep's corruption, and an ancient fungus god, Bifrons, claims to be their progenitor.

Nature: A fungus is a spore-born creature that has grown far beyond an ordinary mushroom. It keeps one element, so a given fungus may be Anemo, Cryo, Dendro, Electro, Geo, Hydro or Pyro. Most are animal-like enough to float, stretch, spin or walk.

The Handbook says the fungi infestation is rumoured to be the result of a lab accident: a certain sage hoped to use spores in medicine and underestimated how well they adapt and reproduce. The Sumeru Preview Teaser gave a milder account, calling them mushrooms that evolved stronger ability to reproduce and to protect the flora. Even so, most people see them as monsters. Fungi use elemental power, but in Homecoming Nahida explains that the ordinary kind draw it from nature instead of from within themselves.

Habitat: Fungi are common enemies across Sumeru. The Jadeplume Terrorshroom entry notes that fungi grow wherever it is damp and fertile. They do not appear in the Natlan overworld.

Two groups live in Liyue: a lone group in Yaodie Valley in Chenyu Vale, and the fungi of the Underground Waterway and the Glowing Narrows in the Chasm's Underground Mines. Small caged fungi sometimes sit in the camps of hilichurls, Treasure Hoarders or Eremites; they cannot be freed and can still be fought.

Abilities and limits: Each fungus fights with its own element: spore bursts, spinning, stretching strikes or flying charges. Pyro scorches them and Electro activates them, which changes their pace and damage.

Their fungus-specific drops are spores, pollen and dust, with nucleus materials added when one is Scorched or Activated. The Handbook warns that fungi adapt and spread quickly.

Relations: People and fungi are mostly enemies, but there are exceptions. Most people consider fungi monsters, Sumeru scholars from Amurta take an interest in them, and some people raise them.

In the limited-time event Fabulous Fungus Frenzy (3.2), a Beast Tamer Tournament in Port Ormos, contestants caught and trained fungi. In the event quest Farewell, My Shroom Buddies, Layla hopes an improved Wisdom Orb might one day let people talk to fungi directly and plans to ask an Amurta scholar, and Yae Miko says the bond between the Traveler and the fungi turned out to be companionship rather than a master-servant arrangement.

Individuals: The Jadeplume Terrorshroom, the lord of fungal beasts in Sumeru. Bifrons, the Sage-Lord of Fungi in the Natlan questline. Xamaran, a giant glowing mushroom in the Chasm that can speak.

The Jadeplume Terrorshroom, a normal boss (3.0) in Vissudha Field, is a large bird-like fungal beast, titled in game as the Deepwood Shroomlord. The Archive says it hunts actively and is more intelligent than a real animal; its tail plumage resembles that of the ancient sacred beast the Spantamad school reveres, so the two may once have lived together.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): treat wild fungi as animal-like and territorial rather than speaking. A speaking fungus is a special case: only Xamaran, the Homecoming survivors and Bifrons talk in the quests above. Keep their cartoonish, puffing look, and let Pyro and Electro visibly change their mood.

104.content: Bifrons is an ancient fungus god, titled the Sage-Lord of Fungi, who appears in the Tribal Chronicles chapter Mushroom Realm Mystery (5.5). According to the quest and the wiki's summary, during the Archon War he offered his "clones" as food to starving people in Sumeru, granting power in exchange; the larger his following, the thinner his power became. He ordered a human follower to carry him somewhere hot to reproduce, and an eruption near the Great Volcano of Tollan buried them. Over 2,000 years later the green berryshrooms in Varesa's orchard let him contact the Traveler, Paimon and Varesa. He still thought the Archon War was going on, and was beaten when the Collective of Plenty simply ate the mushrooms.

105.content: Xamaran is a giant glowing mushroom in the Glowing Narrows of the Chasm's Underground Mines in Liyue, and can speak through spores. Tighnari says it took a long time to reach its present form. It has an affinity for Lumenspar and can be energized with the Lumenstone Adjuvant. After the 5.5 Natlan questline it is revealed to be an offshoot of the fungus god Bifrons, though it long ago lost its mental link to him and speaks of him with disdain.

106.content: During the limited-time event Fabulous Fungus Frenzy (3.2), a researcher organizes a Beast Tamer Tournament at Port Ormos with the backing of a wealthy sponsor, and contestants capture and train fungi. In the sixth event quest, Farewell, My Shroom Buddies, the Traveler's fungus Bongo-Head, Layla's Twirly-Whirly and Yae Miko's Blitzara appear as companions at the end of the tournament. Yae Miko says the event also exposed a criminal conspiracy involving a man named Elchingen.

107.content:
Geovishap (also: Geovishaps, Geo Vishap, Geo Vishaps, Rock-Hard Geo Beast): Geovishaps are large, armoured vishaps native to Liyue's mountains. They are Geo-attuned elite beasts that roll into a ball, slam, and send spikes along the ground. Adults can also soak up Cryo, Pyro, Electro or Hydro from their surroundings and fight with it. They are the grown form of Geovishap Hatchlings and the lesser kin of the great Primo Geovishap.

The Adventurer Handbook and Archive call them mature Geovishaps. Both they and the Primo Geovishaps spent many years hibernating under the mountains and only recently became active, which is why ancient texts were the only record of them until adventurers began meeting them in Liyue. They first appeared in Version 1.3.

Nature: Geovishaps are vishaps, dragon-like elemental creatures of the Light Realm, in their Geo line. They are heavily armoured and aggressive towards people. The name is Geo plus "vishap", an Armenian word for dragon.

Their armour grows over a hatchling's. Archive text says hatchlings are said to shed the shell that first protected them and become Geovishaps after many years. Sumeru Akademiya experts quoted in the hatchling's entry think vishaps become dragons when fully grown, and a hatchling that avoids predators and disasters might one day reign over a mountain.

Habitat: Liyue's rocky country, often in caves and burrows. Known haunts include Tianqiu Valley in Minlin, the Chasm and the highlands of Chenyu Vale.

The Handbook can pinpoint Geovishap Hatchling locations on the map. In the opening quest of the event "Vishaps and Where to Find Them", the Adventurers' Guild treats lone adult sightings as a danger to travellers, caravans and lantern-watchers.

Abilities and limits: Geovishaps roll into a ball and charge, jump and land with a slam, slash and punch with their claws, and drag out lines of spikes from the ground. Their signature trick is Elemental Conversion: partway through a fight an adult absorbs Cryo, Pyro, Electro or Hydro and hits harder with it.

Which element they pick usually reflects the environment: for example a Pyro coating if Flaming Flowers grow nearby. In The Chasm, Khedive explains that a Geovishap which turned Hydro had fed on Hydro-rich waterweeds, matching the energy it takes from local plants.

Relations: Hatchlings are their young. Primo Geovishaps are the larger form. Azhdaha, Geo Dragon Sovereign, is an ancient ancestor of the species. People in Liyue treat them as dangerous beasts.

Folktales say the Primo Geovishaps and their kind retreated underground after a draconic calamity at Tianqiu Valley. The Archive version adds that the overlord of the Geovishaps was imprisoned deep beneath the earth, and that the servants burrowed away to wait. In the quest "No Restoring This Past Land of Beauty", Zhiping suggests the monsters reported in Tianqiu Valley are the Geovishaps and Primo Geovishaps that once terrorised Liyue.

Individuals: - Yiji and Tianyu: a Local Legend pair of Geovishaps called the Rulers of the Chizhang Mountains, found at Chizhang Wall in Chenyu Vale. One is Cryo and one Pyro. They were added in 4.4.
- Azhdaha: the Geo Dragon Sovereign, an ancient Geovishap ancestor (own entry).

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): Geovishaps are elite enemies in the Vishaps group of the Mystical Beasts family, and drop bone shards. Defeating one in each of its elemental forms is an achievement ("...Geovishap, Solarvishap, Lunarvishap...").

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): a Geovishap is a territorial beast, not a talker. Show stone-grey armour, a heavy crouch before the roll, burrowing, and the sudden shift in colour when it takes on another element. Keep to mountain and cave scenes in Liyue.

108.content: A young vishap with a hard Geo exoskeleton. Handbook text says vishaps are agile and not to be underestimated. Hatchlings carry bone shards and dig in groups, and Sumeru Akademiya experts believe vishaps become dragons when fully grown. In gameplay they burrow often and use a spinning attack.

109.content: Tianqiu Valley in Minlin, Liyue, was a settlement long ago and is now ruins with a Primo Geovishap in a cave. Folktales speak of a draconic calamity that ruined the valley, after which the Geovishaps and Primo Geovishaps burrowed deep into the earth to wait for another chance to rise. The wiki links this to Azhdaha's old rampage and his imprisonment by Rex Lapis and the adepti, but the in-game text does not name him.

110.content: Yiji and Tianyu are a pair of Local Legend Geovishaps called the Rulers of the Chizhang Mountains. They live at Chizhang Wall in Chenyu Vale, Liyue, and fight as a Cryo and a Pyro partner. Chizhang was once the city governed by the Mistress of Chenyu Vale. The pair were added to the game in Version 4.4.

key: Vishaps and Where to Find Them
111.comment: Geovishap: Vishaps and Where to Find Them
111.content: During a limited-time event, the Liyue Adventurers' Guild, through Katheryne, reports unusual Geovishap sightings across Liyue and asks adventurers to investigate. Until then the only known sightings were in ancient texts. The adults look like hatchlings but are far more aggressive and destructive. Because of the many lantern-watchers heading to remote spots, the Guild fears dire consequences from an encounter.

112.content:
Ghost (also: Ghosts, Spirits, Lingering souls, Shades of Tokoyo, Sinshades): Ghosts, also called spirits, are spectral figures found in many parts of Teyvat. Per the wiki, they are the souls of the dead that linger rather than being reincarnated, though some are better described as memories projected by the Ley Lines. Most keep a human appearance. They are not a single species: each region has its own sort, from Wuwang Hill in Liyue to Enkanomiya, Tsurumi Island, Natlan and Nod-Krai.

Ghost NPCs stand in graveyards, ruins and places marked by disaster. Most are tied to a place. Flins says they are hard to reason with, and the Final Night Cemetery's ghosts react strongly to the lighthouse being relit.

Nature: The wiki profile calls ghosts souls that remain in the world and do not get reincarnated for unknown reasons. The ghosts of Wuwang Hill and Tsurumi Island appear instead to be memory recreations made by the Ley Lines.

Appearance varies. Ghosts at Wuwang Hill and Mingyun Village keep clear features such as clothing, age and gender. Shades of Tokoyo in Enkanomiya are human-shaped but mostly featureless, resembling dark identical mannequins in robes. The ghosts of Tsurumi Island are blob-like and barely human; whether that is the Ley Line Disorder's effect or a local belief is not stated. Hanachirusato is an outlier: a physical, non-spectral recreation of Kitsune Saiguu made of filth by the Sacred Sakura.

Places: Wuwang Hill in Liyue has a permanent eerie fog and blue ghost lights, and is used for tests of courage. Liyue, Inazuma and Mondstadt each have a handful of ghost NPCs; Boreas and the historical Stanley are listed among Mondstadt's. Enkanomiya has the Shades of Tokoyo, seen during Evernight. Nod-Krai has Lightkeepers' ghosts at the Final Night Cemetery and others at the Sanctum of Departed Heroes.

Shades of tokoyo: In Enkanomiya, Shades of Tokoyo (also Sinshades, afterimages, once called Eidolons and Ghostfire Phantasms) are projections of the past. Byakuyakoku, a nether realm, sometimes projects shadows based on remnant thoughts, and strong emotions called Sins of Tokoyo can become a ley line phenomenon of Sinshades. A Sinshade that realises it is one will soon disappear, as 'to know sin is to be free of it'. Aru, a "sinless" Shade created specifically to help with the Watatsumi Goryou Matsuri, is an exception.

How {{char}} behaves: This is the project's suggested interpretation. Ghosts are bound to a place, a role or a memory; speak plainly of what they last did and let them be caught up in it. Do not turn a ghost into a free-roaming person, and do not assert why any specific ghost remains unless canon states it.

113.content: The Final Night Cemetery on Paha Isle holds the graves of Lightkeepers, and their ghosts linger there with Flins. Flins describes the ghosts as echoes of living souls that failed to enter the Ley Lines at death; they are hard to reason with, and over time will return to the Ley Lines.

114.content: Natlan's dead are meant to enter the Night Kingdom, but it is growing weaker, especially at accepting souls, and many fail to reach the Ley Lines. Citlali says such lost souls wander and fade from existence for good, and that returning them usually takes a complex ritual or a soul-perceiving vessel like Ororon. (The wiki's added claim that a shaman can open the gate for a recently dead soul, which may refuse, is unconfirmed here.)

115.comment: Ghost: Tsurumi and Wuwang Hill Ghosts
115.content: The ghosts of Wuwang Hill and Tsurumi Island appear to be memory recreations made by the Ley Lines. On Tsurumi, ghosts replay the past in the Through the Mists quest series, and one of them, Ruu, developed self-awareness.

116.content:
Gosoythoth (also: Reaper of the Abyss, heart of the Abyss, Gosoythoth, Reaper of the Abyss): Gosoythoth, titled the Reaper of the Abyss, was a powerful sapient entity that Natlan's defenders called the heart of the Abyss. When the Abyss put out the Sacred Flame, it manifested over the Stadium of the Sacred Flame as a black rift and led an all-out invasion of Natlan. It was driven back by Mavuika's Night War, then hunted into the Night Kingdom and killed there by Mavuika and the Traveler in the Version 5.3 finale of the Natlan Archon Quest. It is dead as of 7.1.

It was a quest-exclusive character, first seen in The Surging Darkness (5.1) and killed in Where All Hopes Lie (5.3); the Night War was declared in No One Fights Alone (5.1). Its battle form is the weekly boss Lord of Eroded Primal Fire.

Nature: Gosoythoth had no fixed body. It was an entity of ineffable form that took shape from the Abyss's power once the Sacred Flame was gone. Unlike its monsters it could think: it worked out Mavuika's plan to awaken a last hero and moved to crush Natlan before that could happen.

It referred to itself as an individual and showed confidence, arrogance and, in the end, fear. Xilonen sums up the danger in Despair Engulfs the Heavens: the heart of the Abyss had joined the invasion, which was a power the defenders could not match.

Appearance: Over Natlan it looked like a huge dark rift in the sky: a spiral of dark purple cubes, a green-black eclipse-like light at the centre that resembles an eye, and a galaxy-like aura. It could briefly shrink to a dark purple orb with the same star and sphere patterns. In the Night Kingdom it took the shape of a giant Abyss-corroded dragon (see the Xiuhcoatl form).

History: After the Abyss snuffed out the Sacred Flame, Gosoythoth manifested its heart above the Stadium of the Sacred Flame. Mavuika used the Gnosis to relight the Sacred Flame and briefly held the incursion back. Gosoythoth retreated into the sky and hung over Natlan, staining land and sky black.

Abilities and limits: Rained Abyss Tumors that spawned Abyssal Pylons and monsters; mimicry of enemies; and in the Xiuhcoatl form, Pyro and Abyssal flame attacks, which the weekly boss version also uses to corrode the ground.

Status as of 7.1: Dead. It was killed in the Night Kingdom by Mavuika and the Traveler (Where All Hopes Lie, 5.3).

Canon says only that the Night Kingdom was purged "for the time being", so a return is not ruled out but is not stated either.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay guidance (project recommendation): Gosoythoth is a villain of one arc, not a recurring character. Show it as sapient, proud and cruel, and as afraid of the Traveler. Do not give it a backstory, name for its origin, or ties to other Abyss figures that canon does not state. It should not be alive in any scene set after Where All Hopes Lie.

117.content: In the Night Kingdom, Gosoythoth took the shape of the dead Pyro Dragon Sovereign Xiuhcoatl by pulling his memories out of the ley lines. The result is the Lord of Eroded Primal Fire. It is Gosoythoth imitating a dead dragon, not Xiuhcoatl returned.

118.content: Mavuika declared the Night War after awakening the Divine Throne's power. For its duration the warriors of Natlan kept resurrecting, which destroyed the Abyssal army. It ended Gosoythoth's invasion of the surface and pushed it back into the Abyss.

119.content:
Hilichurl (also: hilichurl people, curse of the wilderness, wilderness curse, cursed Khaenri'ahns): Hilichurls are the masked, tribal creatures that attack travellers in the wilds of every nation, and most people take them for monsters. Many are in fact cursed people: Khaenri'ahns of mixed or foreign ancestry struck with the "curse of the wilderness" in the cataclysm 500 years ago. It wears away memory, speech and appearance but not life, leaving them in slow, painful decline.

This entry covers hilichurls as a people with a past. The monster family (Samachurls, Mitachurls, Lawachurls, gameplay) is in the Hilichurls entry. Few in Teyvat know the truth; Dainsleif, the Traveler and the Traveler's sibling do, as did Chlothar Alberich.

Nature: A hilichurl is bare-chested and barefoot, with a heavy mane, long ears, a loincloth and bandaged limbs, and always wears a mask. The Archive says they look much like humans but seem to have lost their intellect and spirituality. Dainsleif explains in The Grave of the Guarded (2.6) that the mask is so they never see their own reflection in water: compared with how they remember themselves, the sight brings them great despair. So they still remember something of what they were.

Origin: After the cataclysm the gods cursed Khaenri'ahns in two ways. Pure-blood Khaenri'ahns received the curse of immortality. People whose ancestry belonged to other gods' lands received the curse of the wilderness, which turned them into monsters.

Dainsleif confirmed in 2.6 that the hilichurls drawn to The Chasm in Liyue come from Khaenri'ah. In Fortune-Mocking Pedigree (3.5) Chlothar Alberich, living as "Eide", explains: Khaenri'ah began as one bloodline but welcomed anyone who forsook their god, and when the cataclysm came the pure-bloods were named the "greater sinners" and made immortal, while those from other gods' domains were punished as they fled. His own son Caribert, whose mother's roots were in Mondstadt, became a hilichurl as a small child.

Curse: The curse degrades the mind: memories fade, speech and understanding of Common are lost, and the body outlives its time. A hilichurl cannot simply die of age; erosion wears body and mind toward something like death, and old hilichurls are said to be in constant pain. Dainsleif says immortality does not mean one never dies, only that body and soul keep eroding until almost nothing is left.

Decline and end: Old hilichurls that sense their end seek a calm, dark corner to say goodbye to centuries of suffering. Part of The Chasm, near the Inverted City, eases the curse, so many go there and ignore food and danger.

Relations: Most hilichurls are hostile to travellers. Abyss Mages speak Hilichurlian and often command them. The Abyss Order and the Traveler's sibling regard them as Khaenri'ah's lost citizens, to be cleansed so they die naturally or become the base of a rebuilt homeland (Dainsleif). Hilichurls elsewhere are not always hostile: during the limited-time Mimi Tomo event (1.5), hilichurls in several regions, including Starfell Valley, asked the Traveler for help in fights against Treasure Hoarders and Abyss Mages.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 no one has been shown lifting the curse of the wilderness, and hilichurls remain common across Teyvat. No Nod-Krai (6.x) or Snezhnaya (7.0-7.1) content read for this entry changes this picture.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay guidance (this project's recommendation, not canon text): when the Khaenri'ah link matters, play hilichurls as pitiable and dangerous at once. They cannot say what they were, yet still flinch at reflections and mourn in song. Do not let one speak Common or recall Khaenri'ah. A character who knows the truth (Dainsleif, the Traveler, Chlothar) says so quietly, because the knowledge is rare and painful.

Portrayal notes (common mistakes to avoid): - Not all hilichurls are Khaenri'ahns: only many are, and the older ones are unexplained.
- The curse of the wilderness did not hit pure-blood Khaenri'ahns; they got immortality.
- The Traveler cured no one. In 2.6 they only stopped a cleansing device; Caribert and Caterpillar regained speech through Abyssal power and Narzissenkreuz's blade.
- Abyss Mages, Heralds and Lectors are Abyss Order monsters, not hilichurls, even though the wiki reads the Order's monsters as also originating from Khaenri'ah's people.

120.content: The curse of the wilderness is one of two curses the gods placed on Khaenri'ah at the cataclysm. Chlothar Alberich (as Eide) says pure-blood Khaenri'ahns were judged the "greater sinners" and given the curse of immortality, while those whose ancestry belonged to other gods' domains were punished with the curse of the wilderness as they fled, turning them into monsters. The effects are loss of memory, speech and appearance, plus a long, prolonged decline. The Archive and Dainsleif describe hilichurls as the result.

121.content: Dainsleif says hilichurls wear masks to avoid seeing their reflection in water. Compared with how they remember themselves, the sight is a terrible one that causes great despair. This shows hilichurls still remember their human faces. Masks also show a hilichurl's element in their designs, and shamans' masks are horned.

122.content: In Requiem of the Echoing Depths (2.6) the miner Yuehui commissions the Traveler to look into strange hilichurl activity in The Chasm. The Traveler and Paimon meet Dainsleif underground. He explains that these hilichurls come to the area, where the curse is eased, to spend their final years. Black Serpent Knights guard them, led by Halfdan. A pool at the summit is a relic of an older civilisation and is the source of the effect.

123.comment: Hilichurl: Black Serpent Knights guarding the dying
123.content: The Black Serpent Knights are Khaenri'ah's former Royal Guard, now cursed and mindless. In The Chasm they protect hilichurls, and Dainsleif thinks they are still following the last order to protect the people of Khaenri'ah. He recognises one as Halfdan, an elite he knew as a young man, whose silent order makes the others retreat. The knights repeat a single word of the old language: "Run". Halfdan later sacrificed himself to halt the Abyss Order's device, and his soul briefly spoke with Dainsleif before passing on (2.6).

124.content: Caribert was the son of Chlothar Alberich and a mother with Mondstadt roots, so the curse of the wilderness turned him into a hilichurl while he was still a young child. Chlothar cared for him while he lay in torpor. With the help of the Traveler's sibling he tried a forbidden medicine, and after Vedrfolnir's power was given to Chlothar a later dose gave Caribert back his mind and speech.

125.content: Caterpillar ("Cater") looks like a child, but he is not one; he was held in the Fortress of Meropide for centuries and later joined the Ordo's efforts against Jakob's world. He is a former Anemo Hilichurl Rogue. Narzissenkreuz's miracle gave him sentience and human speech, and he was inducted into the Narzissenkreuz Ordo. A log says remains of Carter Scherbius were grafted on "those who have lost their intellect", which is read to mean hilichurls. He calls himself a monster in human skin.

126.comment: Hilichurl: Hilichurls and the Abyss Order
126.content: Abyss Mages speak fluent Hilichurlian and can direct tribes, so hilichurls often fight for the Abyss Order. In the Order's view they are Khaenri'ah's lost citizens. In Hurdle (1.0), when hilichurls turn up near Stormterror's Lair, Venti notes that they avoid dense elemental energy and Diluc concludes the Order must be manipulating them.

127.content:
Hilichurls (also: hilichurl tribes, Hilifolk, hill devils, hill dwellers, majuj): Hilichurls are primitive, masked humanoid monsters found in wild places all over Teyvat. They live in small tribes, speak their own language (Hilichurlian), love meat, hate vegetables, and are usually hostile to humans. Most people believe they cannot be reasoned with. Many of them are former people of Khaenri'ah who were cursed into this form during the cataclysm 500 years ago.

A hilichurl tribe works like an extended family. The usual figures are ordinary hilichurls, Samachurls (shamans), Mitachurls (big warriors), Lawachurls (huge, solitary "kings") and tribeless Hilichurl Rogues.

Nature: Hilichurls are bare-chested and barefoot, with a large mane, long ears, a loincloth, bandaged limbs, greyish-black skin and always a mask. The Archive says they resemble humans but have lost "both their intellect and spirituality".

The masks have a reason. In The Grave of the Guarded (2.6), Dainsleif explains that hilichurls cover their faces so they never see their reflection in water: compared with how they remember themselves, the sight drives them to despair. Hilichurls have been recorded for over a thousand years, but their numbers spread sharply after the "pitch-black calamity" of 500 years ago. They can live in many environments, but they avoid places with very dense elemental energy, which strains their bodies.

Society: Tribes are small and scattered through the wilderness. The Samachurl (shaman) is usually the oldest member and acts like a parent: leading worship, deciding policy and defending the tribe with elemental power. Food and goods are shared according to need.

In some tribes, a stronger Mitachurl overthrows the shaman; these tribes become more aggressive. Every member gathers and fights. Lawachurls are honoured with the title "Lawa" (roughly "king" or "chief") but do not actually rule and prefer to live alone. Hilichurls keep contact with other tribes, some over long distances. Mondstadt has many tribes; remote regions such as Natlan and Nod-Krai have few.

Abilities and limits: They fight with fists, clubs, rocks, crossbows and shields. Some, above all Samachurls, channel elements without a Vision; Jacob Musk calls this unexplained.

Hilichurls make heavy use of Slimes. They keep food fresh with Cryo Slimes, cook with Pyro Slimes, lift supply balloons with Anemo Slimes, and dig slimes out of the ground to throw. Mitachurls slam slimes into their axes to give them an element, Dendro Slimes reinforce wooden shields, and Anemo Rogues ride Anemo Slimes into the air.

Variants: Common hilichurls (fighters, guards, shooters, grenadiers); Samachurls (elemental shamans); Mitachurls (big warriors with axes or shields); Lawachurls (mutated elemental giants: Stonehide, Frostarm, Thunderhelm); Hilichurl Rogues (tribeless Anemo or Hydro wanderers).

Relations: Hilichurls usually attack outsiders on sight, and adventurers and the Knights of Favonius fight them routinely; a few individuals will talk.

Many hilichurl groups are allied with the Abyss Order, whose Abyss Mages speak fluent Hilichurlian and can persuade them to fight. Abyss Mages are sometimes seen conducting hilichurl dances. The Abyss also drove hilichurls into battle during its invasion of Natlan. Not every hilichurl obeys the Order: a cautious hilichurl in Starfell Valley once asked the Traveler to drive off Abyss Mages and Hilichurl Shooters.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 hilichurls remain common across Teyvat. The curse has not been lifted for anyone; the only known exceptions to their speechlessness (Caribert, Caterpillar) involved Abyssal power or Narzissenkreuz's miracle, not a cure. Frostarm Lawachurls also roam Snezhnaya (7.0).

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): hilichurls are one of the first enemy families the player meets. Their drops are masks, scrolls, arrowheads, horns and similar materials. Rogues are the only group that does not drop hilichurl materials.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): portray hilichurls as dangerous but pitiable. They growl, chant and shout in Hilichurlian rather than speaking the common tongue. They are territorial and protective of camp, meat and tribe, and they dance when pleased. Ordinary Teyvat people see monsters; only those who know Khaenri'ah's history, such as Dainsleif, the Traveler or Chlothar, see cursed people.
