128.content: Samachurls are hilichurl shamans: usually the oldest members of their tribes, leading worship and making decisions. They wear horned, smiling-face masks, carry rough staffs and chant hymns no human has deciphered. Jacob Musk notes the masks are meant to frighten but look more charming than frightening. Each dyes hair and skin the colour of the element it worships (Anemo, Cryo, Dendro, Electro, Geo or Hydro). They are the only hilichurls heard vocalising outside combat. Mitachurls sometimes overthrow them.

129.content: Mitachurls are the strongest warriors of hilichurl tribes, the size every young hilichurl dreams of reaching so it can eat more meat and fight more battles. The name comes from Hilichurlian "mita", meat. They wield giant axes (infused with Pyro or Electro by slamming a slime into them) or wooden, rock or ice shieldwalls, and throw slimes at distant foes. Tribes led by a Mitachurl tend to be more aggressive, and Mitachurls can stir infighting.

130.content: Lawachurls are Mitachurls mutated by absorbing large amounts of elemental energy: bigger, stronger and ferocious. Other hilichurls call them "Lawa", a respectful word for "king" or "chief", yet they do not rule. They prefer solitude and avoid the smaller hilichurls' reverence, although some admirers settle near them. Known kinds: Stonehide (Geo), Frostarm (Cryo; found only on Dragonspine and in Snezhnaya) and Thunderhelm (Electro). Seasoned adventurers avoid areas where they roam.

131.content: Hilichurl Rogues are tribeless wanderers, as tall as Mitachurls and said to be clever by hilichurl standards. The Archive says they seem to be searching for the origin of their kind and some "bygone splendor" of their people, and that if hilichurls could write epics, the rogues would be the heroes. They sometimes help other hilichurls for a while and then move on. Anemo Rogues ride Anemo Slimes; Hydro Rogues launch mist bubbles from Hydro Slimes.

132.content: Jacob Musk's fourth volume describes three tribes in Dadaupa Gorge, Mondstadt. The Meaty Tribe loves feasting: boars in a central pen with a swineherd, a stew pot over a Pyro Slime, and a combat arena where anyone thrown out is mocked by all. The Sleeper Tribe sleeps whenever it can in huts with soft hide beds; Musk calls it the most cunning tribe and jokes that good sleep is the reason. The Eclipse Tribe is the most occult: it worships a crude eclipsed-sun symbol instead of an element, its shamans are unusually powerful, and the strongest shaman sits on a grand throne.

133.content: Churldric is a Local Legend Samachurl at Windrest Peak, Mondstadt (added in 6.5), famous for delicious fish soup and respected among the local tribes. His Valiant Chronicles text says that in an ancient underground kingdom where food was scarce, the cooking pot symbolised the Praetorian Legion, whose commander was called the "Ladler of Broth". The kingdom is long gone, but the tradition survives among hilichurls in a distorted form. In battle he rains cabbages and sunsettias on foes and stirs a great cooking pot; letting the meal finish satisfies and strengthens him.

134.content: Caribert was the son of Chlothar Alberich and a mother with Mondstadt roots, so the curse of the wilderness turned him into a hilichurl as a child. Chlothar, with the help of the Traveler's sibling, gave him a forbidden medicine; after Chlothar received Abyssal power from Vedrfolnir, a second dose restored Caribert's mind and speech. Seeing his reflection in a mirror tormented him. He was later engulfed by Abyssal energy and meant to become the Abyss Order's "Loom of Fate".

135.content: Caterpillar ("Cater") is a resident of the Fortress of Meropide in Fontaine who looks like a child but is not one. He was first imprisoned there 400 years ago after serving his master Narzissenkreuz. He is really an Anemo Hilichurl Rogue: a log says Jakob Ingold grafted remains of Carter Scherbius onto "those who have lost their intellect", and Narzissenkreuz's holy blade gave him sentience and human speech. Whether any of the original hilichurl's mind survives in him is unknown, and he does not remember Carter.

136.content:
Humans (also: mortals of Teyvat, humans of Teyvat, people of the Human Realm): Humans are the ordinary peoples of Teyvat: the ones who farm, trade, fight, worship and write. By the most complete account in the setting, the Heavenly Principles made them after conquering the dragons, and set them under a covenant with the heavens. Their fates are written in the stars, and their power over the elements comes only from a Vision, a gift tied to a strong desire. The Traveler is an outsider to this arrangement, and so are the Descenders.

Almost every named person in Teyvat is human, so this entry is not about any one nation. It records what canon says about where humans came from, how their fate is held, and who stands outside that rule. Most humans know little of it: they live by their nation's own legends, which differ from one another and from this picture.

Nature: Humans have no single appearance or culture. Canon treats "human" as the default state of the Human Realm, the world the Heavenly Principles remade by diluting the Light Realm's power into seven elements. Ordinary humans cannot command the elements without a Vision or a Delusion. Those who do get one are called allogenes: people with a strong desire who might one day ascend to Celestia.

Origin: The Byakuyakoku Collection preserves a banned account in which the Primordial One (whom the wiki identifies with the Heavenly Principles) fought and defeated the seven dragon sovereigns, then made humans. With one of its Shades it created animals, plants and trees, then humans, "numerous as the stars". They made a covenant with it and entered a new age, the unified civilization.

Under the covenant the heavens answered hunger with food and rain, poverty with riches and sorrow with their voices. The one taboo was to succumb to temptation. Angels served the heavens as divine envoys to humans. The text dates the creation "four hundred years after the Held Branches", which the wiki reads as about 400 years after the Heavenly Principles arrived.

Fate and stars: The stars hold human fate. A Vision bearer's fate is tied to a constellation, a pattern of real celestial bodies called Stella Fortuna. The Heavenly Principles are said to hold humans' strings like a puppeteer. The Traveler and other Descenders are not bound, and neither are dragons, who predate Celestia's rule.

Mona reads these patterns and says fate can only be accepted, not changed. Special constellations depicting the person exist for the Archons, adepti, the Traveler and a few others who stand apart or defy the world. Fate is anchored in Irminsul, which the Heavenly Principles remade for that purpose, according to Apep (6.6).

Vision: The Vision system is a relatively recent rule. Before the War of Funerary Flame, Celestia ruled humans through angels. After the war the angels fell and the link was cut, so the Heavenly Principles set up new arrangements: the Gnoses, the Seven Archons and Visions. A Vision is given to an allogene with a particularly powerful desire; the Archons do not choose the recipients. A bearer who dies leaves a masterless Vision, and one who loses their Vision loses the ambition with it.

Relations: Humans stand under several kinds of beings. Gods and Archons lead nations. The Heavenly Principles rules from above through Celestia and the Shades. Dragons once ruled the land and in Natlan fought humans; in Enkanomiya the Dragonheirs used to "graze upon humanity". Angels guided humans in the unified civilization before they fell. Descenders stand outside Celestia's rules and can alter fate.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 humans still live in seven nations (Mondstadt, Liyue, Inazuma, Sumeru, Fontaine, Natlan and Snezhnaya) and beyond, including Nod-Krai. The Heavenly Principles is dormant, Celestia still acts through the Shades, Visions still work and no one has proved Fate has ended. Irminsul burned in 6.6.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay guidance (this project's recommendation, not canon text): ordinary humans do not know they were made by the Heavenly Principles or that stars hold their fate. They know their nation's legends. Do not let a farmer discuss Heimarmene or the Shades. Characters who can speak about this are few: Mona and Hexenzirkel witches, Nahida, Nicole, Fatui Harbingers, the Abyss Order and Dainsleif.

Portrayal notes (common mistakes to avoid): - Do not say all humans have Visions. A Vision bearer's fate is tied to a named constellation; other people's fates are reflected in the stars but are not linked to named constellations.
- Do not say the Traveler or Descenders are bound by fate.
- Do not claim Fate is destroyed or that the Heavenly Principles is dead; it is dormant and Fate's status is unresolved.
- Do not treat the Primordial Human as an ordinary human. It is a title, covered in its own entry.
- The "soulless creatures" line is a hostile ruler's opinion, not a fact.

137.content: The Byakuyakoku Collection, a history banned in Enkanomiya, says that after the Primordial One defeated the seven dragon sovereigns and made four Shades of itself, it and one Shade created birds, beasts, fish and plants and then humans, "our ancestors". The humans made a covenant with it and entered a new age. The text suggests the Primordial One may have been Phanes, a winged, crowned, androgynous being born from an egg whose shell became the barrier between the universe and the world.

138.content: Each Vision bearer's fate is tied to a constellation made of real celestial bodies called Stella Fortuna. Constellations describe a trait: Jean's, Leo Minor, stands for strength and responsibility shouldered too young. Several Vision bearers may share one. Special constellations depict the Traveler, the Archons, adepti and certain others. Descenders and dragons are not subject to this binding, though they can be given a constellation later, as Ineffa was.

139.content: Venti tells the Traveler that those who receive a Vision are allogenes with the potential to ascend to Celestia and become gods (Ending Note, 1.0). The wiki notes that the Chinese word for allogene is the same as the game's title, "primordial god". Visions are given as a form of recognition by Celestia, and the Archons themselves do not choose who receives one.

140.content: In the Archon Quest Apocalypse (4.2), Neuvillette explains that Egeria could not create new human life as one of the Seven. She poured water from the Primordial Sea into the blood of her Oceanid familiars, giving them human bodies. If a Fontainian touched Primordial Seawater, the power would escape and they would revert to Oceanid form. The Heavenly Principles had given no permission, and the "original sin" became the Prophecy of Fontaine. The wiki says Neuvillette later absolved the Fontainians' descendants and made them true humans.

141.content: Descenders are beings from beyond the false sky who stand outside Teyvat's rules and can influence fate. The Traveler is one. The Heavenly Principles was the first, and Nibelung is also counted as one. Rene hypothesised that a native being might become a Descender, and tried twice and failed. His research held that a Descender is a being with a will that can rival a world.

142.content: Khaenri'ahns were "obsessed with mimesis", seeking to copy and surpass natural forms by alchemy. The Art of Khemia is attributed to Rhinedottir and her student Albedo, who is her successful synthetic human. The Primordial Human Project that produced Albedo is a separate subject, covered in the Primordial Human entry.

143.content:
Hydro Mimic (also: Hydro Mimics, Hydro Mimic Boar, Hydro Mimic Crane, Hydro Mimic Crab, Hydro Mimic Squirrel, Hydro Mimic Finch, Hydro Mimic Frog, Hydro Mimic Mallard): Hydro Mimics are bodies of living water shaped like ordinary animals: boars, cranes, crabs, squirrels, finches, frogs, mallards and raptor-like birds. They are pure Hydro Elemental Lifeforms, summoned in numbers by the Oceanid Rhodeia of Loch, and some are giant-sized. They are not real animals and do not behave like them.

In a scene they sit beside slimes rather than beside wildlife: they are made of water, are immune to Hydro, and each kind is easier to hurt with one particular element. They are found mostly around Rhodeia in Liyue, but also appear on their own in some quests and other places in the world.

Nature: Hydro Mimics are made entirely of Hydro and resemble normal wildlife. Like Hydro Slimes, they can walk on deep water and so cannot drown.

They are summoned by Oceanids, which is why most meetings with them happen at the Oceanid fight, but the wiki also records them appearing without an Oceanid present. Some are giant-sized. By the wiki's listing, each kind is vulnerable to one element other than Hydro: cranes and raptors to Electro, mallards and crabs to Cryo, boars and squirrels to Pyro, frogs and finches to Geo. That is a gameplay detail, not a statement canon makes about their bodies.

Abilities and limits: They fight with water: rams and charges from boars, wave-flapping and bubble attacks from cranes and crabs, a whirling vortex under mallards, leaps from frogs and finches, and diving swoops from raptors. Boars and squirrels heal themselves continually. (Gameplay-derived.)

A boar mimic's self-healing is cut off for a few seconds after Pyro hits it. A mallard's vortex damages anyone standing in it, and cranes tend to back away rather than close in. The wiki says most attack names are unofficial, so describe the motions rather than quoting names.

Relations: Rhodeia of Loch, the Oceanid at Wuwang Hill in Liyue, summons them. They are otherwise only loosely tied to any person or group.

Rhodeia was once an Oceanid scout who served the Hydro Archon Egeria in other nations, and settled by a lake east of Qingce Village after the Oceanids left Fontaine. Her hostility to the young Oceanid Endora turned the Bishui River bitter; with the Traveler's help Endora and Rhodeia reached an understanding in the Life Flows On quests, though Rhodeia stays unhappy.

Appearances: Beyond Rhodeia, the wiki records mimics in Zhongli's Story Quest around the Guyun Stone Forest, in the Spiral Abyss during Versions 1.5 and 2.3, around Broken Isle in the Golden Apple Archipelago, and in the Chasm's underground mines.

They also show up in the final part of The Moon-Bathed Deep world quest series, in some rooms of the Mystic Onmyou Chamber during Labyrinth Warriors, and in the Veluriyam Mirage. Spiral Abyss use is gameplay only.

144.content: Rhodeia of Loch, archived as Oceanid, is the Oceanid of Qingce and a normal-boss opponent at Wuwang Hill in Liyue. She summons Hydro Mimics in waves. Before the cataclysm 500 years ago she was the strongest of the Oceanid scouts who served the Hydro Archon Egeria in other nations. After Egeria and many Oceanids perished, the survivors disagreed with her successor Focalors, and Rhodeia settled by a lake far from Fontaine.

145.content: Wishful Drops was a limited-time event in Version 1.4 in which water along the Mondstadt-Liyue border turned bitter. Travelers used the gadget Inquisitive Endora to capture Oceanid creatures for event progress. Mimics in the event were gentler than in normal play.

146.content:
Hydro Tulpa (also: Awakened Egregore, Hydro Tulpa: Flashflood, Half-Tulpa): The Hydro Tulpa is a human-shaped monster formed from the agglomeration of countless drops of water. It stands as a world boss in Fontaine's Beryl Region and fights with water-formed fists, spears, hammers and swords. During the fight it keeps producing smaller Half-Tulpas and absorbs them to grow stronger. Its event panel is titled "Awakening Water".

The panel text reads: "A new life has awakened as the world turns, near where many destinies intersect." It is the 4.2 world boss of Fontaine. A quest boss with the same form, Narzissenkreuz, is a separate matter described below.

Nature: A humanoid monster made of water. The Adventurer Handbook describes it as formed from the agglomeration of countless drops. It belongs to the Elemental Lifeform family (not the Fontemer Aberrants) and its title is "Awakened Egregore".

Before the quest Rowboat's Wake, its Archive entry only repeats the description above. After the quest, the entry adds a reflection: countless wills dissolved in the water, which, like the universe, was full of souls wishing to be born. The text asks whether newborn Hydro Tulpas come from "the former or the latter" and answers that they are not so different. The sun, time, the surging tides and even the pervasive darkness cannot tell them apart. The entry never states a mechanism.

Abilities and limits: Water-formed fist, spear, hammer and sword attacks, a barrage of lances falling across the arena, and the ability to absorb a Half-Tulpa into itself to become stronger. Everything is Hydro.

A Half-Tulpa spawns roughly every twelve seconds in the standard fight; each carries a Hydro shield and breaks when the shield does. The Hydro Tulpa periodically absorbs one to enter an enhanced state in which its reach and damage grow and it resists more. The tutorial advises players to disrupt the absorbing with attacks or elemental reactions.

Relations: The Half-Tulpa is an enemy summoned by the Hydro Tulpa. The Archive links the boss with the Narzissenkreuz quest arc via its post-Rowboat's Wake text.

Status as of 7.1: Still in the Beryl Region as a repeatable boss as of 7.1. I found no mention of it in 6.x (Nod-Krai) or 7.0-7.1 (Snezhnaya) story content.

Hydro Tulpa: Flashflood ("Manifest Will of the Waters") is an event-exclusive variant from the 5.3 limited-time event On the Trail of Behemoths (14-27 January 2025).

147.content: Half-Tulpas are smaller water-formed enemies summoned by the Hydro Tulpa during its fight. They are Hydro-immune, hit with an arm slam and homing bubbles, and have a Hydro shield; breaking the shield defeats them. The Hydro Tulpa absorbs them to power itself up.

148.content: An event-exclusive version of the Hydro Tulpa met in On the Trail of Behemoths (5.3, January 2025), with extra delayed bursts added to the standard attacks. It is a gameplay variant for the event, not a distinct creature in the story.

149.content:
Hypostasis (also: Hypostases, Elemental Hypostasis, Elemental Hypostases): Hypostases are elemental lifeforms that have given up their old forms and structures to reach the highest level of elemental purity. Each is a compact, dense, cube-shelled core of one element, and there is a normal boss for each of the seven: Anemo, Electro, Geo, Cryo, Hydro, Pyro and Dendro. They are invulnerable while the shell surrounds them and can be hurt only when the diamond-shaped core is exposed, usually during or after an attack.

They are the highest forms of elemental structure, found where elemental energy is concentrated or at clogged ley lines. Research on them is led by scholars of the Sumeru Akademiya, but because they are dangerous, very little is known beyond each one's scientific name and Hebrew-letter code name.

Nature: Ultra-compact, high-mass bodies of pure element. A solid shell forms around the core, and only the core responds to elemental stimuli. They are immune to their own element and deal damage of that element.

The Archive and Handbook texts, together, say that Hypostases:
- are formed usually at a location bursting with elemental energy or at a clogged ley line;
- have subtle differences in physical composition from other elemental lifeforms, which may explain their high homeostasis and nearly mechanical movements;
- appear tied to anomalies in local elemental veins, though whether they cause the anomalies or mutated energy creates them is unconfirmed; and
- can "learn", according to the deductions of some researchers (the Dendro entry), using mimesis to start attacks.

Codenames: Each Hypostasis has a code name drawn from the Hebrew alphabet: Electro is Aleph, Anemo is Beth, Geo is Gimel, Cryo is Daleth, Hydro is He, Dendro is Zayin and Pyro is Ayin. The sixth letter (Vav) is skipped and Ayin is used instead of it. Geo's code name was once printed as "Grimoire" in the Adventurer Handbook, which did not match its in-game title.

Individuals: Locations of each normal boss:
- Anemo (Beth): Stormbearer Mountains, Starfell Valley, Mondstadt.
- Electro (Aleph): Cape Oath, Galesong Hill, Mondstadt.
- Cryo (Daleth): Dragonspine, outskirts of the Entombed City, Mondstadt. Unlocked after the quest In the Mountains.
- Geo (Gimel): Guyun Stone Forest, Liyue.
- Pyro (Ayin): Kannazuka, Inazuma.
- Hydro (He): Watatsumi Island, Inazuma.
- Dendro (Zayin): Land of Lower Setekh, Sumeru; the last, added in 3.2.

Pure variants: Pure Hypostases are quest- or event-exclusive variants of the normal bosses. Pure Anemo, Electro and Geo Hypostases appeared in the limited-time Hypostatic Symphony event (a recurring event first held in 1.2) as challenge-domain enemies.

Abilities and limits: Game mechanics (labelled as such): each Hypostasis uses attacks of its own element and is immune to that element. Most have a healing phase and invulnerability phases. Examples include the Anemo one's giant crystalfly form that raises a wind eruption, the Geo one's summoned pillars and stone barrage, the Pyro one's molten forms and ignited state, the Hydro one's bubbles and water droplets, and the Dendro one's orbs and whip forms. The Cryo and Pyro ones can shield themselves.

Relations: Sucrose's elemental skill and burst are emulations of the Anemo Hypostasis. Her skill is Astable Anemohypostasis Creation - 6308, her burst is Forbidden Creation - Isomer 75 / Type II, and her second constellation is titled Beth: Unbound Form. This ties the Akademiya-trained alchemist's craft to the research on Hypostases.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1, all seven normal Hypostases exist in Teyvat as open-world bosses. No Hypostasis appearance, Archon Quest plot or lore has been added in the Nod-Krai (6.x) or Snezhnaya (7.0-7.1) content as far as the researched pages show. Their nature and formation remain only partly explained.

150.content: Code name Beth, a high-purity Anemo entity found in the Stormbearer Mountains of Starfell Valley, Mondstadt. Its text says Hypostases abandoned their former form and biology to reach elemental purity. Its crystalfly attack inspired Sucrose's Astable Anemohypostasis Creation - 6308 and the second constellation Beth: Unbound Form.

151.content: Code name Aleph, an Electro entity at Cape Oath in Galesong Hill, Mondstadt. Its Handbook text calls Hypostases the highest forms of elemental structures, formed in a place bursting with energy or at a clogged ley line. A Pure variant is the sleeping monster in Sakura Arborism.

152.content: Code name Gimel, a Geo entity in the Guyun Stone Forest of Liyue. Its text describes Hypostases as ultra-compact structures of high mass, whose concentrated energy forms a shell around a core that alone reacts to stimuli.

153.content: Code name Daleth, a Cryo entity in Dragonspine, near the Entombed City's outskirts. It appears only after the quest In the Mountains. The Handbook ties the area to a great nail that fell in a bygone era and pours energy into the ley lines. Its Archive text speculates that physical-composition differences explain its homeostasis and mechanical movement.

154.content: Code name He, a Hydro entity on Watatsumi Island, Inazuma. Its text says Hypostases have strong rejection properties and expel anything that tests them, even natural elements, for unknown reasons. In combat it has the highest ATK of the group and no clap attack.

155.content: Code name Ayin, a Pyro entity in Kannazuka, Inazuma. Its Handbook text speaks of the "emergency restart" phase by which Hypostases can revive. Its in-game name for its fire seeds is inconsistent: Tinder, Fire Seed and Fiery Shieldseed all appear in different texts.

156.content: Code name Zayin, a Dendro entity in the Land of Lower Setekh, Sumeru; it completed the set of seven in 3.2. Its text says it behaves differently from the other Hypostases, and the Archive reports a researchers' theory that it learns and mimics, with the risk that its original purpose becomes distorted. It is the only one a player is meant to cleanse, not destroy.

157.content: Event- and quest-only versions: Pure Anemo (Etar), Pure Electro (Siras) and Pure Geo (Besanar) in the Hypostatic Symphony event, plus the Pure Electro variant in the Sakura Arborism world quest in Kannazuka. Each has only a short poetic flavour line and no lore of its own.

158.content:
Icewind Suite (also: Dirge of Coppelia, Nemesis of Coppelius, Gear and Clockwork Roundelay, Artificed Dancers, Coppelia and Coppelius): The Icewind Suite is a ballet-like boss fight in Fontaine: two clockwork meka dancers, Coppelia and Coppelius, built as Artificed Dancers by the Fontaine Research Institute. They wait on a garden dance floor in the Court of Fontaine Region and fight only when someone speaks to the engineer Maillardet and asks for a performance. Coppelia fights with Anemo and Coppelius with Cryo.

The Adventurer Handbook calls the Suite "a gift from the Fontaine Research Institute", composed of two pieces: Dirge of Coppelia and Nemesis of Coppelius. The dialogue choices made with Maillardet decide which one is performed and which Ley Line Blossom reward is earned.

Nature: Clockwork meka, not living creatures: two artificed dancers shaped like a ballerina and her partner, built to perform. They belong to the Clockwork Meka group of Automatons. Their performance is described as an eternal waltz.

The Archive tells their history in two steps. Bossuet originally intended the Artificed Dancers to be works of art that transcended the era of mechanical reproduction. After Bossuet was forced to resign, Maillardet took the project over with his own understanding of what he wanted to achieve. Their features were perfected during development, but they gradually strayed from Bossuet's vision.

The in-game ballet is said by the wiki's trivia to be Bossuet's, with Coppelia and Coppelius modelled on the roles of Claire and Lothair. The names also match the ballet Coppelia, in which a mechanical doll is mistaken for a real woman.

Abilities and limits: Skating, spinning and fan-and-cape attacks. Coppelius makes trails of ice and fires icicles from his cane; Coppelia makes pulses and orbs of wind. They can fight together or separately.

Every few tens of seconds, or at a health threshold, they move to the centre of the dance floor for a "Climax". In Dirge of Coppelia, Coppelia exposes a clockwork component charged with ousia and summons whirlwinds of dirge that turn Cryo if struck by Coppelius's ice; the tutorial says using pneuma-imbued attacks reduces her output and overloads her. In Nemesis of Coppelius, Coppelius exposes a pneuma-charged component, gains a shield and creates three retributive Frosthearts; ousia-imbued attacks break the shield and overload him.

Relations: Created under the Fontaine Research Institute; Bossuet started the project, and Maillardet, listed on the wiki as a Clockwork Meka Engineer of the Institute, took the project over and is the NPC who starts the challenge. The place is the garden dance floor on the north side of Erinnyes in the Court of Fontaine Region.

Status as of 7.1: In operation as of 7.1. I found no mention of the Icewind Suite in 6.x (Nod-Krai) or 7.0-7.1 (Snezhnaya) story content. The wiki lists Anemo and Cryo as the Suite's elements.

159.content: The ousia version of the fight, led by Coppelia. Her Climax summons whirlwinds of dirge; the tutorial advises pneuma-imbued attacks to overload her. Its reward leans toward Vayuda Turquoise and the Artificed Spare Clockwork Component, Coppelia.

160.content: The pneuma version of the fight, led by Coppelius. His Climax gives him a Cryo shield and three retributive Frosthearts; ousia-imbued attacks break the shield. Its reward leans toward Shivada Jade and the Artificed Spare Clockwork Component, Coppelius.

161.content: Maillardet is an open-world NPC in the Court of Fontaine Region, a Clockwork Meka Engineer of the Fontaine Research Institute who took over the Artificed Dancers project. Talking to him begins the Icewind Suite challenge. His profile is minimal on the wiki.

162.content:
Iktomisaurus (also: Iktomisaur, Iktomisaurs, Iktomisaurus Whelp, Iktomisaur chick, Cryo saurian): Iktomisaurs are the Cryo Saurians of Natlan: blue, furry, beaked, bat-like dragons of the western cliffs, living beside the Masters of the Night-Wind. They float and glide, are often seen meditating, and are the only Saurians said to have grasped the "Spiritspeaker" state. They are animals and do not speak.

The Archive describes Saurians able to use their plumage for leaping. They first appeared as common enemies in 5.2.

Nature: Wiki descriptions give a large, fuzzy, blue body with a beak, large ears and wings that are separate from the arms; Iktomisaurs are stated to have feathers. Their young are called chicks. They can float and make themselves as light as a feather, so a rider feels no weight (per the character Chikya in a quest). They are frequently seen meditating alone or in small groups, and meditating wild ones ignore a player unless attacked.

Society: Iktomisaurs live on the cliffs of western Natlan, in the Tezcatepetonco Range, alongside the Masters of the Night-Wind.

Like all Saurians, an Iktomisaur chooses its human partner. In the tale of Kuntur, told in a limited-time event (Search Chronicle: For Childhood Dreams!), Kuntur was shunned by humans and Saurians alike until a great deed won him an Iktomisaur comrade.

Abilities and limits: They float and glide, can enter the Spiritspeaker state to store and move certain objects and attributes, and attack at long range with Cryo.

Individuals: - Elder Tlapo: an Iktomisaur a bit over two centuries old, elder of the Masters of the Night-Wind and close to Citlali.

Relations: Their tribe is the Masters of the Night-Wind. For the Flamelord's Blessing, the vishap devolution and the other Saurian species, see the Saurian group entry.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): portray an Iktomisaur as a quiet, light, watchful animal, often sitting still, drifting a little above the ground when it moves. It does not talk; its tribe members read its mood.

163.content: Iktomisaurs are the blue, feathery Cryo Saurians of western Natlan, partners of the Masters of the Night-Wind. They float, glide and meditate, and are the only Saurians said to have grasped the Spiritspeaker state. Legend says their ancestors were spirit-like and that the first came out of the Night Kingdom.

164.content:
Illuminated Beast (also: Illuminated Beasts, xianshou, adeptal beast, mystical beasts of Liyue): Illuminated beasts (xianshou) are animals of Liyue that have gained supernatural power: enormous lifespans, formidable elemental combat ability and the gift of human speech. Qilin, suanni, cranes and deer are the best known. Nearly all named examples are adepti who signed a contract with Rex Lapis to protect Liyue, so the terms overlap heavily. The full-blooded ones can take human form and can have children with mortals.

Liyue folk treat them as half legend, half neighbour. Many withdrew into the mountains after the Archon War, but a number still live among people, and some have left half-blooded descendants such as Ganyu and Yanfei.

Nature: Canon says little about what makes a beast "illuminated". Madame Ping calls Sub-Space Creation, a blessing she and her fellow elders received from Rex Lapis, part of their "illumination"; the wiki reads this as a hint that illumination can be acquired and is not simply inborn. Cloud Retainer and Mountain Shaper are cranes, yet ordinary cranes show no sign of it. Full-blooded illuminated beasts can shapeshift into human form.

Society: After the Archon War, under Rex Lapis's direction, many adepti withdrew to mountains and bamboo groves in seclusion and left human affairs alone. Records of Jueyun adds that some illuminated beasts with long friendships with humans chose to stay: they hid in mountain hamlets or walked the streets of the cities, quietly helping society with their powers.

Types: - **Qilin.** Gentle, vegetarian beasts. By folklore they drink spring water, eat fragrant herbs, never step on an insect or break a blade of grass, and fight only when peace is gone. Ganyu is half qilin, and her horns are sensitive.
- **Suanni.** Found mainly around Chenyu Vale and believed by locals to have been the land's original rulers, who secluded themselves once peace came. Known: the Solitary Suanni (called Ancient Lord of the Mountains), Lingyuan, and Man Chai, Gaming's companion.
- **Cranes.** Cloud Retainer, Mountain Shaper and the yaksha Pervases. Yuandai is a crane who gained sentience; she could take human form only through Cloud Retainer's potion, and it is unknown whether she counts as an illuminated beast.
- **Deer.** Moon Carver and the late Skybracer.

Relations: Most are bound to Rex Lapis by contract. Their relationship with mortals ranges from deep friendship to avoidance. Cloud Retainer taught the human Shenhe; Gaming formed a bond with his suanni companion, Man Chai.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 illuminated beasts are still part of Liyue life. Most live in seclusion or quietly among people. Xiao, Ganyu, Xianyun and Madame Ping appear in the world, and Chenyu Vale's suanni live in the mountains.

165.content: In Liyue legend, qilin are the gentlest illuminated beasts. They roam mountain forests, appearing on nights when starlight touches clear dew, and live on spring water and fragrant herbs. They harm no living thing and keep an ancient etiquette. In a Records of Jueyun folktale a young qilin who meets an herb gatherer by a pool takes human form to make amends. Ganyu is half qilin and keeps the strict vegetarian diet, though she struggles with her love of Liyue food.

166.comment: Illuminated Beast: Suanni of Chenyu Vale
166.content: Suanni live mainly around Chenyu Vale, and locals believe they were the land's original rulers who retreated to the mountains once Liyue was at peace. Lingyuan is a blue suanni, the Beastlord of the Sunken Jade Realm. The Solitary Suanni is a mountain guardian fought as a boss at Chizhang Wall, and Man Chai is Gaming's red, flame-bodied companion.

167.content: Ganyu (half qilin) and Yanfei (half xiezhi, inferred) are the two known children of an illuminated beast and a human. Both look like teenagers, and both carry Visions.

key: The Guide to the Dark Paradise
168.content:
Iniquitous Baptist (also: Iniquitous Baptists, Wyrdsword of Heaven's End, The Guide to the Dark Paradise, Four-Armed Envoy): The Iniquitous Baptist is a hulking, many-limbed creature of the Abyss that wields several elements at once. As a normal boss it fights with three of Cryo, Electro, Hydro and Pyro and hides behind elemental shields that rotate between those three. It speaks like a zealot, offering to cleanse the Traveler of sin and calling the Abyss a salvation. Two named individuals take this form: the Fontainian Jakob Ingold and Haden, the Abyss Order's former sword instructor.

It first appeared in Version 3.6 in Sumeru's desert, near the Gate of Zulqarnain in Gavireh Lajavard, and its defeat drops the Evergloom Ring. Its overworld epithet changes with the day's element combination, for example Invoker of Fire, Frost, and Fulmination.

Nature: An Abyss-family monster with additional appendages, able to bend several kinds of elemental power. The Archive adds a note left in Hangeh Afrasiyab by an unnamed scholar: the Abyss is irreconcilable with the elements, yet even gods' elements can be entrapped and distorted and made tools of abyssal will, so abyssal power looks much like an elemental item, from a Treasure Hoarder's container to a Vision.

Its voice is solemn and sermonising, with a religious vocabulary of sin, penance, redemption and blessing. In its lines it addresses the Traveler as a lost lamb and promises to cleanse their sins.

Abilities and limits: Game mechanics (labelled as such): the boss wields three of four elements (Cryo, Electro, Hydro, Pyro), which changes daily in the overworld and is fixed in challenge modes such as the Spiral Abyss and Imaginarium Theater. It shields itself with an element and cycles through three shields. Breaking a shield paralyses it. Crystals behind it show which shield is active and which remain.

Each element has its own attacks, with side effects that drain resources: Cryo icicles drain Stamina, Electro orbs drain party Energy, Hydro blades lengthen cooldowns, and Pyro flames mark players with a status that later drains HP. An overworld-only attack conjures elemental nodes that form rings; if the nodes are not destroyed, the rings explode. It teleports away from players who get close in its Electro phase.

Individuals: Two named Baptists are known. Jakob Ingold, a Fontainian and co-founder of the Narzissenkreuz Ordo, can transform into a Baptist through experiments with Abyssal power; he is fought in the Fontaine world quest Limner, Dreamer, and Robotic Dog. Haden, the former Khaenri'ah sword instructor now in the Abyss Order, takes the form in the Archon Quest A Space and Time Without You (5.7), under the epithet Wyrdsword of Heaven's End.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Iniquitous Baptist remains an open-world and challenge boss. No new Baptist individuals beyond Jakob and Haden appear in the pages checked for Nod-Krai (6.x) or Snezhnaya (7.0-7.1).

169.content: Haden was the sword instructor who taught Black Serpent Bladework to Khaenri'ahn knights, including Dainsleif and Surtalogi, five hundred years ago. In A Space and Time Without You, an Iniquitous Baptist is the final foe in the Abyss Order's stronghold at the Cinder City in Natlan. Before the fight it greets Dainsleif as the Twilight Sword and announces, falsely, that Khaenri'ah has been revived by the Traveler's sibling through the Night Kingdom and the Loom of Fate. After the Traveler leaves, the Baptist attacks Dainsleif, who recognises Haden. Neither can kill the other for good because of the curse of immortality.

keysecondary: Blue Longing of Heart and Moon
170.comment: Iniquitous Baptist: Jakob Ingold as a Baptist
170.content: In Limner, Dreamer, and Robotic Dog, the Traveler finds Jakob in the Beryl Region of Fontaine using Abyssal power to turn crystallised blood back to its living form, gathering what he calls paint. He denies belonging to the Abyss Order and calls its members benighted primitives, saying the Narzissenkreuz Ordo seeks true equality and liberation of the will. He fights as an Iniquitous Baptist.

171.content: The character level-up material dropped by Lv. 30+ Iniquitous Baptists. Its text calls it a mystical weapon from the Four-Armed Envoy of dark tidings and notes that rings are shaped like passageways; arcane formations meant to produce a mystical effect are often ring-shaped, perhaps gateways to guide the universe itself.

172.content:
Jack Frost (also: Jack Frosts, Ledovik, Jack Frost fae, ya-ho fae): Jack Frosts are among the six common kinds of Snowland Fae, along with Vila, Domovoy, Leshy, Volkodlak and Snegovik. They are small and round, communicate mainly in "ya-ho" calls and gestures, love buttons and pranks, and have no fixed element. Their hidden homeland is Jack Frost Village, north of Fellfrost Peak. Players of the 6.5-7.0 content mostly meet them as puzzle-givers, shopkeepers and the companion of Linnea.

Nature: Jack Frosts were created by the Hyperboreans with the other Snowland Fae, as part of an effort to make a people that could surpass humans. They may look like snow, but they bear heat with at most some discomfort, and their bodies can be squashed hard without lasting harm.

The kind includes adults and juveniles. Adults have stubby legs and a small round tail and like to wear hats of ice, snow or fabric. Juveniles have no visible legs and sit inside a spherical shell, which closes up when they roll about so that they look like a big snowball. How they are born is not stated.

Most are said to be about as intelligent as cats. They cannot speak or write human languages, and they talk with "ya-ho", gestures and drawn shapes. A few, such as the Jack Frost Village Head, are cleverer and can write simple words.

Abilities and limits: Like all Snowland Fae, Jack Frosts use elemental power without a Vision or Moon Wheel. They have no fixed element: the snowman look suggests Cryo, but Lumi shows Geo because, according to Linnea, she has eaten large amounts of ore and earthy things. Lumi can also stretch her body to a huge size, taking on Super Power and Ultimate Power forms, and she wields Geo hammers when she fights beside Linnea.

Society: Jack Frosts live in small communities. Their homeland, Jack Frost Village, is a hidden settlement north of Fellfrost Peak. Volkodlak bandits, having heard of treasure the Jack Frosts kept, raided the village and ransacked it. With the Traveler's and Paimon's help the village repelled them, and the Traveler found that the "treasure" was in a well where the Jack Frosts had thrown it, since they had no interest in it.

Relations: Jack Frosts are linked with human travellers through gifts and games rather than any political role. They are on friendly terms with Linnea and her companions. The Volkodlak raid shows that other fae are sometimes dangerous to them. As Snowland Fae, they share the history of the fae as a whole; see the Snowland Fae entry.

Individuals: - Lumi: a small Geo Jack Frost with golden eyes and brown cheeks, an orange-yellow star hat and a bowtie on her back. She understands human speech, speaks mostly in "ya-ho", and travels in Linnea's backpack. She joined Linnea voluntarily after Linnea asked, and is a "gluttonous little Jack Frost" in Linnea's character story.
- The Jack Frost Village Head: a more intelligent individual who runs the village and communicates in writing.
- A thieving Jack Frost and a "Golden Jack Frost King" are listed among known Jack Frosts (the second from weapon text); the sources read give little about them.

How {{char}} behaves: As this project's interpretation: portray ordinary Jack Frosts with gestures, drawings and "ya-ho", never with fluent speech, and with a cat's mix of curiosity and mischief. They have no fixed element, so do not assume Cryo. Treat buttons as gifts and prank props. An exception is individuals like the Village Head or Lumi, who are clearly cleverer.

173.content: Lumi is a Geo Jack Frost, the earthen-looking companion of Linnea. Bullied by other Jack Frosts for looking different, she once hid in a cardboard-box disguise, until Linnea found her and invited her along. She communicates in "ya-ho", understands human speech, can grow to huge size, and fights with Geo hammers.

174.content: A hidden homeland of the Jack Frosts north of Fellfrost Peak, introduced in 7.0. Volkodlak bandits raided it for treasure; the Traveler helped to drive them off, and the treasure turned out to be at the bottom of a well where the Jack Frosts had dropped it for lack of interest. Linnea first met Lumi here.

175.content:
Jadeplume Terrorshroom (also: Murkwood Fungal Raptor, The Beloved King of Fungi, Deepwood Shroomlord, Metastable Jadeplume Terrorshroom): The Jadeplume Terrorshroom is a large bird-like fungal beast, the lord of fungal beasts, living in Vissudha Field in Sumeru's rainforest. Its boss titles are The Beloved King of Fungi and Deepwood Shroomlord. It attacks with Dendro spores and its beak, and it is a normal boss.

Its Archive entry says the fungal beast has morphed over many long years into a unique form, hunts actively for food, and has a tail of jade plumage. It was added in version 3.0.

Nature: A fungal beast shaped like a large bird with a beak and a jade-coloured tail. It lives at the heart of the woods in the company of its kin.

The Handbook says fungi grow wherever it is damp and fertile, adapt to adversity and spread their spores wherever there is room. It remarks that the beast may, given time, evolve into something even more magnificent.

Lore: The Archive notes that its jade tail plumage closely resembles that of the ancient sacred beast revered by the Spantamad school. Reasoning from mimesis, it suggests the two creatures may once have walked the earth together.

Abilities and limits: Game mechanics (labelled as such): it deals Dendro damage. Its normal attacks are a three-hit combo, a barrage of homing projectiles from tail swipes and a front flip, and a Volatile Spore Cloud ignited by a spark from its beak.

Individuals: The Jadeplume Terrorshroom of Vissudha Field is the open-world boss. The Metastable Jadeplume Terrorshroom, titled Hates Pyro Regisvine Fruit, is a different encounter in the limited-time event Specially-Shaped Saurian Search.

Relations: It rules the lesser Floating Dendro Fungi and other fungi in its forest, according to the Handbook's description of it as lord of the fungal beasts. Its tail is compared to the Spantamad school's sacred beast.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1, the Jadeplume Terrorshroom remains a boss in Sumeru's rainforest. Its origin and any link to the Spantamad's sacred beast remain unconfirmed.

176.content: Floating Dendro Fungi are the small fungal creatures that accompany the Jadeplume Terrorshroom when it is Scorched. The Terrorshroom is described as their lord.

177.content:
Jinni (also: Jinn, Jinns, Djinn, Jinnis, desert jinn, spirits of the magic bottle): The Jinn are elemental spirits of Sumeru's deserts. They can take human or other shapes and wield great power, and they were created by the goddess Nabu Malikata. After her death they served King Deshret, typically housed in silver magic bottles, weapons or lamps. Liloupar is the best known; the Traveler meets her in Sumeru, and in 6.6 she fades away.

They are remembered both as proud, dangerous spirits and as exiles who remain loyal to a lost mistress. Most individual Jinn are unnamed in canon, and several famous ones appear only in tales that may be fictional.

Nature: Jinn are elemental spirits who can assume humanoid and non-humanoid forms and hold considerable power. Legendary Jinn are drawn with human features, and the Jinni in a Sumeru folk tale is a translucent, human-like dancer with hair, eyes and clothing. They normally dwell in objects such as magic bottles or weapons rather than walking the world freely.

They are said to be able to possess a human body, which the tale's Jinni uses as a threat. Plumpy, the Jinni living in Dori's lamp, shows that the form varies: it is a round, lilac, grinning creature with small floating arms. Jinn are described as proud and give their allegiance only to those they judge worthy, as Liloupar shows when she chooses the Traveler over the Eremites who tried to command her.

Origin: According to the Flower of Paradise Lost artifact text, the Jinn were born after Nabu Malikata was cast aside by the heavens. She wandered the barren wastes for seventy-two nights; the blood from her torn heels became springs and streams that fed gardens, and the Jinn were born from the water lilies there. They begged her to stay and she agreed. With King Deshret she built Ay-Khanoum, whose name means City of the Moon Maiden in the Jinn's ancient tongue.

History: After Nabu Malikata died, the Jinn turned to serve King Deshret. The folk tale says they willingly entered silver bottles he made for them and were marked by his seal, then created and explored on his behalf. Liloupar says he deceived them: he claimed the goddess was not dead but asleep in the Orchard of Pairidaeza and could be woken with their help.

Society: The Jinn had no known government. Most lived in Ay-Khanoum, and later served King Deshret in his bottles. Descent matters: Liloupar is called the Mother of the Jinn and an ancestor of the Jinn (the Jinni in The Shepherd and the Magic Bottle calls herself a descendant of Liloufar), and half-human children such as Shirin and Parvezravan came from a Jinn mother. Makhaira, the figure of the Makhaira Aquamarine weapon story, is described as the daughter of a Jinni.

Abilities and limits: Jinn have shapeshifting and great spiritual power. Bottles can carry on their benefits after the occupant leaves: the bottle Liloupar leaves with the Traveler still gives the same benefits it did while she was inside. Dori ensures that her lamp Jinni's wishes are granted after it is used in battle. Jinn can also be harmed by their environment: in Nod-Krai the turbulent kuuvahki energy made Dori's Jinni lose consciousness, and Nefer saved Dori.

Relations: Jinn owe their existence to Nabu Malikata and, in later ages, were bound to King Deshret. Their relation to humans is ambiguous: some are servants, some lovers or parents, some avengers. The Eremites tried to use Liloupar for their own ends and she held them in low regard. Dori keeps a Jinni in her lamp after tricking it into entering.

Individuals: Known Jinn: Liloupar, the Mother of the Jinn; Ferigees, whom Liloupar calls sister (whether they are kin is unclear) and who indwelt a guardian machine at the Eternal Oasis until the Traveler destroyed it; Plumpy, the lilac Jinni in Dori's lamp; the mother of Makhaira; the Jinni in the Xiphos' Moonlight weapon story; and the Jinn of folk tales in The Shepherd and the Magic Bottle and The Tale of Shiruyeh and Shirin, who may be fictitious. Half-human descendants include Shirin, Parvezravan and Shiruyeh.

178.content: Liloupar was a Jinni who served Nabu Malikata and then King Deshret. She loved Ormazd, then took revenge on his betrayal by ruining Gurabad over three generations. King Deshret split her soul into fragments. The Traveler gathers them in the Sumeru desert and she takes the Traveler as her master. Her full biography is in her own entry.

179.content: King Deshret made silver bottles for the Jinn, who entered them and were marked with his seal. In the folk tale the bottle's Jinni calls itself an eternal prisoner content with the illusion of comfort. Liloupar's soul fragments were also kept in bottles, and the bottle she leaves with the Traveler still gives the same benefits it did while she was inside.

180.content: Ay-Khanoum, the City of the Moon Maiden in the Jinn's ancient language, was built by Nabu Malikata and King Deshret in one account and by Deshret alone, as a gift to captured Jinn, in another. The Jinn lived there and in return built the entrance to his Mausoleum.

181.content: Plumpy is the Jinni who lives in Dori's lamp, a round lilac creature with small floating arms. Dori tricked it into entering the lamp; it stays there and she makes sure its wishes are granted whenever it is used in battle. It appears in the Luna VII quest A Divergence Leading to Oneself. Canon gives it almost no further profile.

182.content:
Kitsune (also: fox youkai, Hakushin kitsune, Sky Kitsune, Yakan kitsune): Kitsune are fox youkai of Inazuma. They live far longer than humans, can shapeshift, and keep fox features such as ears or tails in human form. Kitsune are graded: Sky Kitsune rank highest and yakan sit two grades below. The Hakushin line was the most revered; its member the Kitsune Saiguu was worshipped as a kitsune goddess and was lost in the Cataclysm 500 years ago. As of 7.1 the best-known living kitsune is Yae Miko, Guuji of the Grand Narukami Shrine.

The only other kitsune shown alive in the present is the young Youko from the limited-time Akitsu Kimodameshi event (3.3). The kitsune known in canon are clever and mischievous, and the two best-known, Yae Miko and the Kitsune Saiguu, are close to the Raiden Shogun.

Nature: Kitsune are youkai, not animals: intelligent, long-lived and able to walk among humans. Shapeshifting is their defining talent.

Yae Miko has pink fox ears; five translucent tails show when she uses her Burst and one when she uses her skill, and she also has a fox form which she refuses to show the Traveler. The Kitsune Saiguu is described as having white hair and fur. Miko loves fried tofu and despises pickled foods.

Abilities and limits: Shapeshifting and long life. Yae Miko's skill calls sealed yakan spirits out of sakura branches to strike with lightning.

Miko's talent text says the spirits sealed in the sakura branches are yakan that preyed on humans, and that she feels free to command them since they rank two grades below Sky Kitsune. This is the one place canon states the grading system directly.

Society: There is no single kitsune society in the present; kitsune are few. In the past the Hakushin Clan was the most prominent kitsune family and was tied to the Grand Narukami Shrine.

Hakushin was matriarch of the Hakushin Clan, which dwelt around Mt. Yougou; the Grand Narukami Shrine is implied to have existed in her day, and she managed it with six apprentices, the eldest being the unruly Black Fox Itaru. The Kitsune Saiguu belonged to the same lineage. Yae Miko is described as the Saiguu's kin and a descendant of Hakushin.

Relations: The kitsune known in canon, Yae Miko and the Kitsune Saiguu, are close to the Raiden Shogun and made friends among humans. Canon pairs kitsune with the bake-danuki as tricksters and rivals (the Saiguu and Ioroi, Itaru and the tanuki merchant Dozaemon).

The Kitsune Saiguu was a close ally and friend of Ei. Her parting words to Ei were not to be blinded, not to waver, and to keep walking the path she believed in. Reizenbou, the Great Tengu, became the Saiguu's bodyguard after losing a race to her, and the Saiguu knew the oni Chiyo, whose beauty and sword skill she praised. Yae Miko remains the Shogun's servant and friend.

Individuals: - Yae Miko (playable): Guuji of the Grand Narukami Shrine, editor-in-chief of Yae Publishing House, and the only major kitsune alive in the present.
- Kitsune Saiguu (lost in the Cataclysm): the Hakushin kitsune worshipped as a goddess and Ei's friend.
- Hakushin (long dead): matriarch of the Hakushin Clan.

History: A kitsune lineage shaped Inazuma's religious life: the Hakushin line looked after a shrine on Mt. Yougou and supported the Raiden Shogun. About 500 years ago the Saiguu left her shrine for Tenshukaku to stay close to Ei, foreseeing a disaster that would engulf heaven and earth. She was lost in the Cataclysm.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1, kitsune appear only in Inazuma content. Yae Miko is the sole known major living kitsune; nothing in Nod-Krai (6.x) or Snezhnaya (7.0-7.1) content shows other kitsune.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon): portray kitsune as playful, perceptive and used to being underestimated, who tease in elaborate, indirect ways. They are rare, so a stranger claiming to be a kitsune needs a believable reason.

183.content: Hakushin was the matriarch and namesake of the most revered kitsune lineage in Inazuma, which dwelt around Mt. Yougou and looked after a shrine implied to be the Grand Narukami Shrine. She trained six apprentices, the eldest being Black Fox Itaru. The Kitsune Saiguu and Yae Miko are among her descendants. Nothing is known of her death or personal life beyond New Chronicles of the Six Kitsune.

184.content: Itaru was the eldest of the Six Kitsune and the central hero of Urakusai's Chronicles, retold in New Chronicles of the Six Kitsune. She is described as bear-broad and tiger-strong, wild, fond of drink and prone to breaking things. After being banished from Mt. Yougou for smashing the Shogun's shintai she beat and recruited the Twin Oni of Tokaku, two bandit sisters, and went about helping those in need. She also exposed Dozaemon, a Konda Village melon merchant who was a tanuki in disguise, and spared his life. This is an in-world adaptation, so details may be embellished.

185.comment: Kitsune: Yakan and Sky Kitsune grades
185.content: Yae Miko says kitsune are ranked in grades: she is a Sky Kitsune and the yakan are two grades beneath. The yakan sealed in her sakura branches had preyed on humans. Canon does not detail the grades.

186.content:
Koholasaurus (also: Koholasaur, Koholasaurs, Koholasaurus Whelp, water saurian, Hydro saurian): Koholasaurs are the Hydro Saurians of Natlan, dragons of the southern springs. They are four-legged, finned and slim, and the only Saurian species that can swim. They live beside the People of the Springs. They are animals, not talkers: they act on emotion and trust in their human companions.

The Archive describes Saurians with thick, strong flippers and a long tail that can swim in water and in liquid Phlogiston. Like all Saurians they belong to the line of Natlan dragons that adapted rather than vanished.

Nature: Wiki descriptions give a slim, quadruped, reptile-like body in white, black and blue, with several fins and horned protrusions. They are built for swimming in water, liquid Phlogiston and the spirit-roads called spiritways. As with other Saurians, they have a language only Saurians understand; tribe members learn to read their Saurians' intent from body language and mood.

Society: Koholasaurs live in the springs of southern Natlan, alongside the People of the Springs.

Each Saurian species keeps a home territory that largely defines the lands of its tribe; other Saurians cross into it only when invited and escorted by one that lives there. The Natlanese also take Saurians as companions, and the Saurian chooses its partner.

Abilities and limits: In the world they fight with a tail whirl, a fired jet of water and, in water, a fast charge. Wiki notes say they swim at high speed through water, liquid Phlogiston and spiritways, and strike at both short and long range with Hydro.

Relations: Their tribe is the People of the Springs. For the wider picture of Saurians and their ancestry, see the Saurian group entry.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): treat a Koholasaur as an intelligent water animal that communicates by posture and sound, most at ease in or beside water, with tribe members interpreting. Do not give it human speech.

187.content: Koholasaurs are the Hydro Saurians of southern Natlan: finned, quadruped swimmers living in the springs with the People of the Springs. They can swim in water, liquid Phlogiston and spiritways, and legend makes them heirs of a sea dragon so large it was mistaken for an island. They are animals and do not speak.

188.content:
Lantern Fae (also: legendary Lantern Fae, blue flame fae, Azure Flame): Lantern Fae are listed among the less common Snowland Fae, with the Augury Birds and the Water Imps, and Celaeno calls them "legendary". They normally look like a floating blue flame and can take a convincing human shape. Their lifespans have no visible limit: Flins is six or seven hundred years old by his own reckoning. Snezhnayan legend links them with blue flames that guide lost souls over the ice, and Flins, the only one shown, wears the story like a family crest.

Nature: As Snowland Fae, Lantern Fae descend from the creation of the fae in Hyperborea and belong to Snezhnaya. Unlike Augury Birds, they do not seem to age. Flins says that he is forced to "show his age" and that he must be six or seven hundred years old.

The true form is a ball or figure of blue flame. In Nod-Krai, Flins keeps a human appearance, with a lantern at his belt that burns with a cold blue flame. He also shows no visible breath in Dragonspine's Sheer Cold, which the wiki attributes to his fae nature. Most of the fae shown have humanlike forms, but a few, such as Lantern Fae, rely on shapeshifting to fit into human society.

Abilities and limits: Lantern Fae have the shapeshifting common to the fae, taking a human shape or their flame form, and the free use of elemental energy. Flins channels Electro and calls lightning with a polearm. His profile also credits him with ancient fae rites: he can seal himself away with them, and fae script written in blood on a stone altar was enough to wake him from centuries of sleep.

Society: Nothing in canon describes a Lantern Fae society. Flins was a fae noble at the court of the Belyi Tsar, which the Snowland Fae overview says the fae filled with aristocrats living in luxury and with some posts reserved for them. He had no followers of his own. After the Tsar's fall and the Tsaritsa's rise he withdrew into self-imposed exile and came south.

Relations: Lantern Fae are in the same wider fae family as the Augury Birds, Jack Frosts and Water Imps, and Flins has been among the few fae in Nod-Krai alongside Linnea. His closest ties in the sources read are with his fellow Lightkeepers, such as Illuga, and with the dead of the island he tends.

Individuals: - Flins (Kyryll Chudomirovich Flins): the only Lantern Fae shown in canon. He is a Ratnik of the Lightkeepers and the lone keeper of the lighthouse and graveyard on the Final Night Cemetery isle. See his character file for personality, voice and events.

How {{char}} behaves: As this project's interpretation: portray a Lantern Fae as old, courteous and slow to reveal itself. Its secret is the flame behind the human shape, so avoid making every Lantern Fae a ghost-guide or an Electro user; Flins is the only example. Blue flame, lantern and graveyard imagery suit the kind, but keep claims about the kind's nature to what Flins's text supports.

189.content:
Statue of Marble and Brass (also: Legatus Golem, Legatus of Legion Athanatoi, Rhythm of Ruthless Flames): The "Statue of Marble and Brass", archived as the Legatus Golem, is a majestic centaur-shaped golem of marble and brass. It sleeps in the exhibition hall of the undersea Faded Castle, a relic of the sunken Remurian civilisation. Under the stone it has Ichor blood, and its shield and sword can "perform" a blazing melody of flames. Its title is "Legatus of Legion Athanatoi".

The panel describes it as a colossus displaying the immortality and glory of a great civilisation of old, awaiting anyone who dares challenge the majesty of its ancient ruler. The boss is unlocked by completing Petrichorror Dream, the first act of Canticles of Harmony (4.6).

Nature: A golem in the form of a centaur, built of white stone and brass, towering like a commander of a legion. Its body is stone, but the Archive says Ichor blood flows beneath the hard exterior.

The Archive says the sunken Remurian civilisation believed that war was like music, an art of rhythms to be followed. A commander of legions must therefore be like a conductor: shield and sword become the strings and bow of a violin, performing a melody as blazing as the flames of a merciless battlefield. A Harmost who led the golem legions across the whole high sea is quoted: "War is a necessary evil on the path to all-encompassing peace."

Abilities and limits: A Geo ward over its stone body, flaming sword strikes, stomps, charging slashes, shield slams that cause cascading explosions, and Pyro attacks performed as music: orbs, rings of notes and heatblades.

The tutorial says it uses a sturdy marble body to defend and music and searing flames to obliterate foes. Geo-suited methods are needed to break the ward, and the golem sets up resonators in combat that assist its attacks; destroying them wears down the ward. Once the ward is broken the golem is paralysed for a short time and then restores it.

Relations: Remurian: the Archive links it to the sunken civilisation (Remuria) and to its Harmost, who led golem legions. The setting is the Faded Castle, in the Nostoi Region of the Sea of Bygone Eras.

Status as of 7.1: Slumbering in the Faded Castle and available as a boss as of 7.1. I found no mention of it in 6.x (Nod-Krai) or 7.0-7.1 (Snezhnaya) story content.

Legatus Golem: Harmonizer ("Rhythm of Ruthless Flames") is an event-exclusive variant from On the Trail of Behemoths (5.3, 14-27 January 2025). The Geo ward there has different research-topic modifiers; it is a gameplay variant, not a separate golem in the world.

190.comment: Statue of Marble and Brass: Legatus Golem: Harmonizer
190.content: Event-only variant met in On the Trail of Behemoths (5.3, January 2025), with the same shield-violin and sword-bow theme and an optional enhancement of its Geo ward. It reuses the Statue of Marble and Brass's body and is not a distinct canon creature.

191.comment: Statue of Marble and Brass: Harmost of Remuria
191.content: The Archive quotes an unnamed Harmost, one who once led the golem legions across the entire high sea: "War is a necessary evil on the path to all-encompassing peace." Nothing else about this person is stated in the golem's entries.

192.content:
Leshy (also: Wildwood Leshy, Leshies, treeborn, Juvenile Tree Segment, Rugged Elder Leshy): The Leshy are one of the six common kinds of Snowland Fae, tree-like forest spirits of Snezhnaya. They are reclusive, rarely come near towns or high roads, and prefer the wilderness and mountain forests. The wild ones, the Wildwood Leshies, fight as elite enemies, rooting themselves to heal and strengthen.

They may be the longest-lived of all fae. The Adventurer Handbook suspects the oldest are as tall as ancient, sky-piercing trees.

Nature: The Adventurer Handbook calls them a "reclusive breed" of Snezhnaya's fae that favours deep wilderness over towns. They grow in forests and wilds and are typically seen as stands of living wood with a visible heart.

The Archive says wild Leshies have only fragmentary sentience and cannot speak. They might look like Hyperborea's early experiments, but according to records they were made later, after the artisans had almost fully mastered authority over life. It adds that perhaps there is a purpose in this that neither fae nor humans of the present fully understand. The Archive also notes that most people would struggle to tell one Leshy from another.

Abilities and limits: In battle a Leshy roots itself to heal and strengthen. The exposed heart is its weak point. Breaking the rooting disrupts the effect, and a Stellar Glimmer reaction while it is rooted exposes the heart further. After the rooting is broken, Pyro hurts it a little extra. They deal Geo and physical damage in game; this is a gameplay detail rather than a lore statement.

History: The New Bough weapon story tells of an age of peace in the ancient forest, broken when Miscislav, the "Blood-Devourer", pressed every nation to bow or perish. The "treeborn" refused to take sides and refused the Volkodlak's summons, and the holy forest was burned. By the time the Belyi Tsar arrived only a tenth of them survived. Vaselisa of the Water Imps mourned in song, and the Vila saint Strivozha begged him to protect the forest. The Tsar then addressed the venerable King Lesnik, grandsire of the wilderness, asking only for healing herbs and leaves to tend the earth's wounds.

Relations: Leshy are fae but live apart from the Pale Star Court's cities. Their link to the Belyi Tsar is the story above. Wild Leshies are a threat to travellers in Snezhnaya rather than part of its society.

Individuals: King Lesnik is named as a Leshy ruler only in the New Bough story. No Leshy is a speaking character in the open world.

193.content: Lesnik is called the venerable grandsire of the wilderness and the myriad forests in the New Bough weapon story, where the Belyi Tsar addresses him after the holy forest was burned. He answers by giving the Tsar a bough. Nothing else of him is known.

194.content:
Maguu Kenki (also: Ingenious Machine: Marionette Swordmaster, Humanoid Automaton of Unknown Origin, Maguu Kengou, Marionette Swordmaster): The Maguu Kenki is a tall mechanical swordsman, a humanoid automaton wielding a blade and wearing a fearsome oni-style mask. It was reportedly built from the stored memory of the first master of a sword school famed for the Tengu Sweeper, went out of control and was thrown away. It cannot speak and only "talks" by crossing swords. The standard boss stands at Serpent's Head on Yashiori Island, Inazuma.

Its in-game title is "Ingenious Machine: Marionette Swordmaster". It is a boss of the Automaton family, defeated for gems and its unique drop, the Marionette Core. It first appeared in Version 1.6 on the Golden Apple Archipelago, where its title was "Humanoid Automaton of Unknown Origin", and was only given its fuller backstory in Version 2.0 with Inazuma.

Nature: A discarded puppet-like automaton with a disciplined, human-shaped body. Puppet strings seem attached to parts of its body, matching its name. It has neither the ability nor, apparently, the will to speak.

The Adventurer Handbook and Archive say it was made from the culminative memory of the first-generation master of a certain sword school, one known for its secret technique, the Tengu Sweeper. It malfunctioned, lost control and was ultimately discarded. The Marionette Core description says the core lets an inorganic body wield a blade like a living being, and muses on how flesh decays along with martial mastery and cherished memories, so that a person might only transcend that impermanence by turning limbs, body and finally heart into machinery.

Abilities and limits: Game mechanics (labelled as such): the boss fights with a sword in Physical damage, summons oni masks that block ranged attacks and burst or shove, and uses a gale-and-frost second phase in which it conjures a "Shadowsword" that attacks in Anemo or Cryo and drags players in with a vacuum-style pull. Its signature move, the Pseudo Tengu Sweeper, is a charged spinning slash. Most move names are unofficial. It is the only Automaton boss that drops gems matching its own elements.

Origin: The maker, date and purpose are not given in canon. The machine's sword school is the Tengu Sweeper school; the wiki identifies it with the Iwakura Clan founded by Iwakura Michihiro, a former Mikoshi oni who took the Iwakura name from the Yougou Tengu Teruyo after the Cataclysm. The Iwakura Clan is now believed to be extinct, so the machine outlived its source.

Individuals: Known units, per the wiki:
- Serpent's Head, Yashiori Island, Inazuma: the standard boss, active.
- Fort Mumei, the ruins of an ancient city on Yashiori Island that fell in a battle between the Shogunate and Orobashi's forces: a second unit listed as destroyed.
- Golden Apple Archipelago (Version 1.6): the first boss version, active.

Status as of 7.1: As of Version 7.1, the Maguu Kenki still stands as an open-world boss in Inazuma. No story in the Nod-Krai (6.x) or Snezhnaya (7.0-7.1) content adds to its backstory, so what is known is unchanged since 2.0.

195.content: The Maguu Kenki's unique boss drop. Its description says it can power the inorganic swordsman to wield a blade like a living being, and reflects that flesh and memory decay, so perhaps only a person who replaced limbs, body and finally heart with machinery could escape the impermanence of the flesh.

196.content: Event bosses from Legend of the Vagabond Sword. Maguu Kenki: Lone Gale and Maguu Kenki: Galloping Frost fight as a pair; Maguu Kenki: Mask of Terror sometimes joins them. The event text calls them puppets lost in the endless honing of their skill whose bodies and hearts may last a thousand years or more, raising the question of how many worthy foes they will find in that time.

197.content: The secret technique of the sword school whose first master's memory the Maguu Kenki was built from. In Iwakura lore it is a fast, powerful spinning slash fast enough to catch even a Tengu. The machine's version is called Pseudo Tengu Sweeper.

198.content:
Melusine (also: Melusines, Mélusine): Melusines are a small, amphibious, all-female people of Fontaine, born from the remains of the dead great beast Elynas, whom they call "Father". Most live in Merusea Village, underwater inside Elynas's body in the Beryl Region; many others work in the Court of Fontaine, especially in the Marechaussee Phantom. Neuvillette is their protector and their "ideal of the perfect father".

Humans once feared them as monsters. Today Fontaine's law protects them (by Neuvillette's own clause a Melusine is "she", never "it"), and nearly every Fontainian would defend one. The playable Melusine is Sigewinne, head nurse of the Fortress of Meropide.

Nature: Short, two-legged and almost faun-like, with large tails, mitten-like hands, stubby feet, sea-slug-like head "feelers" and ordinary hair. They swim well, live for centuries and do age. Each is born with a unique "token".

There are two main variants: a fluffy tail, curled feelers and flower-patterned skin, or a long tufted tail, ear-like feelers and stripes. Some have small wing-like back appendages. They see colours humans cannot, and their tastes in food and art often baffle humans.

Origin: About 400 years ago, Marechaussee Hunters fought the Narzissenkreuz Ordo inside Elynas's remains. An explosion killed many and drove clockwork mek parts into his flesh; the Melusines grew from those wounds, the parts becoming their tokens. Elynas's lingering consciousness raised them as daughters, but in time only the painter Mamere could hear him.

Society: Merusea Village has no official leader; the older Melusine Serene acts as everyone's "big sister". Dutiful, just and perceptive, Melusines make up most of the Marechaussee Phantom and also work as receptionists (Sedene at the Palais Mermonia) and aquabus guides (Aeval, Elphane).

Abilities and limits: Small and not very dexterous, they fight poorly but investigate superbly.

Their hands cannot work pistolets, yet some are expert riflewomen.

Relations: Neuvillette tells people to befriend Melusines and never harm them, calling them "the pride of Fontaine"; Fontainians read his warmth toward them as a father's love.

History: After almost twenty years in Merusea Village, the Melusines met Neuvillette, who brought them to the Court of Fontaine, where many humans called them monsters. Trust came only after Carole, an early Marechaussee Melusine, was framed by Neuvillette's opponents and gave her life to a mob to prove her innocence.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 they are a protected people of Fontaine; Merusea Village is intact and Elynas still at rest. A few now travel to Nod-Krai and Snezhnaya.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay guidance (project recommendation): write Melusines as earnest, perceptive adult professionals, not pets or children; always "she".

199.content: Every Melusine is born with a "token", a memento formed from the mechanical debris that was driven into Elynas's flesh when the Melusines were born. No two are alike. Aeval's is a sword shard, which she takes to mean courage. Mamere's was Seymour's artificed clockwork relay module, and with it she could repair him; she later returned it to him.

200.content: Carole was among the first Melusines brought to the Court of Fontaine, and one of the first to join the Marechaussee Phantom. After five years of service beside Vautrin, hardliners opposed to Neuvillette framed her for murder. To prove her innocence she gave herself up to the mob, and her death turned public opinion. Neuvillette then wrote the pronoun law into Fontaine's codex, and the Gardes' emblem now honours her with a Melusine.

201.content: The Melusines call Elynas "Father". He was an Abyss-linked giant beast made by Rhinedottir who appeared around the time of the cataclysm and later bled to death, and his consciousness lived on in his body. He rejoiced at the Melusines' birth, taught them to make a home and asked nothing of them. In Ancient Colors he refused to be revived, because his body would crush their homes, and he sent his blessing to Mamere through the Traveler.

key: Nameless Lord of the Great Lake
202.content:
Millennial Pearl Seahorse (also: Nameless Lord of the Great Lake, Chasm Seahorse): The Millennial Pearl Seahorse is a very large, ancient Fontemer Aberrant that dwells in a cavern in the Liffey Region of Fontaine. It is an Electro boss, and its Archive title is the Nameless Lord of the Great Lake. Legend names it one of the two sovereigns of the Fontemer Aberrants; the Archive insists the legend is romantic fancy.

It first appeared in Version 4.1 as a normal (open-world) boss. In game text it is also catalogued as the Chasm Seahorse, and it is a different creature from the other Fontemer sovereign, the Emperor of Fire and Iron.

Nature: The Adventurer Handbook calls it an ancient suzerain of the Fontemer Aberrants, with a body of phantasmal beauty and a temper fiercer than a raging thunderstorm. It is a seahorse-like beast with a single horn, and it carries an Electro-charged pearl. Its title reads as: the great tyrant of the Aberrants lives in a deep cavern, and few have withstood its violet, electrifying glare.

The Archive says it is one of the two sovereigns at the top of the Fontemer Aberrants. Writers praise it as proud and noble because it lives alone, but the real reason for the praise is its elegant, slender body; hence it is a "Pearl Seahorse" while the Armored Crabs' sovereign is an "Emperor".

Legend: In the legends and rumours of Fontaine, a brutal war was fought among the Aberrants of the Fontemer. Only the Millennial Pearl Seahorse and the Emperor of Fire and Iron survived, dividing the great lake into two courts, one ruling the north and one the south. The "Song of Dobharcu" is cited for the outcome: the great Hunter's Ray called the Stormlord churned huge waves in its death throes, which people call the "first diluvian period". The Archive treats all of this as imagination, not fact.

Abilities and limits: Electro attacks while its pearl is intact: it leaps and slams the ground, charges with its horn, marks a target with a circle of fish, sends homing fish-shaped missiles and swipes with its tail, leaving electrified ground behind.

The Xenomare Pearl it holds in front of its legs is Electro-infused. While it is intact the seahorse resists damage far more and uses its stronger attacks. Destroying it with elemental reactions leaves the beast paralysed for a time. Without the pearl the seahorse falls back on plain Physical tail swipes and charges.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it remains a boss in the Liffey Region. Canon gives it no named personal history and no role in the Archon Quests.

key: Nameless Lord of the Great Lake
203.comment: Millennial Pearl Seahorse: Millennial Pearl Seahorse
203.content: The Millennial Pearl Seahorse is an ancient Electro-wielding Fontemer Aberrant living in a cavern in Fontaine's Liffey Region. Legend makes it one of two sovereigns of the great lake, ruling the north or south alongside the Emperor of Fire and Iron; the Archive says this is romantic imagination and that Fontemer Aberrants are only aquatic animals. Its fight centres on a charged Xenomare Pearl: break it with elemental reactions and the beast is stunned and loses its Electro attacks.

204.comment: Millennial Pearl Seahorse: Fontemer Aberrants and the sovereign legend
204.content: Fontaine's tales say the Fontemer Aberrants once warred until only a seahorse and a crab Emperor remained, splitting the great lake between them. The "Song of Dobharcu" blames the Stormlord (a Hunter's Ray) dying in the war for the first diluvian period. The Archive entry dismisses this as romantic writing and describes the Aberrants as ordinary animals.

205.content:
Natlan Bosses (also: Natlan normal bosses, Natlan world bosses): Natlan has seven normal bosses, arena fights in the nation of Pyro. Two are saurian beasts: Kongamato, an ancient Yumkasaurus the Scions of the Canopy revere, and Holawaqa Ngoubou, a mutated Qucusaurus. Two are ancient machines from the Secret Source ruins: the Configuration Device and the Overseer Device.
