282.content: Electro Seelie are the Inazuma variant. They move fast when approached, release a harmless Electro shockwave, and generate their own Court on arrival. Some act as puzzle guides that trace a path and vanish.

283.content: Luminous Seelie in the Chasm's Underground Mines recharge the Lumenstone Adjuvant and activate Lumentorches nearby. Loading-screen text says the Chasm's unique climate mutated them.

key: The Last Prince of the Sands
284.content:
Setekh Wenut (also: The Last Prince of the Sands, Lord of the Desert, Wenut: Abnormal Turbulence): The Setekh Wenut is a giant eyeless sandworm living in the Wenut Tunnels of the Desert of Hadramaveth, in Sumeru's Great Red Sand. It is a normal boss with the title The Last Prince of the Sands. It finds prey by sound and vibration and fights with Anemo blasts and by drilling out of the ground.

It is a Mystical Beast. Its Handbook entry says Wenut sometimes take on forms very like plants and that some call them descendants of the lord of plants, while others say the form is a lure for prey.

Nature: A huge blind predator of the deep desert, hunting through sound and vibration.

The Archive says these creatures came from deep within the Great Red Sand. A branch of their genus survived by adapting to earth-based living and became known as the Wenut. Some desert folk wrongly think sandworms are the last stage of a quicksand eel's life cycle, because the two behave similarly.

Lore: Legend says that in the ancient past, before time itself existed, these creatures lived with their progenitors and offspring in a land of verdant grass and colossal trees, moving through slick soil as fish do through water.

Abilities and limits: Game mechanics (labelled as such): its first phase uses a body sweep and Anemo spit; after a short opening (about 20 seconds, or the first sliver of its health) it switches to a drilling thrust from below, a Stream of Gales of Anemo projectiles, a Stormbreath sweep and a Pressurized Beam. It also digs out and back into the ground, exposing itself.

Individuals: The Setekh Wenut of the Wenut Tunnels is the open-world boss. Wenut: Abnormal Turbulence is an event-only enemy from the limited-time event Fulminating Sandstorm.

Relations: It is the boss form of the Wenut that threaten desert travellers, and is related in the Handbook's account to Apep, the lord of plants, by the claim that Wenut were once his scions.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1, the Setekh Wenut remains a boss in the Wenut Tunnels. Its ancient origin is known only as legend.

285.content: Wenut are giant sandworms of the Desert of Hadramaveth. They emerge from the ground in certain areas to attack travellers. The Setekh Wenut is the boss form.

286.content: Pseudo-Stamens are the exclusive drop of the Setekh Wenut.

287.content:
Slime (also: Slimes, Hydro Slime, Pyro Slime, Cryo Slime, Electro Slime, Anemo Slime, Geo Slime, Dendro Slime): Slimes are the most common Elemental Lifeforms. The Adventurer Handbook calls them pudgy elemental life forms and notes that desserts made from slimes of different elements are said to taste distinctly different. Each is made of a single element (Anemo, Cryo, Dendro, Electro, Geo, Hydro or Pyro), is immune to it, and keeps it applied to itself. Small slimes mainly bump into things; large slimes have a wider range of attacks, all including a leap and slam. Since 6.7 (Luna VIII) a unique Prism Slime lives in the Lunar Highlands of Nod-Krai.

Nature: Slimes, like other Elemental Lifeforms, are made of condensed elemental energy: the type determines the element and the concentration the size (per the Large Anemo Slime Archive entry). They are usually found in environments matching their element and tend to gather in groups. They must take in elemental energy to survive, so they are drawn to potent sources such as Mist Flower extract, which characters in some quests use as "Elemental Bait". The Loading Screen text calls them lowly life forms of minimal intelligence, and Breeze Amidst the Forest (vol. I) says life that arises from the elements either descends into a slime or ascends into a crystalfly.

Abilities and limits: Game mechanics, for reference: slimes are immune to their element and have it applied constantly. Small slimes primarily bump. Large slimes vary their attacks by element, and all share a leap-and-slam. In scene terms, a Pyro slime burns, a Cryo slime chills, an Anemo slime floats, an Electro slime shocks.

Relations: Humans use slimes experimentally: Garcia made a slime-based lubricant for his Numbering Machine, and Akim uses slime as a main ingredient of his clay-like building material "Concresoil". Amber uses Pyro Slime Condensate for her Baron Bunny, and the operators of the ruin-guard factory used Electro Slimes to power machinery. Hilichurls use small slimes to make explosive barrels, Cryo slimes to preserve food, and Large Anemo Slimes as cargo balloons; grenadiers and mitachurls throw slimes, and lawachurls throw larger ones, switching to smaller ones if their elemental shield is broken.

288.content: The Prism Slime (title "Creation's Afterglow") was added in version 6.7 as a Local Legend in the Lunar Highlands of Nod-Krai; reaching it requires finishing the Pioneers (Part 2) quest. It is the only slime not found in Teyvat proper. It adopts the element of whoever fights it, inhales the seven elemental slimes around it, and, once charged, swells into a light-gathering state. Its Valiant Chronicles description says that the first element was once scattered like light through a prism until the Creator separated it into seven forms, and that on this corner of the moon elemental forms from the mortal world can be steeped in flawless source-light to retrace their origins and return to the primordial unity, "perhaps by the same principle" as the primordial light said to reverse destruction.

289.content: Slimes need to extract elemental energy to survive and are irresistibly drawn to potent sources such as Mist Flower extract. Characters in the Darknight Hero's Alibi and Astrology and the 50-Year Pact quests use these as "Elemental Bait" to lure slimes.

290.content: Slime is sometimes used in cooking; the item text for Tasty Slime Condensate notes that slime-containing foods are usually passed off as agar-based because most people balk at eating it. Escoffier and Xiangling have both experimented with slime, and a "Salt and Pepper Slime" of Xiangling's inspired Kuki Shinobu's Roasted Lavender Melon (Shinobu's Character Story).

291.content: Hilichurls make explosive barrels from small slimes, keep food cold with Cryo slimes, ride Anemo slimes into the air, and carry cargo with Large Anemo Slimes used as balloons (as seen in the Dangerous Haul quest). In fights, grenadiers and mitachurls throw slimes; mitachurls infuse axes with Pyro or Electro slimes or build Dendro slime shields; lawachurls throw larger slimes and switch to smaller ones if their elemental shield is broken.

292.content:
Snegovik (also: Snegurochka, Snegurochka (female Snegovik), snow fae, Snow Maiden, Grand Duchess of the Snegurochka): The Snegovik, "snow fae", are one of the six common kinds of Snowland Fae. Their women are called Snegurochka. By several in-world accounts they were made for companionship and are born with incomplete souls, and only love for a human can make them whole. They live all over Snezhnaya, and their Grand Duchess traditionally resides at the House of Hesperides.

Male Snegovik are natural-born knights who forge weapons from ice and snow. Snegurochka are born ice-and-snow mages who can work Prime Ice. The Eye of Graeae cautions that the "made for love" idea is one research perspective, not established fact.

Nature: Snegovik are said to be created as servants or companions for the Hyperboreans. They are among the most numerous fae in Snezhnaya today and live across the whole nation.

Archive text on the Glaciomancer says their souls were incomplete when they were first made, and that only by falling in love with humans could they make themselves whole. The Eye of Graeae adds that, once a Snegovik is complete, the constraint on them is gone, which it offers as the reason tales of them so often turn cruel or cold, while a Snegovik who cannot find love suffers and dies. It stresses this is a research perspective and may not be true. The Archive wonders if a whole Snegovik still needs love, and notes that many love stories between Snegovik and humans end in tragedy.

Appearance: Snegovik are humanoid with pale skin, glowing ice-blue eyes and bluish-grey to white hair, and they bear blue crystalline markings on legs, faces, hair ends and necklines like other fae. Snegurochka have blue fingertips, often tear-shaped crystal marks on their faces, knee-length off-the-shoulder gowns in blue patterns and usually a kokoshnik headpiece. Male Snegovik are about twice human height, with blue crystal forming ears, a beard and a horn-like spike on the forehead, an ice-crystal gauntlet on the right forearm, quilted coats with fur collars and silver armour on the chest and left forearm.

Abilities and limits: Males are described as natural-born knights who forge weapons from ice and snow, and females as born mages of ice and snow who can also manipulate Prime Ice. The Eye of Graeae says Pavlina, the Snegurochka princess, was unmatched in Snezhnaya at shaping Prime Ice. Snegovik can faint in prolonged warmth like other cold-bound fae.

Society: They are ruled by a Grand Duchess of the Snegurochka at the House of Hesperides. The wiki lists Yalyane Morevna, called Knyazhna of Blood, as an ancestor, and her granddaughter as the first Grand Duchess. The wiki's Pavlina page says Yalyane Morevna decreed that the Grand Duchess must have a soul. Oksana, the lobby receptionist, says few humans are invited there now and most guests are Snegovik living elsewhere.

Relations: Snegovik are one of the kinds of fae under the Pale Star Court. Their bond with humans is central to how they are described: they are said to seek human companionship, and the stories about them are often tragedies. They are one of the fae kinds that served under the Belyi Tsar.

Individuals: Named Snegovik include Pavlina (princess), Larisa (a rival for the title), Yalyane Morevna (an ancestor), Oksana (House of Hesperides receptionist), Donskoy (a Snegovik guard of the Belyi Tsar) and Liubov, among others. The adventurer Viliana's mother is also a Snegovik.

293.content: Snegurochka is the common name for a female Snegovik, not a formal title. They are born ice-and-snow mages who can work Prime Ice and typically wear blue gowns with a kokoshnik. Their Grand Duchess rules from the House of Hesperides.

294.content: Several sources say the Snegovik were made for companionship and are born with incomplete souls, made whole only by loving a human. The Eye of Graeae says this is one research perspective and may not be fact. Stories tell of Snegovik growing cold once complete, or dying if they never find love.

key: The Remnant Body of the Eternal Flamefeather
295.content:
Snezhnaya Bosses (also: Immortal Construct, The Remnant Body of the Eternal Flamefeather, Chimeric Winged Lion, Solo Accompanist, Guardian Blade of Drifting Snow, Outcast Ice Shadow): Snezhnaya has three open-world bosses as of 7.1. Two are discarded creations of the alchemist Koshchei: the Immortal Construct, a feral winged beast with crimson leaf-like wings, and the Chimeric Winged Lion, a two-headed lion-and-bird chimera. The third is the Guardian Blade of Drifting Snow, an ancient Snegovik knight who has left her people's mountain manor and still trains alone in the snow.

The first two belong to the Aberrant Chimeric Monsters, the by-products of bio-alchemy from the age of the Belyi Tsar. The Guardian Blade belongs to the fae of crystalline flesh. In the game they are classed as "Mystical Beasts".

Immortal construct: A mindless winged beast in Everfrozen Earth, titled "The Remnant Body of the Eternal Flamefeather". It is a by-product, made only to serve someone else's plan, and now wanders the wilds with no purpose left.

The Archive says Koshchei made it while creating the individual called the Firebird. He is said to have kept the one success from each batch and thrown away or discarded the rest. This derivative should have fused with some form of power to be completed. Without that, it only wanders the mountain gorges as an incomplete, mindless beast. The Event Menu text speaks of an unfinished grand ritual and "hollow dreams" locked in its shell.

Chimeric winged lion: A two-headed chimera, one head a lion and one a falcon, titled "Solo Accompanist", found in the Volkodlak Tundra. It commands Anemo and Electro power far beyond ordinary man-made monsters.

The Archive calls it a product of bio-alchemy and one of the man-made monsters that were abandoned. To bring a certain great wish to fruition, an alchemist (Koshchei) created many primordial bodies, "Prototypes", by a technique that must never be retold. Only one grew into the perfect creation he planned. The others, close to perfection but failures, were carelessly remade into two-headed monsters, and these still have tremendous power; among chimeras nothing can stand against them. The Handbook adds that anomalous materials fused into its shell may explain the power.

Guardian blade: An ancient Snegovik swordswoman titled "Outcast Ice Shadow", met at Fellfrost Peak in southern Snezhnaya. She left the House of Hesperides and trains alone, awaiting a day she may return.

The Handbook says she is held in high esteem among her kin. After the current Snegurochka princess came to power she left the clan's mountain manor, perhaps because their ideals no longer aligned. The Archive adds that she once served the legendary Great Snegurochka, Yalyane Morevna, and was entrusted for life with protecting the Snegovik clan. Seven were given this charge; she alone remains, so every succession of the Snegovik sovereign must take place under her watch. The current princess is Pavlina.

Origins: The Immortal Construct and Chimeric Winged Lion come from the same cause: the unregulated alchemy of the Belyi Tsar's age, when alchemists such as Koshchei combined every form of life. The Handbook says most such monsters died in the war against the Onslaught of Dark Beasts and the survivors are rare exceptions. The Guardian Blade has no such link; she is a fae knight from a much older clan.

Placement: Immortal Construct: Everfrozen Earth (northern Snezhnaya); Chimeric Winged Lion: Volkodlak Tundra; Guardian Blade of Drifting Snow: Fellfrost Peak, south of Snezhnograd and above the town of Svetloledovka, whose Prime Ice mining belongs to the Snegurochka's mountain. Versions: 7.0 for the first two, 7.1 for the third.

Relations: The Construct and the Lion are linked through Koshchei, Hvergelmir and Zver; the Guardian Blade is linked to Pavlina, Yalyane Morevna and the House of Hesperides. Nothing connects the knight to Koshchei.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 all three can be fought in the open world. No source says what becomes of them or whether more Snezhnaya bosses will follow in later versions; nothing beyond 7.1 is recorded here.

key: Remnant Body of the Eternal Flamefeather
296.content: A feral, mindless winged beast with crimson leaf-like wings, titled "The Remnant Body of the Eternal Flamefeather". The Archive says Koshchei made it as a by-product while creating the Firebird; with no purpose left, it roams the mountain gorges as an incomplete beast. Its Pyro-edged Lifeflare state is a game mechanic.

297.content: A two-headed chimera with a lion head and a falcon head, titled "Solo Accompanist". A failed Prototype remade by Koshchei, it is among the strongest chimeras. It is found in the Volkodlak Tundra and uses Anemo and Electro power. Zver, the Belyi Tsar's companion, was a rare sentient member of the kind.

298.comment: Snezhnaya Bosses: Guardian Blade of Drifting Snow
298.content: An ancient female Snegovik knight who once served Yalyane Morevna and guarded the Snegovik clan's successions. She left the House of Hesperides after Pavlina became Grand Duchess and now trains in the snow at Fellfrost Peak. Her name is not given; she fights with Cryo blades, icicles and an ice coffin.

299.content:
Snowland Fae (also: Fae, Filii Adamici Evoluti, Evolved Children of Humanity, fae of Snezhnaya): The Snowland Fae, or simply "fae", are Snezhnaya's nonhuman supernatural peoples. Hyperborean artisans created them thousands of years ago. They live alongside humans, can use elemental power without a Vision, and many can change their shape. The first Cryo Archon, the Belyi Tsar, united them, and under his rule they formed the ruling aristocracy of the Northlands. After his death in the Cataclysm about 500 years ago, the Tsaritsa took power and the fae lost most of their old privileges.

The six common kinds are the Vila, Domovoy, Leshy, Volkodlak, Snegovik and Jack Frost. Rarer kinds include the Lantern Fae, the Water Imps ("Sirens") and the Augury Birds. Four fae are playable: Flins (Lantern Fae), Linnea (Augury Bird), Vesna (Vila) and Vodyanitsa (Water Imp). The Harbinger Pulcinella is a Domovoy.

Nature: The fae vary widely. Many look nearly human, often with blue crystalline markings; others resemble animals (the Volkodlak), little snowmen (Jack Frosts) or trees (Leshy). They have their own language and script.

Lifespans differ by kind. Flins reckons himself six or seven hundred years old "by human measure", Augury Birds live little longer than humans, and Domovoy may live indefinitely yet still grow old. Most prefer the cold. Linnea and Flins cope with Nod-Krai's milder climate, but Flins suspects some fae can no longer survive anywhere warm. Jack Frosts feel discomfort in heat but do not melt as fairy tales claim. The Fae language is not mutually intelligible with Snezhnayan: a Fatui private wrote that he "couldn't understand a word" of a fae's speech.

Origin: The fae began in Hyperborea, the "golden realm" that once stood where Snezhnaya is now. Using "forbidden methods" given to them by the rebel angel Koitar, its artisans forged fae spirits on the bones of giant beasts and spun the fallen light of the Frost Moon into their flesh. When the Celestial Nail destroyed Hyperborea, many fae shrieked and turned into "icy silver mist". Humans who survived struggled in the frozen land, and afterwards fae were the main inhabitants of the north.

History: After Hyperborea fell, the fae formed kingdoms and clans of their own. A being called Monomakh emerged from the remains of the Cryo Dragon believing himself a fae, founded Kitezh as the seat of the Pale Star Court and set out to unify the fae. He defeated King Miscislav of the Volkodlak and his allies at Kitezh, and the remaining clans submitted to him. He took the title Belyi Tsar, "protector of all fae", and later became the Cryo Archon. The fae became his nobility, with some posts open only to them, and he eventually welcomed "pardoned" humans into the realm and moved the capital to Snezhnograd.

Society: Each kind has traditionally had its own rulers: a Grand Duke or Grand Duchess of the Vila, a Grand Duke of the Domovoy, a Grand Duchess or princess of the Snegurochka at the House of Hesperides, and in ancient times a king of the Volkodlak. Old noble houses survive. House Strivozha is an ancient Vila bloodline, and Vesna's grandfather Pyotr is the reigning Grand Duke of the Vila. Most of the Druzhna, the Tsaritsa's personal guard, are Vila.

Abilities and limits: All fae can wield elemental energy and magic without a Vision or a Moon Wheel. Some kinds also fly, shapeshift or work ice.

Flins says plainly that fae "don't need Moon Wheels", but he wears one as cover for his Electro power. Linnea keeps hers only because Lumi likes how shiny it is. A fae's element is not fixed by kind: Jack Frosts are usually linked to ice, but Linnea's companion Lumi shows Geo after eating huge amounts of ore. Pulcinella, a Domovoy, uses Hydro. Vodyanitsa is unusual in holding a true Hydro Vision.

Relations: Old divisions between fae and humans persist, but the two peoples live side by side, especially in Snezhnograd. Flins once thought fae and humans must share an ancestry, and he now believes a common spirit unites them. Ordinary people know the fae well enough that townsfolk in Nasha Town and Snezhnograd often take Paimon for one.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the fae are subjects of the Tsaritsa. They are numerous across Snezhnaya, rare in Nod-Krai, and still influential through noble houses, the Druzhna and individuals such as Pulcinella. The Nod-Krai loading screen says Snezhnaya's fae aristocracy and their ruler held power "a long, long time ago".

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay guidance (project recommendation): treat "fae" as a family of distinct peoples, not one species. Give each fae the traits of their own kind, and remember that most look nearly human. In Snezhnaya a fae neighbour, clerk or noble is ordinary, while in Nod-Krai one is a curiosity.

300.content: "Filii Adamici Evoluti", "the evolved children of humanity", is the earliest name of the fae. The Belyi Tsar found it in the oldest Hyperborean records during his forays into the Shadow Realm (Notes by a Certain Noble Individual III). He concluded that the fae were never meant to be human servants, as legend claims, but were entrusted with a far grander purpose. He did not write down what that purpose was.

301.comment: Snowland Fae: Six common kinds of fae
301.content: In Linnea's Story Quest (6.5), Linnea names the six most common kinds of fae: the Vila, Domovoy, Leshy, Volkodlak, Snegovik and Jack Frosts. Her sister Celaeno adds the rarer kinds: the legendary Lantern Fae, the "Sirens with their lilting songs" (Water Imps) and the Augury Birds. A Snezhnaya loading tip adds that many other lineages have since dwindled or withdrawn from the world.

302.content:
Solitary Suanni (also: Ancient Lord of the Mountains, Mist-Cloaked Paths, suanni boss): The Solitary Suanni is an illuminated beast of Chenyu Vale, Liyue, called the Ancient Lord of the Mountains. Its in-game text says it is an elegant, proud creature that lives apart from the material world in mountains shrouded in adeptal energy. As a boss it wields Anemo and Hydro against intruders on the Southern Mountain, at Chizhang Wall.

Suanni are more often treated as symbols of good fortune than as monsters, and the Handbook says they are oft thought to exist only in fantasy. The Mist-Cloaked Paths description says it still drives away outsiders from fog-hidden mountains with wild mists and furious waves.

Nature: A beast of graceful form and lonesome, proud nature, in the Mystical Beasts family and attuned to Anemo and Hydro.

The Archive says suanni live in mountains shrouded in adeptal energy and have been admired for generations for their preference for living aloof from the material world. They are regarded as a sign of good fortune.

Lore: In Chenyu Vale legends, the leader of the suanni was called the Mountain Lord and was ranked with the adepti. The Archive records that the well-known Wushou Dance of Chenyu Vale came from the movements of suanni. Since only a handful of people have seen one, the dance costume head has changed over thousands of years of artistic interpretation into its present style.

Abilities and limits: Game mechanics (labelled as such): the boss uses Anemo and Hydro. Its attacks include a tail sweep followed by a plunge that sends out a wave, water blades from backflips, a vortex and splash, a barrage of homing scales, and a stomp. It lunges while imbued with Anemo and Hydro.

Individuals: The Solitary Suanni is found at Chizhang Wall on the Southern Mountain of Chenyu Vale. It is a single named boss, not a group.

Relations: Suanni are one of the illuminated beast kinds of Liyue, alongside qilin, cranes and deer. Local legends rank the Mountain Lord with the adepti. Xuanwen Beasts live in the same mountains and may be linked to them.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1, the Solitary Suanni remains a boss in Chenyu Vale. Whether it is Lingyuan or another suanni is not stated by the boss's own texts.

303.content: Xuanwen Beasts, named for the dark patterns on their bodies, are fierce Anemo and Hydro creatures of the mountains of Chenyu Vale. Folklore says they were servants of an adeptus and devolved after the adeptus died; the Archive also reports a theory that they are the thinned descendants of suanni. Neither can be verified.

304.content:
Specter (also: Specters, Anemo Specter, Cryo Specter, Dendro Specter, Electro Specter, Geo Specter, Hydro Specter, Pyro Specter): Specters are small elemental lifeforms that float in the air. The Adventurer Handbook describes them as monsters born from highly concentrated elements, little sprites with a gentle temperament much like slimes, though they can sometimes explode into a rage. They exist in all seven elements and are immune to their own.

They are common in Inazuma, in Enkanomiya and, per the wiki, in Sumeru. Specters were added in Version 2.1. They are everyday pests rather than characters: no individual specter has a name, voice or recorded motive.

Nature: Specters are made of concentrated elemental energy and drift above the ground. They are calm by default but fly into a rage if struck hard.

Like slimes they are classed as Elemental Lifeforms, and each carries one element: Anemo, Cryo, Dendro, Electro, Geo, Hydro or Pyro. Their Japanese name is Flime, which the wiki notes is likely a blend of "fly" and "slime". When struck hard in a single blow they grow larger and angrier, and when defeated they pause and then explode.

Abilities and limits: They float, spit or throw elemental bolts, and have a rage state: after a very heavy hit they swell and use stronger attacks. On death they blow up. (Gameplay-derived.)

A specter's rage (Fury) builds only from a single heavy blow, in steps that depend on how much of its health the blow takes, and at full Fury it grows bigger and uses only enhanced attacks; its death-explosion is also stronger. Each element has its own moves: Anemo specters fire wind bolts and create a vacuum field, Hydro specters fire bubbles and heal nearby enemies, Geo specters spit rocks and cause a quake, Cryo specters throw ice and snow and resist freezing, Electro specters call lightning and bump into targets, Pyro specters throw fire. The wiki marks move names as mostly unofficial.

Relations: Specters have no leader or society. They share their family, the Elemental Lifeforms, with slimes.

Kokomi's Specter Eco-Management group on Watatsumi Island treats specters as pests. In event dialogue Kokomi jokes that she could swap the posts of two officials, Tsuyuko and Naki, which would put Tsuyuko in charge of the group; Tsuyuko later compares it to Liyue's programs against rats, cockroaches, flies and barnacles. Specters appear in Inazuma's Felonious Floaters daily commission as a group of wild specters threatening nearby areas.

305.content: Specter Eco-Management is a Watatsumi Island group mentioned in dialogue during the limited-time event Three Realms Gateway Offering. Kokomi jokes that swapping posts would put Tsuyuko in charge of it, and Tsuyuko later compares it to Liyue's pest programs. It shows that Watatsumi treats specters as pests, but little else about the group is stated.

306.content:
Tainted Hydro Phantasm (also: Tainted Hydro Phantasms, Tainted Water-Splitting Phantasm, Tainted Water-Spouting Phantasm, Hydro Phantasm, Hydro Phantasms): Tainted Hydro Phantasms are elite Hydro elemental lifeforms, strange water spirits that arose in Fontaine's waters after the Oceanids were gone. The Archive says they lack the elegance and beauty of the Oceanids, which is why they are called tainted. They come in two forms, the Water-Splitting and the Water-Spouting Phantasm.

They are permanently imbued with Hydro and shrug off Hydro damage. They are hostile to travelers; a harbor request in Fontaine records a visitor from Liyue so scared of "water that attacks people" that he refused to leave his ship.

Nature: Elemental lifeforms made of Hydro, born from Fontaine's waters. Their Archive entries call them "tainted" because they came after the calamity and lack the beauty and grace of the Oceanids.

The Archive states that with the Oceanids gone from Fontaine, strange elemental lifeforms have appeared in the waters. It adds that the toxins once dissolved in the water have long been diluted and cleansed, yet unless containers of pure water still survive somewhere, Fontaine's waters will never again naturally give birth to Oceanids. A material description adds that the life in the water is formless, and that formless life takes the shape of the water that holds it.

Abilities and limits: They fire bubbles of water and, once enraged, grow larger and hit harder. They are permanently Hydro and immune to Hydro damage.

Gameplay (labelled, not lore): the Water-Splitting Phantasm uses fists, a spinning arm and, up close, an arm that becomes a fish to slap. The Water-Spouting Phantasm sends a stream of water and large projectiles, and inflates itself to burst outward when someone is close. Both periodically enter an enraged state, grow in size and become immune to Frozen; freezing one for too long forces the rage. In the Genius Invokation TCG, a Phantasm monster card also never freezes and is always Hydro-applied.

Relations: They replaced the Oceanids in Fontaine's waters; the Archive explicitly contrasts the two. Sigewinne once needed an extract from a Water-Splitting Phantasm among the ingredients for a task.

In the quest "Beauty Expert" (4.0), Paimon and the Traveler seek a special ingredient on Sigewinne's list. It was a Tainted Hydro Phantasm Extract, obtained by defeating a Tainted Water-Splitting Phantasm. In the weekly request "Hydro Phantasm Havoc", Lectoure asks for the Phantasms to be dealt with so a frightened passenger will leave the ship.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Tainted Hydro Phantasms remain ordinary hostile lifeforms in Fontaine's waters. No later content found reveals their origin, and none was found in Nod-Krai or Snezhnaya.

307.comment: Tainted Hydro Phantasm: Tainted Hydro Phantasm
307.content: Tainted Hydro Phantasms are elite Hydro lifeforms that appeared in Fontaine's waters after the Oceanids were gone. They are aggressive, can enrage and grow, and lack the Oceanids' beauty. They are a wild creature, not a people.

308.comment: Tainted Hydro Phantasm: Phantasms versus Oceanids
308.content: The Archive presents the Phantasms as what filled the waters after the Oceanids were extirpated from Fontaine. They lack the Oceanids' elegance, and the waters will not give birth to Oceanids again unless pure water survives. Most Oceanids died with Egeria, and survivors left. No source says the two are related by descent.

309.comment: Tainted Hydro Phantasm: Phantasm drops and extract
309.content: Defeated Phantasms leave water whose life force has not yet ebbed. The three grades of material are a drop, a scoop and a bottled newborn Phantasm, the last described as a new lifeform that arose from a dispersed one. Sigewinne's quest used a special extract taken from a Water-Splitting Phantasm.

310.content:
Tatankasaurus (also: Tatankasaur, Tatankasaurs, Tatankasaurus Whelp, charging saurian, Electro saurian): Tatankasaurs are the Electro Saurians of Natlan: huge, horned, buffalo-like dragons of the volcanic southwest, living beside the Collective of Plenty. They are usually docile, but an angered Tatankasaur cannot be reasoned with until its energy runs out. They are animals and do not speak.

The Archive describes a Saurian with a hard, bony crest and a powerful body suited to dashing around volcanic landscapes.

Nature: Wiki descriptions give a quadruped, massive, fluffy body in purple and beige, with crystal protrusions along the body and great horns atop the head. Their young are called whelps.

Society: Tatankasaurs live in the volcanic regions of Natlan's southwest, around Atocpan, with the Collective of Plenty.

Like each Saurian species, they hold a home territory that largely defines their tribe's lands; others enter only by invitation and escort. A Tatankasaur, like any Saurian, chooses its human partner.

Abilities and limits: They stomp and charge, dashing across large gaps and smashing massive rocks and boulders. The wiki describes them as close-range Electro fighters.

Relations: Their tribe is the Collective of Plenty. For the wider picture of Saurians, see the Saurian group entry.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): portray a Tatankasaur as a heavy, steady animal that tolerates a lot, then breaks into a blind charge only when truly angered. Do not give it speech.

311.content: Tatankasaurs are the huge, horned Electro Saurians of Natlan's volcanic southwest, partners of the Collective of Plenty. They are fairly docile, but once angered become unreasonable until their energy is spent. They charge, stomp and shatter boulders. Legend says their ancestors could move mountains with their horns.

312.content:
Tenebrous Mimiflora (also: Tenebrous Mimifloras, Tenebrous Mimesis, Tenebrous Papilla, Void Obliterator Bubble, Void Fantasy Plant): Tenebrous Mimifloras are plant-like monsters of the Abyss found in Natlan. They enter battle disguised as other creatures, protected by a Void Ward, and fall back to their true form when the ward breaks. Their largest form is the Tenebrous Papilla, a boss at Quahuacan Cliff that mimics other bosses. Their attacks inflict Attrition, a slow loss of health.

They first appeared in 5.1 as an elite enemy group, the Tenebrous Mimesis. Archive text says they bear only a surface resemblance to plants, having adopted that form to approach the tree-like world and copy its concepts.

Nature: Archive text calls them Abyssal monsters that descended from a twisted, alien world. Where the corrosive waves of the dark tide lap, such plant-like monsters are said to grow.

The entry stresses that the plant shape is borrowed: they took it to come closer to the tree-like world, extract the concepts they needed, and analyse and imitate them. Inactive in the wild, a Mimiflora may sit as a closed bud that looks like a closed Embercore Flower.

Abilities and limits: Mimicry: on entering battle it may take the shape of another enemy, and in that form it cannot be damaged until its Void Ward is destroyed. Its true form fires spikes and homing spheres.

Gameplay (not literal lore): the Void Ward wears down with each elemental hit, and faster under Nightsoul-aligned attacks. Once it is gone the Mimiflora returns to its true form, is briefly stunned, and later transforms again with a weaker ward. Fifteen variants copy creatures such as Saurian hatchlings and warriors, a Geovishap Hatchling, an Anemo Hilichurl Rogue, a Crackling Axe Mitachurl, a Ruin Guard and a Secret Source Automaton. A Mimiflora whose name is plain "Tenebrous Mimiflora" does not transform. Its attacks apply Attrition stacks: each stack removes a little health after a delay.

Society: Nothing in the texts shows Mimifloras acting as a group or serving a master. They are described as individual predators of memory and concepts.

Relations: They belong to the Abyss and so oppose everything of Teyvat. Their copying of Saurians, hilichurls and automata shows no loyalty to what they imitate.

Individuals: The Tenebrous Papilla ("Void Fantasy Plant"), added in 5.2, is the sole named individual: a normal boss at Quahuacan Cliff with three mimic types.

Scene use: This project's suggestion (not canon): a Mimiflora is suited to uncanny scenes in which something familiar behaves slightly wrongly, with plant-like details visible through its disguise.

313.content: A boss form of the Tenebrous Mimiflora, found at Quahuacan Cliff in Natlan and added in 5.2. It mimics other normal bosses in three possible sets of forms, summons a Void Ward and charges a large explosion that inflicts Attrition. Archive text says it infiltrates deep into the earth to extract memories and moves toward the Irminsul's core.

314.content:
Tengu (also: crow tengu, Great Tengu, Yougou Tengu, tengu warrior): Tengu are youkai of Inazuma with black wings and crow-faced masks. They are swift, skilled with the bow and sword, and strong beyond their slim frames. Most lived in seclusion; the elite Yougou Tengu guarded Mt. Yougou and the Grand Narukami Shrine. The tengu most people meet today is Kujou Sara, a general of the Tenryou Commission who was adopted into the Kujou Clan and serves the Raiden Shogun with unbroken devotion.

The chieftain of the Yougou Tengu bore the title Great Tengu. As of 7.1 the only tengu known from the present day are Sara and an unnamed tengu who once wrestled Arataki Itto.

Nature: Black wings are a common trait (Teruyo, Sara), and every known tengu wears a crow mask. Sara has two pairs of raven-black wings and a red crow mask at the side of her head.

Tengu are slimmer than oni but much stronger than they look. The wiki observes that Akuou kept the mask of Sasayuri as a trophy, suggesting masks carry honour or importance; canon does not confirm what they mean.

Abilities and limits: Flight, archery, swordsmanship and speed. Tengu arts are taught beyond their own clans.

The Great Tengu taught the human Takamine the Mistsplitter her archery, which Takamine later taught the shrine maiden Asase Hibiki. Another of the Yougou Three, the onmyouji Kamuna Harunosuke, learned the tengu art of transcension from the Yougou Tengu and combined it with Liyue adepti arts to create onmyoudou.

Society: Tengu live mostly in seclusion in forests and mountains. The Yougou Tengu are an elite group who protected Mt. Yougou, and so the Grand Narukami Shrine on it.

The chieftain of the Yougou Tengu bears the title of Great Tengu. Sasayuri and Reizenbou are the two known holders. The Yougou Tengu also created the Empty Boat of a Thousand Gates at the end of the Araumi labyrinth, where the Yougou Three trained under them.

Relations: Tengu have served or allied with the Raiden Shogun and the Narukami kitsune. They appear alongside the oni in Inazuman tales and duels.

The Great Tengu Reizenbou guarded the Kitsune Saiguu, and Sasayuri served the Shogun as a general. In the present Sara serves the Shogun as a general of the Tenryou Commission. Itto once had an unsettled sumo match with a young tengu on Byakko Plain years ago, which ended with both of them rolling down a mountain and the tengu carrying the ankle-sprained Itto home; he also lost his Vision to Sara in a duel.

Individuals: - Kujou Sara (playable): Tenryou Commission general who enforces the Vision Hunt Decree; adopted by Kujou Takayuki after a young tengu was found with a Vision.
- Sasayuri (killed in the Orobashi war): Great Tengu of Yougou, a general of the Shogun.
- Reizenbou: Great Tengu 500 years ago, Saiguu's protector and mentor of the Yougou Three; went into exile after the Cataclysm.

History: Tengu were among Inazuma's oldest inhabitants and lived in seclusion. Sasayuri served Ei and died fighting Orobashi's people. Reizenbou later led the Yougou Tengu and was given the bow Thundering Pulse by the Shogun.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1, tengu remain few and secluded. Kujou Sara is the only known tengu in human society; Reizenbou and Teruyo disappeared 500 years ago. No tengu were found in the sources checked for Nod-Krai (6.x) or Snezhnaya (7.0-7.1).

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon): tengu are disciplined, direct and fast, with a duelist's sense of honour. They are rare and reserved with humans.

315.content: The Yougou Tengu are an elite group of tengu tied to Mt. Yougou, responsible for protecting the mountain and the Grand Narukami Shrine on it. Their chieftain holds the title Great Tengu, held by Sasayuri and later Reizenbou. They created the Empty Boat of a Thousand Gates in the Araumi labyrinth, where the Yougou Three trained under them. Their names carry divine power, according to Teruyo.

316.content: Sasayuri, the Great Tengu of Yougou, was a general of the Raiden Shogun who died in the war with Orobashi's people. The duel Akuou planned over Tenshukaku never happened; they fought on Yashiori Island, and Sasayuri's mask broke. The name is Japanese for the bamboo lily.

317.content: Reizenbou was the Great Tengu of the Yougou Tengu five hundred years ago and bodyguard to the Kitsune Saiguu, whom she had let win a race. She trained the Yougou Three, taught Takamine archery, and gave him the bow Thundering Pulse after a bet that ended in a draw. The wiki treats her as Teruyo's mother. After the Saiguu was lost in the Cataclysm she went into self-imposed exile; the Empty Boat of a Thousand Gates was her last home.

318.content: Teruyo was a Yougou Tengu who gave Mikoshi Michihiro the name Iwakura, hoping to free him from the curse of oni blood, and challenged him to a duel that lasted thirteen years. After he grazed her wing she named him Tengu Victor and left forever. Her fate is unknown.

319.content: Tengu warriors carry magical feather fans (hauchiwa) with various effects. For ordinary people, the Red Feather Fan merely makes the body lighter in the air, speeding gliding.

320.content:
Tepetlisaurus (also: Tepetlisaur, Tepetlisaurs, Tepetlisaurus Whelp, Tepetlisauri): Tepetlisaurs are the Geo Saurians of Natlan: bipedal, lizard-like dragons with large brown bodies, rocky protrusions and a drill-shaped horn on the forehead. They live in the mines of eastern Natlan alongside the Children of Echoes, and can tunnel through rock and even solid Phlogiston.

They are one of six common Saurian species, each tied to a Natlan tribe. In the game's bestiary they are a common enemy of the Natlan Saurians group, fighting close-range with Geo attacks.

Nature: Tepetlisaurs are strong-clawed, rock-armoured animals. Their drill-horn and claws let them dig through stone and solid Phlogiston, and they climb crystals of solid Phlogiston easily.

The Archive entry gives their legendary origin: the ancestor of all Tepetlisaurs was a drake as large as a mountain with an exceptionally long life. When it slept, mountains rose along its back; when it woke and shook off dirt and stone, gems and jade were left shining among its scales. The huge drill-shaped objects in the Children of Echoes' lands are said to be the remains of its great horn. Like all Saurian ancestor stories, this is legend, not recorded history.

Society: Tepetlisaurs belong to the Children of Echoes and live in the mines of eastern Natlan. Like other Saurians they choose their human partners and keep to their own tribe's territory.

Saurians do not enter another species' tribal settlement unless invited and escorted; in the game, an outside Saurian entering a settlement is expelled, and the world story explains this with protective runes whose origin is unknown. A Tepetlisaur belongs among the Children of Echoes, and the other tribes' Saurians belong in their own lands.

Abilities and limits: Tepetlisaurs fight with their drill-horn and claws, striking with Geo force. They burrow into the ground and travel under it, then burst out to slam down on a target.

Gameplay (not literal lore): as enemies they use a drill-horn combo with an optional jumping smash, and a burrowing strike that surfaces to taunt before leaping out. They resist Geo strongly. When the Traveler indwells one, burrowing spends Phlogiston while moving, and it can scale walls at speed while burrowing; it is the best climber among the indwellable Saurians.

Relations: Their human partners are the Children of Echoes. Among the other species they are the miners' counterpart to the forest Yumkasaurs of the Scions of the Canopy.

The Traveler indwelt adult Tepetlisaurs several times in the quest "Medicine Born of Guilt" while looking for the young Qucusaur Antu.

Individuals: Little One, a Tepetlisaur whelp marked by the Flamelord's Blessing and called the "Chosen of Dragons" by Kukulkan, accompanies the Traveler in the Natlan world story. The young Tepetlisaur Aguara appears in Linnea's Story Quest.

Little One is described under the Saurians entry. He later sets off on his own adventures. In the Natlan story the Blessing was removed through an old rite at the Great Volcano of Tollan during version 5.5.

321.content: Tepetlisaurs are Natlan's Geo Saurians: brown, bipedal, rocky dragons with a drill-shaped horn, living in eastern Natlan's mines with the Children of Echoes. They dig through stone and solid Phlogiston. Legend says their ancestor was a mountain-sized drake whose sleeping back raised mountains.

322.content:
Thunder Manifestation (also: Raging Thunder of Amakumo Peak, Crackling Thunder Manifestation, Stormy Resentment): The Thunder Manifestation is an unusual Electro lifeform, a giant violet bird of lightning that haunts Amakumo Peak on Seirai Island in Inazuma. It looks somewhat like an Oceanid but lacks her intelligence or memories. What drives it is raw, primal fury that the texts variously call resentment, hatred or regret.

Its title is "Raging Thunder of Amakumo Peak". The Archive says such beings come down like lightning only on places that host great lingering resentment, like the fragmented Amakumo Peak under its always-roiling clouds, and that while the land's grudges do not fade, neither will the roaring thunder. The boss unlocks when the world quest series Seirai Stormchasers is completed. It first appeared in Version 2.1.

Nature: An Electro elemental lifeform of lightning and storm. It does not speak or reason like an Oceanid, and acts from a single overwhelming emotion.

The Handbook, once the boss is unlocked, says it weaves thunder and lightning as a song to the resentment that drives its every move, and is "an elemental being driven by pure regret". The Archive adds that it has no Oceanid-like intelligence or memories. The Storm Beads it leaves behind are described as crackling Electro pearls, and the item text says the singers hold that the unbearable disappointments and sufferings of life drive these beings to wander the broken earth, scattering sky-searing lightning.

Abilities and limits: Game mechanics (labelled as such): all attacks are Electro. At first it sets lightning-strike probes around the arena that pulse when it has noticed a player, sweeps in a spinning wing attack, and calls waves of bolts. A pulse or shockwave that hits a player enrages it. While enraged, it teleports across the arena, slashes with a wing, closes two walls of lightning around a target, shoots electric feathers, dives across the arena and fires a homing thunder cage. Most move names are unofficial.

History: The ancient Thunderbird Civilization of Tsurumi Island worshipped Kanna Kapatcir, a powerful Thunderbird the wiki's Kapatcir page calls a monster misunderstood as the island's guardian. The boy Ruu was sacrificed in her name; when she found him dead, her grief became lightning that destroyed the tribe.

Quests: In Seirai Stormchasters: Part IV the Traveler seals the final Warding Stones, then defeats the Thunder Manifestation, and afterwards finds a Peculiar Pinion, a feather. Taisuke judges from its dimensions that the bird must have been as large as the floating stone platform above. Completing the series unlocks the boss for repeat challenges.

Event variant: The Crackling Thunder Manifestation, titled "Stormy Resentment", is an event-only enemy in Feast of the Departed Warriors (Version 3.7, June 2023), with a stronger moveset built around lightning probes.

Status as of 7.1: As of Version 7.1 the Thunder Manifestation remains a permanent boss on Seirai Island. No Nod-Krai (6.x) or Snezhnaya (7.0-7.1) content adds to its lore.

323.content: The Thunder Manifestation's unique boss drop: crackling Electro pearls. The item text says such beings only descend upon lands where powerful hatred dwells, driven forever across the broken earth by life's unbearable disappointments and sufferings.

324.content: Four stones on Seirai Island that the quest Seirai Stormchasters has the Traveler seal. Neko says Asase Hibiki once sealed and unsealed them and that they were meant to seal a bird of enormous size. Sealing the last two, up in the sky, forms a platform of floating stones where the Thunder Manifestation is fought.

325.content:
Tighnarian (also: Tighnarians, Valuka Shuna, Tighnarian people): The Tighnarians, called Valuka Shuna ("large desert dog") by the Aranara, are a humanoid, foxlike people of Sumeru. They came from Tighnar and served King Deshret in the Great Red Sand. After his fall they lived in Tulaytullah and later moved to the rainforest. Tighnari, the Forest Watcher, is one of their descendants.

Tighnarians are remembered for wisdom, and for the Temple of Silence, which they founded in Tulaytullah to keep King Deshret's knowledge. Their most famous member, Hermanubis, was one of Deshret's Seven Pillars.

Nature: Hermanubis, the only "true" Tighnarian shown, had a jackal-like head and a humanlike body. Mortal descendants such as Tighnari are mostly human, with big fennec-like ears and bushy tails.

In the desert their hair and fur were pale, which helped with the heat. Over time in the rainforest it turned darker green, and some descendants now tolerate heat badly; Tighnari's own childhood trip toward the desert ended with him fainting from the heat. The Aranara named them Valuka Shuna even though they looked more like foxes than dogs.

History: Tighnarians lived in the Great Red Sand during King Deshret's era and mostly served him as priests. Deshret chose the sage Hermanubis from among them as his familiar. When Deshret died, Hermanubis led the Tighnarian priests to Tulaytullah, where they founded the Temple of Silence to guard knowledge from his fallen civilisation.

Society: While Deshret lived, most of his priests were Tighnarians, and Hermanubis was their leader and a revered guide of priests. Later, Tulaytullah prospered through their wisdom, and people came to link the Tighnarians with the city although they came from Tighnar.

Relations: The Aranara gave them the name Valuka Shuna after they moved to the forest. They worked with the Akademiya before leaving it. The Temple of Silence they founded still exists under Sethos, and Cyno, one of its Ba fragment bearers, is Tighnari's close friend.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 no full Tighnarian remains known; Hermanubis is long dead, though Ba fragments of his power live on in Temple members. Tighnari and his family are the only known descendants, living in Sumeru's rainforest.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay guidance (project recommendation): treat Tighnarians as a long-gone people, known now through Hermanubis and descendants. A descendant is human, with fox-like ears and tail, not a beastman, and may be sensitive to desert heat.

326.content: Hermanubis was a warrior of Tighnar who served King Deshret and became his familiar, the only one of the Seven Pillars to rise from humanity to the rank of a god's familiar. Known as the Greatest of Sages, he was sincere, steadfast, kind and respected even by the other Pillars. After Deshret's death he founded the Temple of Silence in Tulaytullah. When Tulaytullah was betrayed, he divided himself into Ba fragments to protect the Temple, and those fragments still exist.

327.comment: Tighnarian: Tulaytullah and the Temple of Silence
327.content: Tulaytullah was a desert city that prospered while Hermanubis' Tighnarian priests kept Deshret's knowledge there as the Temple of Silence. A Gurabad king besieged it and its elite sided with him, and the Temple left for the rainforest and later returned to the desert near Thamud Oasis. An empty Akademiya office of the same name now handles sealed information.

328.content: Valuka Shuna is the name the Aranara gave the Tighnarians after they moved to the rainforest. It means "large desert dog" in their language, though the Tighnarians looked more like foxes. Tighnari's Character Story 5 tells how, as a child, he found the name in a family manuscript as a child and was startled to learn he was a "large desert dog".

329.content:
Tri-Lakshana Creature (also: Tri-Lakshana Creatures, Tri-Lakshana, Trilakshana creature, Tri-Yana Seed, Seed Mirror, Bouncy Mushroom, Rocklifting Branch): Tri-Lakshana Creatures are special plants and fungi of Sumeru that change when elemental energy touches them. Normally they sit in a Normal state; Pyro leaves them Scorched, and Electro makes them Activated. The Sumeru tutorial tells travellers to use their different forms to aid an adventure.

They are mostly an exploration aid (bouncing, revealing hidden things, clearing enemy attention) and, in a few cases, a hazard. Most appear first in version 3.0, with the Sumeru region.

Nature: The in-game tutorial calls them creatures that can transform due to stimuli from external elemental energy. Contact with Electro puts them in an Activated state; contact with Pyro puts them in a Scorched state. Their Normal state is associated with Dendro.

Most kinds have a pile of white fluff beside them in the Normal and Activated states that blinks; scorching removes it for a time. Exceptions: Fungi have no fluff in any state, Seed Mirrors keep it even when Scorched, and some starshrooms and bouncy mushrooms (for example in The Chasm's underground mines) cannot change state at all. A Scorched creature can usually be restored with Dendro (Fungi cannot). Activated creatures generally return to Normal after a short while, except Fungi.

Kinds: The wiki lists these kinds: Bouncy Mushrooms, Dream Flowers, Fungi, Poisonous Mushrooms, Rocklifting Branches, Seed Mirrors, Starshrooms and Tri-Yana Seeds.

Gameplay: Gameplay note: everything about the three states, Truesense Pulses, bounce height and damage is game mechanics, not described in the world by any character. In roleplay treat them as odd Sumeru flora that visibly react to lightning or fire.

How {{char}} behaves: This project's suggested use: in a scene they are local colour, such as a mushroom that springs a traveller upward after lightning strikes, or a flower that withers when a flame passes. Do not invent scholarly explanations, folklore or sentience for them; canon gives none.

330.content: Tri-Lakshana Creatures are Sumeru plants and fungi with a Normal state, an Electro-Activated state and a Pyro-Scorched state; the Sumeru tutorial introduces them as creatures that transform in response to external elemental energy. Gameplay-driven, with no deeper canon explanation.

331.content:
Umibouzu (also: Umibozu): Umibouzu are huge, intelligent sea creatures known in Inazuma, extinct in most waters. Sailors regard them as foes and many were hunted; the people of Watatsumi Island instead treat each as a lonely individual. They appear only through the world quest Solitary Sea-Beast (2.1).

"Umibouzu" is the name used on Narukami Island. Canon has never shown a living one, and its remarks suggest they resemble whales.

Nature: Huge, intelligent, docile and solitary sea animals.

A partial skeleton on Watatsumi Island shows their scale; Kumi describes them as lonely and indifferent to curiosity or hostility from outside their own world. Their biology is otherwise unspecified.

Society: Mostly solitary. Watatsumi's people give each creature its own name rather than a species name.

Narukami Island folk say they attack cargo ships on long voyages and steal fishermen's catch, so they are hunted. Near Watatsumi Island they have grown close to humans. Traces may also exist on Yashiori Island, per an in-world note.

Individuals: - Kuntira: a female umibouzu befriended in childhood by Kumi, who later found her remains on a beach of Watatsumi Island.

History: Umibouzu once ranged more widely but are now gone from most waters. Kumi believed Kuntira the last of her kind; the quest overturns this.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 only Kuntira's offspring are implied to remain; nothing in Nod-Krai (6.x) or Snezhnaya (7.0-7.1) content adds to this.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon): treat them as rarely seen and mourned by those who knew one. Do not invent sightings or powers.

332.content: Kuntira was a female umibouzu and Kumi's childhood friend. Kumi found her skeleton on a beach of Watatsumi Island. Anisa shows that she had many offspring and died at sea.

333.content:
Ursa the Drake (also: Ursa, Ursa's Flesh, the drake Ursa): Ursa the Drake was an Angel that gave up wisdom for raw power and became a corrupted dragon, said to have no distinct element. A thousand years ago it hounded Vennessa's tribe and menaced Mondstadt until Barbatos helped drive it off, after which it was sealed. Four years before the game's story the Fatui and the Knights' inspector Eroch unsealed it for experiments, and its flesh was still being exploited in Mondstadt in the Lohen story quest.

In Mondstadt the name is tied to the death of Crepus, Diluc's father, though the beast involved may have been an imitation. Its remains caused trouble again in the A Knight's Resolve story quest (Lohen), where Varka, Diluc and the Traveler razed the hidden laboratory and destroyed Ursa's remaining power.

Nature: A draconic devolved Angel. Wiki summaries describe it as having abandoned wisdom for power, and it is not tied to a particular element. It controlled hilichurls, and could speak or at least understand speech.

Angels are Celestia's servants, and the wiki's infobox cites Hymns of the Far North for their creation by the Heavenly Principles. Ursa's flesh and blood are potent and dangerous: in the story quest researchers refine them into a serum, and the experiments are treated as deadly and corrupting.

History: A thousand years ago the wandering tribe of Vennessa fled Ursa and its hilichurls for four days before reaching Mondstadt, where the Lawrence aristocracy enslaved them. Lord Lawrence later forced Vennessa to fight twelve battles for her freedom, the last against Ursa, with the tribe fighting beside her. Venti revealed himself as Barbatos and helped her drive Ursa and its army away. These events come from the Vennessa manga. Ursa was later sealed, and the Knights of Favonius were responsible for guarding the seal.

Abilities and limits: Ursa overpowered even a Vision holder in the Crepus attack, and it commanded hilichurls. Its power can be extracted into a serum.

Relations: Ursa's story crosses Barbatos, Vennessa and the Lawrence Clan, then Eroch, Dottore and the Fatui, then Crepus and Diluc, and finally Lohen, Theodore, Adorno and Varka. Nicole, who learned Lohen's suffering stemmed from a former angel, tried to give him guidance, but this failed.

Individuals: The original Ursa is the thousand-year-old drake. The beast that attacked Crepus and the one Dottore slew are described by the wiki as an imitation. Ursa's remaining flesh and power at the Millhaven site were destroyed by Varka, Diluc and the Traveler in A Knight's Resolve.

334.comment: Ursa the Drake: Ursa's Flesh and the Ursa serum
334.content: A substance refined from Ursa's flesh and blood in the Millhaven laboratory. Theodore used low-concentration serum to ease Adorno's decline; high concentration required repeatedly stimulating the flesh. Taking it risks the corrupting voice that tempted Lohen. Varka and the others destroyed the laboratory so it could not be made again.

335.content:
Vila (also: Vilas, wind fae, Grand Duke of the Vila, Grand Duchess of the Vila): The Vila are one of the six common kinds of Snowland Fae. They are small, pale fae with pointed, green-tipped ears and two pairs of insect-like wings that allow brief flight. They were among the first to follow the Belyi Tsar, supplied most of the Druzhna guard, and the playable Vesna, Commander of the Druzhna, is one.

They are traditionally led by a Grand Duke or Duchess of the Vila. Since the Cataclysm some have remained loyal to the Tsaritsa through the Druzhna, while others in the tundra cling to the privileges of the old Tsar's day.

Nature: Vila are humanoid and small in stature, with pale white skin, pointed ears tipped in green and some with a green triangle under the eyes. They fly briefly on insect-like wings, which gives them exceptional mobility.

Like all fae they were created by Hyperborean artisans as part of a drive to surpass humans, and need no Vision for power. The Winged Soarer Knight Archive says their brief flight lets them scout formations and raid over long distances.

History: After Hyperborea fell and the fae settled in Snezhnaya, the Vila were for an unknown period vassals of the Volkodlak under King Miscislav, paying tithes of grain, gold and slaves. When Monomakh, the later Belyi Tsar, set out to unite the fae, the Vila were among the first to follow. Their first Grand Duchess, Vaselisa Strivozha, was defeated alone by the Tsar. He asked them to stop their tribute, and they denounced Miscislav and submitted to the Pale Star Court willingly.

Society: The Vila were traditionally led by a Grand Duke or Grand Duchess. Names recorded include Vaselisa Strivozha, Photius, Gluvasha, Benigna and Pyotr; Vesna's Character Stories make Pyotr the current Grand Duke and her grandfather, and Benigna her parent. House Strivozha is an ancient Vila bloodline whose name carries weight in Snezhnaya. Vesna's profile says the clan existed long before Snezhnaya's early days.

Abilities and limits: Flight on four wings is brief rather than sustained, but it makes Vila fast scouts and raiders. The Druzhna's Winged Soarer Knights, a Vila enemy type, use this in the game's combat.

Relations: Vila served the Volkodlak, then the Belyi Tsar, and now many serve the Tsaritsa. They interact with the other kinds as fellow fae nobility. In the New Bough story Vaselisa Strivozha is called the saint of the Vila and begs the Tsar to protect the Leshy forest, which shows their ties to other fae.

Individuals: Known Vila include Vesna (playable, Druzhna Commander), Vaselisa Strivozha (first Grand Duchess), Gluvasha, Photius, Benigna, Pyotr, Akvilina (Druzhna officer), and the Burner of Cities (rebel).

336.content: The Druzhna is the personal guard that the Belyi Tsar founded and led. Its ranks have always been drawn largely from the Vila. The Tsaritsa took it over as her own guard after the Cataclysm, and Vesna now commands it.

337.content: A female Vila of the old fae nobility who led a short-lived rebellion against the Tsaritsa, raiding by rail across the plains, and who was killed soon after according to item text. Her scheme to destroy the Kresnik's Torches was foiled by Izmaylov's heroes and the movement was suppressed.

338.content:
Vishap (also: Vishaps, Dragonheirs, elemental vishaps): Vishaps are dragon-like elemental creatures of the Light Realm. They once followed each of the Seven Sovereigns by element and were the dominant race of the world; over long ages they are said to evolve into true dragons. Three lines are known today: the Geovishaps of Liyue, the Bathysmal Vishaps of Enkanomiya (with newcomers in Fontaine) and the Pyro vishaps of Natlan, who lost their intelligence and became Saurians.

The word names a kind, not one animal: a Geovishap in a Liyue valley and a Bathysmal Vishap in the dark sea of Enkanomiya are cousins, not the same creature. Their history is mostly known through the three places where they survive.

Nature: Vishaps are elemental creatures of the Light Realm, also called the Vishap Realm or Elemental Realm. They are reptilian, dragon-like beasts rather than people, and where players meet them they are hostile to humans.

Vishaps are fundamentally at odds with the Human Realm, where gods and mortals live, and with the Void Realm. Neuvillette says their ancestry runs back to the Fontemer, which is why they adapt so well. In his companion chat lines he adds that vishaps lose the ability to tell colours apart over the course of their evolution.

Geovishaps: Geovishaps live in Liyue's mountains and have done so since a bygone era, together with their lord Azhdaha. They attune to Geo; adults can also take on Cryo, Electro, Pyro or Hydro one at a time during a fight, drawing on nearby elemental energy.

The Primo Geovishap is the great form met as a world boss in the Tianqiu Valley area of Liyue, always carrying one extra element shown in its scales. Local Legend Geovishaps such as the pair Yiji and Tianyu at Chizhang Wall are called rulers of their mountains. Geovishaps and Primo Geovishaps first appeared in 1.3.

Bathysmal vishaps: Bathysmal Vishaps, also called the Dragonheirs of the Depths or Hydro Vishaps, once ruled Enkanomiya and the depths below it. Their attacks can drain Energy. They hate artificial light.

The people of Byakuyakoku, as Enkanomiya was once called, feared them for thousands of years. Thousands of lanterns and the light of the Dainichi Mikoshi, built with knowledge from Istaroth, kept them at bay. Several thousand years ago the Watatsumi Omikami (Orobashi) defeated them and suppressed them under the sea with jade corals, then brought the people to the surface and made Watatsumi Island for them.

Pyro vishaps: The Pyro vishaps lived in Natlantea, ruled by Xiuhcoatl and the Thirteen Sovereign Lords, and slaughtered many angels in their territory. After the empire fell and the Heavenly Principles conquered the land, they adapted to survive and lost their intelligence, becoming the Saurians of Natlan. Kukulkan and Och-Kan both called this a devolution, because the descendants had lost their ancestors' wisdom and power.

Relations: Vishaps follow the Dragon Sovereigns, whom Bathysmal Vishaps see as the peak of their kind. Liyue's Geovishaps follow Azhdaha. Humans meet them as threats, though Liyue has lived beside them for ages.

Azhdaha, once Morax's friend, was sealed under the Dragon-Queller at Nantianmen after erosion made him attack the humans he had sworn to protect. Neuvillette, the Hydro Dragon reborn in human form, speaks of vishaps as kin. Melusines are the "daughters" of Elynas, born from the remains of an Abyssal beast; Neuvillette's third Character Story treats them as a new form of Hydro vishap or dragonheir in some sense, while the wiki doubts they count as dragons.

Individuals: - Azhdaha: Geo Dragon Sovereign and Geovishap ancestor, sealed under the Dragon-Queller (own entry).
- Jiu: the child-shaped vessel Azhdaha made from part of his power (own entry).
- Pahsiv: a Hydro vishap who takes Melusine form, living in Erinnyes Forest and later seen in the Liffey region of Fontaine; first seen in 4.2.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): treat wild vishaps as dangerous, territorial beasts, with Bathysmal Vishaps shunning light, rather than as talkers. Do not make Geovishaps and Bathysmal Vishaps interchangeable: the first belong to Liyue's rock and ley lines, the second to the dark sea. Pahsiv is the rare friendly exception and speaks only a few words.

339.content: Azhdaha is an ancient Geovishap ancestor and Geo Dragon Sovereign. He slept for untold years under Nantianmen until Morax unearthed him and gave him sight, and he became a friend of Morax and of humanity. Erosion made him forget Morax and their contract, and mining in the Chasm damaged the ley lines and caused him pain. He attacked humans and was sealed under the Dragon-Queller. Later he tried to break free through his vessel Jiu, but the Traveler, Zhongli and his own benevolent consciousness stopped him. His own entry holds the full story.

340.content: Pahsiv is a vishap who can take Melusine form and is called a "fairy" of Erinnyes Forest. She says "pahsiv" for yes and "Melusine" for no. In The Wild Fairy of Erinnyes the Traveler helps her cleanse the Weeping Willow of the Lake. Her only earlier acquaintance was Neuvillette, whom she called "New Valet". In A Gift From the Sea Spirits she rescues the Melusine Puca and later returns to the sea with Puca's signboard.

341.content: The Byakuyakoku name for the Bathysmal Vishaps. Their dislike of light is why Enkanomiya burned thousands of lanterns and built the Dainichi Mikoshi. The Watatsumi Omikami later suppressed them with jade corals.

342.content:
Volkodlak (also: Volkodlaks, Volkodlak Brute, Volkodlak Brutes, beast fae, Miscislavli): The Volkodlak are one of the six common kinds of Snowland Fae, the non-human spirits of Snezhnaya. They are beast-like but humanoid, strong and keen-sensed, and the Adventure Handbook calls them the most populous fae race in the nation. About 3,000 years ago their kings led the Miscislavli Alliance, which the first Cryo Archon, the Belyi Tsar, broke in war. Today they appear as a nation's worth of clans, a few mild or loyal, and as the Volkodlak Brutes that attack travellers in the Snezhnayan wilds.

They vary a great deal in shape: wolfish, bovine, canine, long-eared, elephant or mammoth-like. The wiki shows the race has no single look, and the history book notes subcategories, so treat "Volkodlak" as a family of clans rather than one animal.

Nature: Like other fae, Volkodlak were made by the artisans of Hyperborea, the "Golden City", as part of an effort to build a race that could surpass humans. They stand and work on two legs with beast features and the strength of animals. They are long-lived, though lifespans differ across fae kinds.

A noble's notes found at the Pale Crown Palace give the general origin of all fae: the Evolved Children of Humanity, made with forbidden methods. The Adventure Handbook adds a guess about the Volkodlak specifically: that they may have been made to find out what makes a human human. The Long-Eared Striker's Archive entry gives a separate account for one lineage, saying it was made to test the limits of reproductive capability, and that its great numbers let it survive the fall of the golden realm.
The Handbook also says the crystalline growths on fighting fae come from the surge of energy released as they were made; see the Fae of Crystalline Flesh.

Society: Historically the Volkodlak were ruled by a king. Their great confederation was the Miscislavli Alliance. Since the Belyi Tsar absorbed the fae kingdoms into the Pale Star Court, they have no king of their own, and clans have different loyalties and roles.

Volkodlak clans are described by animal aspect: the Nyholmgarthir were bovine, the Cirnareka wolf-like (a Cirnareka name is rendered "Black Hand"), and the Archive speaks of canine clans with a reputation for loyalty and mildness. Some are go-betweens: Channel Contact types are entrusted with carrying goods and messages.

History: About 3,000 years ago King Miscislav, the "Blood-Devourer", ruled the Miscislavli Alliance as a rival of the first Emperor, Monomakh Snezhnyi. After a short war the Emperor killed Miscislav in battle and became the Belyi Tsar.

In the 428th Cycle, the 76th year after Monomakh founded Kitezh, the Emperor's envoys told the Vila to stop paying tribute to Miscislav because it was "unlovely". The Vila did so. Three years later Miscislav accused the Pale Star Court of breaking the peace and demanded ten years of grain, gold and slaves, thirty times what the Vila had paid, which the Emperor rejected. The book's footnotes say this was likely a provocation: Miscislav feared the Pale Star Court's rise. A year after that he marched on Kitezh. Three times the armies met (the foothills, the frozen lake, the plains), and in the last the Emperor slew him with a spear through the skull. Grand Dukes Skoldyryt and Vodyanoy were also slain, and many princes who followed him.

Abilities and limits: Gameplay, labelled as such: the Volkodlak Brute enemies use weapons and can imbue themselves with elemental energy, then attack in combos. Low-tier brutes (Basher, Lobber, Raider, Sharpshooter) mostly deal Physical damage with a special elemental attack; high-tier ones (Channel Contact, Fanged Zealot, Leomastiff Guard, Long-Eared Striker, Voywolf Hunter) lean on elemental power. Every brute has a special attack that a Stellar Glimmer reaction can interrupt or backfire. In-world: great physical strength, keen senses, agility on snow, and skill with bows, crossbows, cannons and thrown objects (Archive texts).

Individuals: Miscislav (dead; see his own entry). Seriviiki, Skoldyryt: grand dukes recorded in the Pale Starborn book. Bogatov: open-world NPC in Snezhnaya (exact location not recorded), a descendant of Miscislav per the wiki. Furiosa: a Volkodlak archer, a quest NPC and a Local Legend enemy (Voywolf Hunter), described in her own entry.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Volkodlak are an ordinary part of Snezhnayan life and wildlife-like threats, with no ruler. Their Tundra of Ancient Beasts is a region of the Snezhnayan map.

The Volkodlak Tundra, opened in 7.0, is said to be where the Miscislavli capital stood; after Miscislav's defeat the site was demolished and rebuilt, with the Tsar leaving no trace of the old city. A boss, the Chimeric Winged Lion, is fought there (see Aberrant Chimeric Monster). Nothing about the Volkodlak was found in 7.1 sources.

343.content: The Miscislavli Alliance was the Volkodlak-led confederation of fae clans under King Miscislav, the Blood-Devourer, whose vassals included the Vila and in whose host marched the Nyholmgarthir, Cirnareka, and Dalegrad water imps. Its war with Monomakh Snezhnyi's Pale Star Court ended with Miscislav's death at Kitezh and the Emperor's rise as the Belyi Tsar. See Miscislav's own entry for the man.

344.content: The Volkodlak Brutes are the enemy group of hostile Volkodlak in Snezhnaya, part of the Fae of Crystalline Flesh. Four low-tier types (Basher, Lobber, Raider, Sharpshooter) and five high-tier types (Channel Contact, Fanged Zealot, Leomastiff Guard, Long-Eared Striker, Voywolf Hunter) are known. Their special attacks can be disrupted by Stellar Glimmer reactions. Archive entries describe them as beast-strong and keen-sensed, dangerous to anyone untrained.

345.content: The Volkodlak Tundra, "Tundra of Ancient Beasts", is a Snezhnayan region said to have held the capital of the Miscislavli Alliance. After the Tsar's spear pierced Miscislav's head and his iron hooves scattered the confederation, the city was razed and rebuilt, and the usually merciful ruler seemed afraid something might rise from the place, leaving no trace of the old city (Expedition description). The Chimeric Winged Lion is a boss there.

346.content:
Water Imp (also: Water Imps, Rusalka, Siren, Sirens, Vodyanitsa kin): Water Imps are one of the less common kinds of Snowland Fae, with the Augury Birds and Lantern Fae. Their old role was singing, carrying messages and healing along Snezhnaya's rivers, bound by a covenant that no Water Imp should again be made to fight. Over time almost all of them left Snezhnograd for a faraway unfrozen lake. The playable Vodyanitsa, Prima Donna of the Korolevskiy Troupe, is the kind's best-known member and the last one still singing in the city.

Nature: Like the other Snowland Fae, Water Imps came from Hyperborea's creation of the fae and are native to Snezhnaya. They normally have a mermaid-like tail, which at will they change into working human legs to walk on land. Vodyanitsa has fin-shaped ears, pale crystalline scales and, in water, a dark-teal tail, with ribbon-like fins appearing on her back.

They live in or near water and look after their tails. Vodyanitsa's guidance note tells readers to soak the tail in fresh, clean water, with no milk, petals or fruit, and says the best water is from Fontaine. She dislikes dry land: she says her skin dries out after too long ashore and that "for us Water Imps, leaving the water behind is a big enough price to pay already".

Water Imps hear extremely well. Vodyanitsa says she can make out whispers from afar, boasts that she hears "clear as a bell" whatever is whispered, and says that Water Imps can understand and even learn the songs of Frostfin Whales.

History: Vodyanitsa's character stories give the Water Imps' own account. The Water Imps' childhood is placed in Dalegrad, and they once roamed freely, singing blessings to every living thing. Their lord Vodyanoy Dombertiev, "the Lackland", allied with King Miscislav, and the fast, fearless Water Imps became the strength of Miscislav's rise, until his daughter Vaselisa Vodyanovna could not bear the sight of her kin's cold blood frozen on the lake.

Society: Water Imps are a small, close-knit people. Their work was song in many forms: stage performance, street melody, and ambushes that splash passers-by at the water's edge. Vodyanitsa's parents were celebrated singers who held intimate concerts at their estate where fae and townsfolk sang together, and they taught her to think only of the next song. Water Imps include aristocrats: in the 7.0 Archon Quest Vodyanitsa says her Water Imp parents belonged to the aristocracy that the Tsaritsa drove out of Snezhnaya long ago, and that they now live somewhere new that the postman cannot reach. Her profile separately remembers them as celebrated singers.

Abilities and limits: Water Imps use elemental power without a Moon Wheel, like other fae. Vodyanitsa, however, carries a Hydro Vision, which she treats as jewellery. Song is central to their identity. In the covenant story, Water Imps lulled anxious soldiers to sleep with their songs and carried the wounded swiftly downriver on rafts. Vodyanitsa's profile hints at an allure in her voice; see the uncertainties.

Relations: Water Imps are on good terms with the Snezhnayans who love song. Fae history ties them to Dalegrad, the Volkodlak king Miscislav and the Tsar of the Pale Star. Among the rare kinds, Celaeno lists Water Imps alongside Augury Birds and Lantern Fae, but no personal connection between their known members is shown. Vodyanitsa herself is friends with Odette and Alyosha through the Rokot.

Individuals: - Vodyanitsa: Prima Donna of the Korolevskiy Troupe, playable Hydro character from 7.1, the last Water Imp still on stage in Snezhnograd.
- Vodyanoy Dombertiev, "the Lackland": lord of the Water Imps of Dalegrad, who fought for Miscislav (ancient figure).
- Vaselisa Vodyanovna, the "Zmey Maiden": his daughter, who led weaponless Water Imps to the Tsar.
- Litiya Ozerova: a Water Imp performer loved by the human Shram, mentioned in Winter's Mysterious Silence.
- Paraskeva and Xenia: Water Imps whose music Vodyanitsa memorised and whom she names when rehearsing.
- Vodyanitsa's parents: celebrated singers, unnamed in the sources read.

How {{char}} behaves: As this project's interpretation: portray Water Imps as theatrical, warm and a little teasing, with a deep love of ordinary listeners and a dislike of being treated as a status symbol. They are not sea-monsters or temptresses; the kind themselves refuse that label. Keep the tail, wet hair and water imagery, but do not make siren charm literal unless the scene asks for it.

347.content:
Wayob (also: Great Spirits, ancestral wills of Natlan): The Wayob are the great spirits venerated by Natlan's six tribes, believed to embody the will of each tribe's ancestors. They have no body and live in the Night Kingdom, from which they guard their people against the Abyss. Each tribe calls on its own Wayob for protection and blessing. The Abyss's invasion of the Night Kingdom infected them, but they recovered once it was cleansed.

The name is used for both singular and plural. In the Adventurer Handbook, obsidian totems called Wayob Manifestations are described as forms the Wayob take when they appear in Natlan. Wayob appear from 5.0.
